title.zh: 卷一 本紀第一 武帝上
title.raw: 卷一 本紀第一 武帝上 Volume 1: Emperor Wu 1

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第一 本紀第一

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 1, Basic Annals 1
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 1, Annals 1

sentences.zh: 武帝上

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, Part 1
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, Part One

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝，諱衍，字叔達，小字練兒，南蘭陵中都里人，漢相國何之後也。

translations.literal: Gaozu, the Martial Emperor, taboo name Yan, styled Shuda, childhood name Lian'er, a native of Zhongdu village in Nan Luling, was a descendant of Han Chancellor of State He.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, the Martial Emperor, taboo name Yan, styled Shuda, childhood name Lian'er, came from Zhongdu village in Nan Luling and traced his line to Han Chancellor of State He.

sentences.zh: 何生酇定侯延，延生侍中彪，彪生公府掾章，章生皓，皓生仰，仰生太子太傅望之，望之生光祿大夫育，育生御史中丞紹，紹生光祿勳閎，閎生濟陰太守闡，闡生吳郡太守冰，冰生中山相苞，苞生博士周，周生蛇丘長矯，矯生州從事逵，逵生孝廉休，休生廣陵郡丞豹，豹生太中大夫裔，裔生淮陰令整，整生濟陰太守鎋，鎋生州治中副子，副子生南台治書道賜，道賜生皇考諱順之，齊高帝族弟也。

translations.literal: He sired Ding Marquis Yan; Yan sired Attendant-in-Ordinary Biao; Biao sired Grandee's Assistant Zhang; Zhang sired Hao; Hao sired Yang; Yang sired Grand Tutor of the Heir Wang Zhi; Wang Zhi sired Minister of the Household Yu; Yu sired Imperial Censor Zhongcheng Shao; Shao sired Superintendent of the Bright Halls Hong; Hong sired Administrator of Jiyin Chan; Chan sired Administrator of Wu commandery Bing; Bing sired Chancellor of Zhongshan Bao; Bao sired Erudite Zhou; Zhou sired Chief of Sheqi district Jiao; Jiao sired Secretariat Aide Kui; Kui sired Filial and Incorrupt Xiuxiu; Xiuxiu sired Assistant Commandery Administrator of Guangling Bao; Bao sired Grand Master for All Purposes Yi; Yi sired Magistrate of Huaiyin Zheng; Zheng sired Administrator of Jiyin Zheng; Zheng sired Commandery Administration Vice-director Fuzi; Fuzi sired Southern Tribunal Clerk Daoci; Daoci sired the Late Emperor's father, taboo name Shunzhi, a clansman of Qi Gaodi.
translations.idiomatic: He begat Ding Marquis Yan, who begat Attendant-in-Ordinary Biao, and so down the line through Grand Tutor Wang Zhi, Ministers of the Household, censors, administrators, and clerks to the Late Emperor's father Shunzhi, a kinsman of Qi Gaodi.

sentences.zh: 參預佐命，封臨湘縣侯。

translations.literal: He participated in assisting the founding mandate and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linxiang county.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in founding the dynasty and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linxiang county.

sentences.zh: 歷官侍中，衛尉，太子詹事，領軍將軍，丹陽尹，贈鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: His offices included Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Guards, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Defender-in-Chief, and Governor of Danyang; posthumously he was conferred Pacification North General.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Guards, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Defender-in-Chief, and governor of Danyang, and after death was made Pacification North General.

sentences.zh: 高祖以宋孝武大明八年甲辰歲生於秣陵縣同夏里三橋宅。

translations.literal: Gaozu was born in year jiachen of the eighth year of Emperor Xiaowu of Song's Daming era at the Three Bridge residence in Tongxia village, Moling county.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was born in the jiachen year of Daming 8 (464 CE), at the Three Bridge house in Tongxia village, Moling county.

sentences.zh: 生而有奇異，兩胯駢骨，頂上隆起，有文在右手曰「武」。

translations.literal: At birth there were marvels: his hip bones were joined, the crown of his head was raised, and on his right hand was writing that read "Martial."
translations.idiomatic: At birth he showed omens: fused hip bones, a raised crown, and the character for "Martial" written on his right hand.

sentences.zh: 帝及長，博學多通，好籌略，有文武才幹，時流名輩咸推許焉。

translations.literal: When the Emperor grew up, he was broadly learned and mastered many subjects, fond of strategy, and possessed civil and military talent and ability; the celebrated figures of the time all acclaimed him.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he became deeply learned, loved strategy, and showed both literary and martial gifts; the leading men of the age all praised him.

sentences.zh: 所居室常若雲氣，人或過者，體輒肅然。

translations.literal: The residence where he lived often seemed shrouded in cloud-mist; those who passed by involuntarily grew solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Clouds often seemed to hang over his dwelling, and passersby felt themselves grow solemn without knowing why.

sentences.zh: 起家巴陵王南中郎法曹行參軍，遷衛將軍王儉東閣祭酒。

translations.literal: He began his career as Acting Aide in the Law Section on the staff of the Prince of Baling's Southern General of the Center, then transferred to East Pavilion Libationer under General of Guards Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a law aide on Prince of Baling's staff, then became East Pavilion Libationer under General of Guards Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 儉一見深相器異，謂廬江何憲曰：「此蕭郎三十內當作侍中，出此則貴不可言。

translations.literal: Jian, on first meeting, deeply admired him and said to He Xian of Lujiang: "Within thirty years this young Xiao will become Attendant-in-Ordinary; beyond that his nobility is beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: At their first meeting Jian marked him as extraordinary and told He Xian of Lujiang, "This young Xiao will reach Attendant-in-Ordinary within thirty years; after that his rise will be beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 」竟陵王子良開西邸，招文學，高祖與沈約、謝朓、王融、蕭琛、范雲、任昉、陸倕等並遊焉，號曰八友。

translations.literal: " Prince Ziliang of Jingling opened the Western Pavilion to recruit men of letters; Gaozu together with Shen Yue, Xie Tiao, Wang Rong, Xiao Chen, Fan Yun, Ren Fang, Lu Chui, and others all frequented it, and they were called the Eight Friends.
translations.idiomatic: " Prince Ziliang of Jingling opened the Western Pavilion for literary men; Gaozu joined Shen Yue, Xie Tiao, Wang Rong, Xiao Chen, Fan Yun, Ren Fang, Lu Chui, and others there, and they were known as the Eight Friends.

sentences.zh: 融俊爽，識鑒過人，尤敬異高祖，每謂所親曰：「宰制天下，必在此人。

translations.literal: Rong was brilliant and forthright, his discernment surpassing others; he especially honored and admired Gaozu, often telling those close to him: "To command the realm must be this man.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was sharp and perceptive beyond his peers and held Gaozu in special esteem, often telling intimates, "The man who will rule the realm is this one.

sentences.zh: 」累遷隨王鎮西諮議參軍，尋以皇考艱去職。

translations.literal: " He was promoted in succession to Advisory Aide on the Prince of Sui's Western Pacification staff; soon, on his late father's mourning, he left office.
translations.idiomatic: " He rose to advisory aide on the Prince of Sui's western staff, then left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 隆昌初，明帝輔政，起高祖爲寧朔將軍，鎮壽春。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longchang, when Emperor Ming held regency, Gaozu was recalled as General Who Pacifies the North and garrisoned Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Longchang, with Emperor Ming acting as regent, Gaozu was recalled as General Who Pacifies the North and posted at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除太子庶子、給事黃門侍郎，入直殿省。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed Heir Apparent's Household Attendant and Bearer of the Yellow Gate, entering straight duty in the Palace Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he became Heir Apparent's Household Attendant and Bearer of the Yellow Gate, serving on palace duty.

sentences.zh: 預蕭諶等定策勳，封建陽縣男，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit in fixing policy with Xiao Chen and others, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Jianyang county, fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For helping Xiao Chen and others settle the succession, he was enfeoffed Baron of Jianyang, fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，魏遣將劉昶、王肅帥衆寇司州，以高祖爲冠軍將軍、軍主，隸江州刺史王廣爲援。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, Wei sent generals Liu Chang and Wang Su at the head of troops to raid Si province; Gaozu was made General Who Conquers All and army commander, subordinate to Jiangzhou Inspector Wang Guangzhi as relief.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 2, Wei generals Liu Chang and Wang Su invaded Si province; Gaozu was made General Who Conquers All and army commander under Jiangzhou inspector Wang Guangzhi.

sentences.zh: 距義陽百餘里，衆以魏軍盛，趑趄莫敢前。

translations.literal: Over a hundred li from Yiyang, the masses, because Wei troops were strong, hesitated and none dared advance.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred li short of Yiyang, the army hung back before Wei's strength and no one dared move forward.

sentences.zh: 高祖請爲先啓，廣卽分麾下精兵配高祖。

translations.literal: Gaozu requested to open the attack first; Guang immediately assigned elite troops from his command to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu asked to lead the first strike; Guang at once gave him picked troops from his own command.

sentences.zh: 爾夜便進，去魏軍數里，逕上賢首山。

translations.literal: That same night he advanced; several li from the Wei army, he went straight up Xianshou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: That night he marched on, climbed Xianshou Mountain, and halted only a few li from the Wei camp.

sentences.zh: 魏軍不測多少，未敢逼。

translations.literal: The Wei army could not gauge their numbers and did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei force could not tell how many they were and did not dare close in.

sentences.zh: 黎明，城內見援至，因出軍攻魏柵。

translations.literal: At dawn, those inside the city saw relief arrive and thus sent troops out to attack the Wei palisade.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the city garrison saw help had come and sallied out against the Wei stockade.

sentences.zh: 高祖帥所領自外進戰。

translations.literal: Gaozu led his command in attack from outside.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu led his men in from outside.

sentences.zh: 魏軍表裏受敵，乃棄重圍退走。

translations.literal: The Wei army was attacked from within and without, then abandoned heavy encirclement and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Caught between the sortie and Gaozu's assault, the Wei army broke siege and fled.

sentences.zh: 軍罷，以高祖爲右軍晉安王司馬、淮陵太守。

translations.literal: When the campaign ended, Gaozu was made Right Army Prince of Jin'an's Staff Officer and Administrator of Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign Gaozu became staff officer to Prince of Jin'an's Right Army and administrator of Huailing.

sentences.zh: 還爲太子中庶子，領羽林監。

translations.literal: He returned as Heir Apparent's Household Attendant and commanded the Feathered Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Heir Apparent's Household Attendant and took command of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 頃之，出鎮石頭。

translations.literal: Before long, he went out to garrison Stone Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he went out to garrison Stone Fort.

sentences.zh: 四年，魏帝自率大衆寇雍州，明帝令高祖赴援。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Wei Emperor personally led a great host to raid Yong province; Emperor Ming ordered Gaozu to go to relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Wei emperor invaded Yong province in person; Emperor Ming ordered Gaozu to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 十月，至襄陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he reached Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Xiangyang in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 詔又遣左民尚書崔慧景總督諸軍，高祖及雍州刺史曹虎等並受節度。

translations.literal: An edict also sent Minister of the Left Cui Huijing as overall commander of all armies; Gaozu and Yong province Inspector Cao Hu and others all received his direction.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also made Minister of the Left Cui Huijing overall commander; Gaozu, Yong province inspector Cao Hu, and the rest came under his orders.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，慧景與高祖進行鄧城，魏主帥十萬餘騎奄至。

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year, Huijing and Gaozu advanced toward Deng city; the Wei ruler led more than a hundred thousand horsemen and suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the third month, Huijing and Gaozu marched on Deng city as the Wei ruler swept in with more than a hundred thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 慧景失色，欲引退，高祖固止之，不從，乃狼狽自拔。

translations.literal: Huijing turned pale and wished to withdraw; Gaozu firmly stopped him but he would not heed, then in disarray pulled out himself.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing lost color and wanted to retreat; Gaozu tried hard to hold him, but he would not listen and broke away in disorder.

sentences.zh: 魏騎乘之，於是大敗。

translations.literal: Wei horsemen pursued; thus there was great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei cavalry chased them down and routed the army.

sentences.zh: 高祖獨帥衆距戰，殺數十百人，魏騎稍卻，因得結陣斷後，至夕得下船。

translations.literal: Gaozu alone led the troops to hold off battle, killing several tens or hundreds of men; Wei horsemen slightly withdrew, and he was thus able to form ranks and cover the rear; by evening he could board ship.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu alone held the rear, killing dozens or hundreds until the Wei riders fell back; he then formed up, covered the retreat, and reached the boats by nightfall.

sentences.zh: 慧景軍死傷略盡，惟高祖全師而歸。

translations.literal: Huijing's army was dead and wounded almost completely; only Gaozu returned with his army intact.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing's force was nearly wiped out; only Gaozu brought his troops back whole.

sentences.zh: 俄以高祖行雍州府事。

translations.literal: Soon Gaozu was made acting Yong province headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gaozu was put in charge of Yong province headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 七月，仍授持節、都督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡諸軍事、輔國將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, he was still granted Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of Yong, Liang, North Qin, and South Qin four provinces and Ying province's Jingling and Si province's Sui commandery, Assistant State General, and Yong province Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he received bearer of the staff, command over Yong, Liang, North Qin, South Qin, Jingling, and Sui, Assistant State General, and the Yongzhou inspectorship.

sentences.zh: 其月，明帝崩，東昏卽位，揚州刺史始安王遙光、尚書令徐孝嗣、尚書右僕射江祏、右將軍蕭坦之、侍中江祀、衛尉劉暄更直內省，分日帖敕。

translations.literal: That month, Emperor Ming died and Dong Hun succeeded; Yangzhou Inspector Prince Yao Guang of Shi'an, Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Xiaosi, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Jiang Shi, Right General Xiao Tanzhi, Attendant-in-Ordinary Jiang Si, and Minister of Guards Liu Xuan all took turns on duty inside the palace, dividing days for posting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: That month Emperor Ming died and Dong Hun succeeded; Prince Yao Guang of Shi'an, Xu Xiaosi, Jiang Shi, Xiao Tanzhi, Jiang Si, and Liu Xuan rotated palace duty and took turns issuing edicts.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，謂從舅張弘策曰：「政出多門，亂其階矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard this and said to his maternal uncle Zhang Hongce: "Government issuing from many gates—its steps to disorder are set.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard this he told his maternal uncle Zhang Hongce, "When power comes from too many hands, disorder follows close behind.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：『一國三公，吾誰適從？

translations.literal: The Odes says: 'One state, three dukes—whom shall I follow?
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says, 'One realm, three lords—whom should I obey?

sentences.zh: 』況今有六，而可得乎！

translations.literal: ' And now there are six—how can it be done!
translations.idiomatic: ' And now there are six—how is that supposed to work!

sentences.zh: 嫌隙若成，方相誅滅，當今避禍，惟有此地。

translations.literal: If suspicion and rifts form, they will slaughter each other; to avoid calamity today, only this place will serve.
translations.idiomatic: Once suspicion sets in they will destroy one another; to escape disaster now, only this post can save us.

sentences.zh: 勤行仁義，可坐作西伯。

translations.literal: Diligently practice benevolence and righteousness, and one may sit and become Lord of the West.
translations.idiomatic: If we act with benevolence and righteousness, we can secure the west and wait our turn.

sentences.zh: 但諸弟在都，恐罹世患，須與益州圖之耳。」

translations.literal: But the younger brothers are in the capital, fearing they will suffer worldly harm—we must also plot with Yizhou about this."
translations.idiomatic: But our brothers remain in the capital and may come to harm; we must also plan with Yizhou."

sentences.zh: 時高祖長兄懿罷益州還，仍行郢州事，乃使弘策詣郢，陳計於懿曰：「昔晉惠庸主，諸王爭權，遂內難九興，外寇三作。

translations.literal: At the time Gaozu's eldest brother Yi had finished Yizhou and returned, still handling Ying province affairs; he therefore sent Hongce to Ying to lay the plan before Yi: "Formerly Jin Emperor Hui was a mediocre ruler; the princes contended for power, thus nine internal disasters arose and three external invasions occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's eldest brother Yi had just left Yizhou and was acting in Ying province, so Gaozu sent Hongce to lay out the plan: "Under the feckless Emperor Hui of Jin the princes fought for power, bringing nine internal crises and three foreign invasions.

sentences.zh: 今六貴爭權，人握王憲，制主畫敕，各欲專威，睚眦成憾，理相屠滅。

translations.literal: Now the six exalted ones contend for power; each holds the king's command, controls the ruler and drafts edicts, each wishing exclusive authority; grievances over trifles become hatred—in principle they will slaughter each other.
translations.idiomatic: Now six men grasp the imperial seal, draft edicts for the throne, and each seek sole power; the smallest slights become deadly grudges, and slaughter is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 且嗣主在東宮本無令譽，媟近左右，蜂目忍人，一總萬機，恣其所欲，豈肯虛坐主諾，委政朝臣。

translations.literal: Moreover the heir on the eastern palace originally had no fine reputation; he draws close to petty companions, bee-eyed and cruel to men; holding all affairs of state, indulging every desire—how would he willingly sit empty as nominal sovereign and delegate government to court ministers?
translations.idiomatic: The heir has never had a good name; he keeps vicious company, governs by caprice, and will never sit idle while ministers run the realm.

sentences.zh: 積相嫌貳，必大誅戮。

translations.literal: Accumulated mutual suspicion and division will certainly mean great executions and slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual distrust will only deepen until blood fills the palace.

sentences.zh: 始安欲爲趙倫，形迹已見，蹇人上天，信無此理。

translations.literal: Shi'an wishes to become another Zhao Lun—his tracks are already visible; a lame man climbing to Heaven—truly there is no such principle.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yao Guang of Shi'an already shows the makings of another Zhao Lun; a cripple climbing to Heaven is not in the order of things.

sentences.zh: 且性甚猜狹，徒取亂機。

translations.literal: Moreover his nature is very suspicious and narrow; he will only seize opportunities for chaos.
translations.idiomatic: He is suspicious and petty by nature and will seize any chance to make trouble.

sentences.zh: 所可當軸，惟有江、劉而已。

translations.literal: Those who can hold the axle are only Jiang and Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Only Jiang and Liu are left who might hold the center.

sentences.zh: 祏怯而無斷，暄弱而不才，折鼎覆餗，翹足可待。

translations.literal: Shi is timid and indecisive; Xuan is weak and without talent—overturning the cauldron and spilling the broth can be awaited with foot raised.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shi is timid and cannot decide; Liu Xuan is weak and incompetent—the cauldron is ready to tip.

sentences.zh: 蕭坦之胸懷猜忌，動言相傷，徐孝嗣才非柱石，聽人穿鼻，若隙開釁起，必中外土崩。

translations.literal: Xiao Tanzhi's breast harbors suspicion; at every word he speaks of mutual harm. Xu Xiaosi's talent is not pillar-stone stuff—he lets others lead him by the nose; if rifts open and trouble rises, inside and outside will surely collapse like earth.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tanzhi is jealous and quick to wound; Xu Xiaosi lacks the strength to bear weight and lets others lead him. Once the breach opens, court and country will crumble together.

sentences.zh: 今得守外籓，幸圖身計，智者見機，不俟終日。

translations.literal: Now obtaining guardianship of an outer fief, fortunate to plot for one's body—the wise see opportunity and do not wait a full day.
translations.idiomatic: We hold an outer province and can still save ourselves; the wise act at once and do not wait for tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 及今猜防未生，宜召諸弟以時聚集。

translations.literal: Before suspicion and guard have yet arisen, the younger brothers should be summoned to gather in good time.
translations.idiomatic: Before suspicion hardens, we should call our brothers together while we still can.

sentences.zh: 後相防疑，拔足無路。

translations.literal: Afterward, when mutual guarding and suspicion arise, there will be no road to pull up one's feet.
translations.idiomatic: After that, once they watch one another, we will have no way out.

sentences.zh: 郢州控帶荊、湘，西注漢、沔；

translations.literal: Ying province controls and links Jing and Xiang, pours west into the Han and Mian;
translations.idiomatic: Ying province commands Jing and Xiang and opens west onto the Han and Mian;

sentences.zh: 雍州士馬，呼吸數萬，虎眎其間，以觀天下。

translations.literal: Yong province's soldiers and horses, breathing in and out several ten thousands, tiger-stare from among them to observe the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yong province fields tens of thousands of troops and can watch the realm like a crouching tiger.

sentences.zh: 世治則竭誠本朝，時亂則爲國剪暴，可得與時進退，此蓋萬全之策。

translations.literal: When the age is ordered then exhaust loyalty to the court; when the times are chaotic then for the state cut down violence—one can advance and retreat with the times; this is roughly a plan of ten thousand certainties.
translations.idiomatic: In peace we serve the dynasty faithfully; in chaos we strike down the violent and move with the times. That is the safest course.

sentences.zh: 如不早圖，悔無及也。

translations.literal: If one does not plot early, regret will have no reaching.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not act now, regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 」懿聞之變色，心弗之許。

translations.literal: " Yi heard it and changed color, his heart not assenting.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi heard this, turned pale, and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 弘策還，高祖乃啓迎弟偉及憺。

translations.literal: Hongce returned; Gaozu then memorialized to welcome his younger brothers Wei and Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Hongce returned, and Gaozu memorialized to bring his brothers Wei and Dan to him.

sentences.zh: 是歲至襄陽。

translations.literal: That year they arrived at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Xiangyang that year.

sentences.zh: 於是潛造器械，多伐竹木，沉於檀溪，密爲舟裝之備。

translations.literal: Thereupon he secretly made weapons, felled much bamboo and wood, sunk them in Tanxi, secretly preparing boat equipment.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly built weapons, cut bamboo and timber, sank the logs in Tanxi, and quietly prepared boats.

sentences.zh: 時所住齋常有五色回轉，狀若蟠龍，其上紫氣騰起，形如繖蓋，望者莫不異焉。

translations.literal: At the time the residence where he stayed often had five-colored revolutions, shaped like coiled dragons; above them purple qi rose up, shaped like parasol-canopies—all who looked were without exception astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Over his quarters five-colored vapors often swirled like coiled dragons, and purple clouds rose in the shape of canopy umbrellas; all who saw them were astonished.

sentences.zh: 永元二年冬，懿被害信至，高祖密召長史王茂、中兵呂僧珍、別駕柳慶遠、功曹史起士瞻等謀之。

translations.literal: In winter of the second year of Yongyuan, news that Yi was killed arrived; Gaozu secretly summoned Chief Clerk Wang Mao, Central Command Troops Master Lu Sengzhen, Vice Prefect Liu Qingyuan, Merit Officer Shi Qishi Zhan, and others to plot.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Yongyuan 2, word came that Yi had been killed; Gaozu secretly called in Wang Mao, Lu Sengzhen, Liu Qingyuan, Shi Qishi Zhan, and others to plan.

sentences.zh: 旣定，以十一月乙巳召僚佐集於廳事，謂曰：「昔武王會孟津，皆曰『紂可伐』。

translations.literal: When settled, on day yisi of the eleventh month he summoned staff officers to gather in the main hall and said: "Formerly King Wu at Meng Ford—all said 'Zhou can be attacked.'
translations.idiomatic: When the plan was set, on yisi day in the eleventh month he assembled his staff and said, "At Meng Ford King Wu's allies agreed that Zhou could be overthrown.

sentences.zh: 今昏主惡稔，窮虐極暴，誅戮朝賢，罕有遺育，生民塗炭，天命殛之。

translations.literal: Today the benighted lord's evil is full, extreme cruelty at the limit, executing and slaughtering court worthies, rarely leaving survivors; the people smeared in charcoal; Heaven's mandate strikes him down.
translations.idiomatic: Today the tyrant's crimes are complete, his cruelty absolute, the court slaughtered, the people in ashes, and Heaven itself condemns him.

sentences.zh: 卿等同心疾惡，共興義舉，公侯將相，良在茲日，各盡勳效，我不食言。

translations.literal: You are of one heart in hating evil, together raising righteous action; dukes, marquises, generals, and chancellors—surely on this day; each exhaust your merit and effort—I do not eat my words."
translations.idiomatic: Join me in righteous revolt; titles and rewards belong to this day if you give your all. I will not break my word."

sentences.zh: 」是日建牙。

translations.literal: That day they raised the standard.
translations.idiomatic: That day he raised the banner of revolt.

sentences.zh: 於是收集得甲士萬餘人，馬千餘匹，船三千艘，出檀溪竹木裝艦。

translations.literal: Thereupon gathering yielded more than ten thousand armored warriors, over a thousand horses, and three thousand boats; they brought out the Tanxi bamboo and wood to equip the warships.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered more than ten thousand armored men, over a thousand horses, and three thousand boats, hauling up the Tanxi timber to fit out the fleet.

sentences.zh: 先是，東昏以劉山陽爲巴西太守，配精兵三千，使過荊州就行事蕭穎胄以襲襄陽。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dong Hun had made Liu Shanyang Administrator of Baxi, assigned three thousand elite troops, to pass through Jing province and meet Acting Headquarters Officer Xiao Yingchou to strike Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dong Hun had made Liu Shanyang administrator of Baxi, given him three thousand picked troops, and sent him through Jing province to join Xiao Yingchou in attacking Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖知其謀，乃遣參軍王天虎、龐慶國詣江陵，遍與州府書。

translations.literal: Gaozu knew their plot and sent Aides Wang Tianhu and Pang Qingguo to Jiangling, writing universally to the province and prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu learned of the plot and sent Wang Tianhu and Pang Qingguo to Jiangling with letters to every office in the province.

sentences.zh: 及山陽西上，高祖謂諸將曰：「荊州本畏襄陽人，加脣亡齒寒，自有傷弦之急，寧不闇同邪？

translations.literal: When Shanyang advanced west, Gaozu said to the generals: "Jing province originally fears Xiangyang men; add lips perishing teeth cold—their own urgency of a wounded bowstring—would they not tacitly join?
translations.idiomatic: As Shanyang marched west Gaozu told his generals, "Jing province has always feared Xiangyang men, and with us they share the fate of lips and teeth; wounded as they are, would they not secretly side with us?

sentences.zh: 我若總荊、雍之兵，掃定東夏，韓、白重出，不能爲計。

translations.literal: If I gather Jing and Yong troops, sweep and settle the eastern Xia—even if Han Xin and Bai Qi returned, they could not devise a plan.
translations.idiomatic: If I unite Jing and Yong, I can sweep the east; not even Han Xin and Bai Qi reborn could stop us.

sentences.zh: 況以無算之昏主，役御刀應敕之徒哉？

translations.literal: How much more against a benighted lord beyond calculation, and disciples who wield kitchen knives answering edicts!
translations.idiomatic: How much less against a witless tyrant and the kitchen boys who obey his orders!

sentences.zh: 我能使山陽至荊，便卽授首，諸君試觀何如。

translations.literal: I can make Shanyang reach Jing and immediately lose his head—try and see how it goes."
translations.idiomatic: I can have Shanyang lose his head the moment he reaches Jing—watch and see."

sentences.zh: 」及山陽至巴陵，高祖復令天虎齎書與穎胄兄弟。

translations.literal: When Shanyang reached Baling, Gaozu again ordered Tianhu to carry letters to the Yingchou brothers.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanyang reached Baling, Gaozu again sent Tianhu with letters to the Yingchou brothers.

sentences.zh: 去後，高祖謂張弘策曰：「夫用兵之道，攻心爲上，攻城次之，心戰爲上，兵戰次之，今日是也。

translations.literal: After Tianhu left, Gaozu said to Zhang Hongce: "The way of using troops—attacking hearts is supreme, attacking cities next; heart-battle is supreme, arms-battle next—today is such a day.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianhu left, Gaozu told Zhang Hongce, "In war the first victory is over the mind, the second over walls; battle of wills comes before battle of arms—and today is such a day.

sentences.zh: 近遣天虎往州府，人皆有書。

translations.literal: Recently sending Tianhu to the province and prefecture—everyone had letters.
translations.idiomatic: When I sent Tianhu through the province, every office received a letter.

sentences.zh: 今段乘驛甚急，止有兩封與行事兄弟，云『天虎口具』；

translations.literal: This stretch by post was very urgent, only two letters to the acting headquarters brothers, saying 'Tianhu will explain in person';
translations.idiomatic: This courier run was rushed, and only two letters went to the acting headquarters brothers, saying 'Tianhu will explain in person';

sentences.zh: 及問天虎而口無所說，行事不得相聞，不容妄有所道。

translations.literal: when asked, Tianhu had nothing to say in person—the acting headquarters could not mutually hear, could not recklessly say anything.
translations.idiomatic: yet when questioned Tianhu had nothing to say, so the brothers could not compare notes or speak freely.

sentences.zh: 天虎是行事心膂，彼聞必謂行事與天虎共隱其事，則人人生疑。

translations.literal: Tianhu is the acting headquarters' trusted core; when they hear it they will surely say the acting headquarters and Tianhu together concealed the matter—then every person will harbor doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhu is their trusted man; hearing this they will think the brothers hid the truth with him, and everyone will grow suspicious.

sentences.zh: 山陽惑於衆口，判相嫌貳，則行事進退無以自明，必漏吾謀內。

translations.literal: Shanyang confused by the crowd's mouths will judge mutual suspicion and division; then the acting headquarters in advance and retreat cannot clarify themselves, must leak our plot within.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang, swayed by rumor, will suspect them; unable to clear themselves, the brothers will betray our plan from within.

sentences.zh: 是馳兩空函定一州矣。

translations.literal: Thus with two empty letters one fixes a whole province.
translations.idiomatic: With two empty letters we can settle a whole province.

sentences.zh: 山陽至江安，聞之，果疑不上。

translations.literal: Shanyang reached Jiang'an, heard it, and indeed doubted and did not ascend.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiang'an Shanyang heard the tale, grew suspicious, and would not go on.

sentences.zh: 穎胄大懼，乃斬天虎，送首山陽。

translations.literal: Yingchou greatly feared; he then beheaded Tianhu and sent the head to Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Yingchou beheaded Tianhu and sent his head to Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 山陽信之，將數十人馳入，穎胄伏甲斬之，送首高祖。

translations.literal: Shanyang believed it; with several tens of men he galloped in—Yingchou hid armed men and beheaded him, sending the head to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang believed him, rode in with a few dozen men, and Yingchou's hidden troops cut him down and sent his head to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 仍以南康王尊號之議來告，且曰：「時月未利，當須來年二月；

translations.literal: He then came to report the proposal to honor Prince of Nankang, and said: "The time and month are not favorable; one must wait until the second month of next year;
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed enthroning Prince of Nankang and said, "The season is wrong; we should wait until the second month of next year;

sentences.zh: 遽便進兵，恐非廟算。

translations.literal: hastily advancing troops—fear it is not temple calculation."
translations.idiomatic: to march now would be to ignore the planners' counsel."

sentences.zh: 」高祖答曰：「今坐甲十萬，糧用自竭，況所藉義心，一時驍銳，事事相接，猶恐疑怠；

translations.literal: Gaozu replied: "Now sitting with armor of a hundred thousand, provisions naturally exhausted—moreover relying on righteous hearts, for the moment fierce and sharp, matters connecting one after another—still fearing doubt and slackness;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu answered, "We sit here with a hundred thousand armored men while supplies drain away; our soldiers are bold for the cause and events press on us one after another—I already fear hesitation;

sentences.zh: 若頓兵十旬，必生悔吝。

translations.literal: if the army halts ten ten-day periods, regret and grudging must arise.
translations.idiomatic: halt ten days and regret will set in.

sentences.zh: 童兒立異，便大事不成。

translations.literal: If a child stands apart, at once the great affair will not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Let one man waver and the whole enterprise fails.

sentences.zh: 今太白出西方，仗義而動，天時人謀，有何不利？

translations.literal: Now Venus appears in the west; acting righteously in movement—Heaven's time and human counsel, what is not favorable?
translations.idiomatic: Venus now stands in the west; we move in righteousness—what omen or counsel could be better?

sentences.zh: 處分已定，安可中息？

translations.literal: Disposition is already settled—how can one halt midway?
translations.idiomatic: The decision is made; how can we stop halfway?

sentences.zh: 昔武王伐紂，行逆太歲，復須待年月乎？

translations.literal: Formerly King Wu attacked Zhou, marching against Grand Year—must one again wait for year and month?"
translations.idiomatic: King Wu marched against Zhou though the stars were against him—must we wait for a better month?"

sentences.zh: 」竟陵太守曹景宗遣杜思沖勸高祖迎南康王都襄陽，待正尊號，然後進軍。

translations.literal: Jingling Administrator Cao Jingzong sent Du Sichong to urge Gaozu to welcome Prince of Nankang to establish court at Xiangyang, wait for the correct honorific title, then advance the army.
translations.idiomatic: Jingling administrator Cao Jingzong sent Du Sichong to urge Gaozu to bring Prince of Nankang to Xiangyang, proclaim him properly, and only then march east.

sentences.zh: 高祖不從。

translations.literal: Gaozu would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 王茂又私於張弘策曰：「我奉事節下，義無進退，然今者以南康置人手中，彼便挾天子以令諸侯，而節下前去爲人所使，此豈歲寒之計？

translations.literal: Wang Mao again said privately to Zhang Hongce: "I serve Your Grace with a duty that admits no advance or retreat; yet now, with the Prince of Nankang placed in another's hands, they will seize the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords—and Your Grace going forward will be made someone's tool. Is this truly a plan for the bitter cold?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mao took Zhang Hongce aside and said, "I serve you without thought of turning back—but if Nankang falls into other hands, they will hold the emperor hostage and rule the lords through him, and you will march only as their instrument. Is that a strategy for hard times?"

sentences.zh: 」弘策言之，高祖曰：「若使前途大事不捷，故自蘭艾同焚；

translations.literal: Hongce spoke of this; Gaozu said: "If the great enterprise ahead should not succeed, then orchid and mugwort burn together indeed;
translations.idiomatic: Hongce relayed this; Gaozu answered, "If the great cause ahead fails, orchid and mugwort may burn together after all;

sentences.zh: 若功業克建，威懾四海，號令天下，誰敢不從！

translations.literal: if merit and enterprise are fully achieved, awe will overawe the four seas, orders will command the realm—who would dare not obey!
translations.idiomatic: but if success is won, awe will fill the four seas and orders will run through the realm—who would dare refuse?

sentences.zh: 豈是碌碌受人處分？

translations.literal: How could one meekly submit to another's disposal?
translations.idiomatic: Why should we tamely accept someone else's terms?

sentences.zh: 待至石城，當面曉王茂、曹景宗也。

translations.literal: When we reach Stone City, I shall instruct Wang Mao and Cao Jingzong face to face."
translations.idiomatic: When we reach Stone City, I will explain this to Wang Mao and Cao Jingzong in person."

sentences.zh: 」於沔南立新野郡，以集新附。

translations.literal: South of the Mian he established Xin Ye commandery to gather newly attached people.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Mian River he created Xin Ye commandery to settle new adherents.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，南康王爲相國，以高祖爲征東將軍，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, the Prince of Nankang became Chancellor of State; Gaozu was made General Who Conquers the East and granted one suite of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, second month, the Prince of Nankang was made Chancellor of State; Gaozu was appointed General Who Conquers the East and given one suite of martial music.

sentences.zh: 戊申，高祖發襄陽。

translations.literal: On day wushen, Gaozu departed Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: On day wushen, Gaozu set out from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 留弟偉守襄陽城，總州府事，弟憺守壘城，府司馬莊丘黑守樊城，功曹史起士詢兼長史，白馬戍主黃嗣祖兼司馬，鄀令杜永兼別駕，小府錄事郭儼知轉漕。

translations.literal: He left his younger brother Wei to hold Xiangyang city and oversee prefectural affairs; his younger brother Dan to hold Lei city; Prefecture Marshal Zhuangqiu Hei to hold Fan city; Merit Officer Shi Qishi to serve additionally as chief administrator; Garrison Commander Huang Sizu of White Horse to serve additionally as marshal; Administrator Du Yong of Shao to serve additionally as aide-de-camp; petty office recorder Guo Yan to manage grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He left his brother Wei to guard Xiangyang and oversee the prefecture; his brother Dan to hold Lei city; Zhuangqiu Hei, prefecture marshal, to hold Fan city; Shi Qishi, merit officer, to double as chief administrator; Huang Sizu, garrison chief at White Horse, to double as marshal; Du Yong, magistrate of Shao, to double as aide-de-camp; and Guo Yan, petty office recorder, to handle grain transport.

sentences.zh: 移檄京邑曰：

translations.literal: He issued a proclamation to the capital, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He sent a proclamation to the capital that read:

sentences.zh: 夫道不常夷，時無永化，險泰相沿，晦明非一，皆屯困而後亨，資多難以啓聖。

translations.literal: The Way is not constantly level; times have no eternal transformation; peril and ease follow one another, obscurity and clarity are not one—all must dwell in hardship before flourishing, and draw on many troubles to inaugurate the sage.
translations.idiomatic: The Way is never always smooth; ages never stay unchanged; danger and safety alternate, darkness and light shift—great beginnings rise from hardship, and sages are forged through trial.

sentences.zh: 故昌邑悖德，孝宣聿興，海西亂政，簡文升歷，並拓緒開基，紹隆寶命，理驗前經，事昭往策。

translations.literal: Thus when the Prince of Changyi rebelled in virtue, Emperor Xiao of Han arose; when Haixi ruled in disorder, Emperor Jianwen ascended—all opened foundations and continued the imperial mandate; reason verifies the former classics, events illuminate past records.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Changyi turned wicked, Emperor Xuan arose; when Haixi misruled, Emperor Jianwen took the throne—each renewed the dynasty and carried forward Heaven's mandate, as the old texts foretold and past annals confirm.

sentences.zh: 獨夫擾亂天常，毀棄君德，姦回淫縱，歲月滋甚。

translations.literal: The lone tyrant disturbed Heaven's constants, destroyed princely virtue; wickedness and licentious excess grew day by day.
translations.idiomatic: This solitary ruler overturned Heaven's order and ruined royal virtue; treachery and debauchery deepened with every passing month.

sentences.zh: 挺虐於鬌剪之年，植險於髫丱之日。

translations.literal: He raised cruelty from the years of first shearing; he planted peril from the days of childhood locks.
translations.idiomatic: Even in the years when his hair was first cut, he showed cruelty; from childhood itself he nurtured danger.

sentences.zh: 猜忌凶毒，觸途而著，暴戾昏荒，與事而發。

translations.literal: Suspicion and poisonous malice showed at every turn; violence, perversity, and reckless ruin broke out with every affair.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion and venom marked every path he took; brutality, perversity, and ruin followed every deed.

sentences.zh: 自大行告漸，喜容前見，梓宮在殯，靦無哀色，歡娛遊宴，有過平常，奇服異衣，更極誇麗。

translations.literal: From when the late emperor's illness was announced, a gleeful countenance appeared before all; though the spirit coffin lay in state, he showed no grief, but feasted and made merry beyond the ordinary, wearing strange garments of utmost ostentation.
translations.idiomatic: Once the late emperor's illness was announced, joy showed on his face; though the imperial coffin still lay in the hall, he wore no mourning and feasted beyond all measure, dressing in outlandish finery more lavish still.

sentences.zh: 至於選采妃嬪，姊妹無別，招侍巾櫛，姑侄莫辨，掖庭有稗販之名，姬姜被干殳之服。

translations.literal: In choosing concubines he made no distinction between sisters; in summoning attendants for hair and toilet, aunt and niece could not be told apart—the rear palace had the name of a marketplace, and palace women wore arms-bearing garb.
translations.idiomatic: He chose consorts without distinguishing sisters from one another; he called in attendants until aunt and niece were indistinguishable—the inner palace became a public market, and palace women went armed like soldiers.

sentences.zh: 至乃形體宣露，褻衣顛倒，斬斮其間，以爲歡笑。

translations.literal: At times bodies were exposed naked, undergarments worn upside down, and cutting and chopping performed for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes bodies were displayed bare, underclothes worn reversed, and mutilation staged for laughter.

sentences.zh: 騁肆淫放，驅屏郊邑。

translations.literal: He rode unrestrained in lewd abandon, driving people from suburban towns.
translations.idiomatic: He indulged every excess and drove the people from towns beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 老弱波流，士女塗炭。

translations.literal: Old and weak drifted like waves; men and women were ground to charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: The aged and weak were swept away like floodwater; men and women were crushed to ruin.

sentences.zh: 行產盈路，輿尸竟道，母不及抱，子不遑哭。

translations.literal: Women in labor filled the roads; coffins lined the ways; mothers could not reach to hold their children; sons had no time to weep.
translations.idiomatic: Women giving birth clogged the roads; corpses filled the streets; mothers could not cradle their infants; sons could not pause to mourn.

sentences.zh: 劫掠剽虜，以日繼夜。

translations.literal: Plunder and abduction continued day after day.
translations.idiomatic: Robbery and kidnapping went on without pause, day into night.

sentences.zh: 晝伏宵游，曾無休息。

translations.literal: He hid by day and roamed by night, never resting.
translations.idiomatic: He lay low by day and prowled by night, never ceasing.

sentences.zh: 淫酗摐肆，酣歌壚邸。

translations.literal: Drunken debauchery and riotous noise—singing drunk in alehouse districts.
translations.idiomatic: He drowned himself in wine and riot, singing drunken songs in tavern quarters.

sentences.zh: 寵恣愚豎，亂惑妖㜸。

translations.literal: He favored and indulged foolish lads and deluded himself with demonic women.
translations.idiomatic: He pampered witless youths and let sorcerous women lead him astray.

sentences.zh: 梅蟲兒、茹法珍臧獲斯小，專制威柄，誅剪忠良，屠滅卿宰。

translations.literal: Mei Chon'er and Ru Fazhen—base slaves of the lowest sort—monopolized authority, executed the loyal and good, and slaughtered ministers and high officials.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Chon'er and Ru Fazhen, men of the meanest bond-servant stock, seized all power, cut down the loyal, and butchered ministers and high officials.

sentences.zh: 劉鎮軍舅氏之尊，盡忠奉國；

translations.literal: General Who Guards the Army Liu, honored as maternal uncle, served the state with full loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: General Who Guards the Army Liu, the emperor's uncle by marriage, gave the state his whole loyalty;

sentences.zh: 江僕射外戚之重，竭誠事上；

translations.literal: Vice Director Jiang, weighty among outer kin, devoted his utmost in service to the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Jiang, a kinsman of weight, served the throne with complete devotion;

sentences.zh: 蕭領軍葭莩之宗，志存柱石；

translations.literal: Army Commander Xiao, kin by marriage, held will to be a pillar of the state;
translations.idiomatic: Army Commander Xiao, related by marriage, meant to stand as a pillar of the realm;

sentences.zh: 徐司空、沈僕射搢紳冠冕，人望攸歸。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xu and Vice Director Shen—crown of the gentry—were where men's hopes gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Xu and Vice Director Shen, foremost among the gentry, were the men to whom all looked.

sentences.zh: 或《渭陽》餘感，或勳庸允穆，或誠著艱難，或劬勞王室，並受遺託，同參顧命，送往事居，俱竭心力。

translations.literal: Some bore the lingering feelings of "Wei Yang," some had merit in harmony, some showed loyalty through hardship, some toiled for the royal house—all received the late emperor's trust, jointly shared the regent's charge, served the departed and attended the living, each exhausting heart and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Some were bound by kinship, some by long service, some by loyalty tested in crisis, some by labor for the throne—all had been entrusted at the deathbed, appointed regents together, and served the dead and the living with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 宜其慶溢當年，祚隆後裔；

translations.literal: They should have overflowed with blessings in their years, and fortune descended on their descendants;
translations.idiomatic: They deserved blessings in their own time and glory for their heirs;

sentences.zh: 而一朝齏粉，孩稚無遺。

translations.literal: Yet in a single morning they were ground to dust, not even children spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in one morning they were destroyed to the last, not even infants left alive.

sentences.zh: 人神怨結，行路嗟憤。

translations.literal: Men and gods alike nursed grievance; travelers on the road sighed in rage.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth seethed with resentment; wayfarers groaned in fury.

sentences.zh: 蕭令君忠公幹伐，誠貫幽顯。

translations.literal: Minister Xiao was loyal, capable of public service; his sincerity pierced the hidden and the manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xiao was loyal and able in public affairs; his devotion reached from the living world to the dead.

sentences.zh: 往年寇賊游魂，南鄭危逼，拔刃飛泉，孤城獨振。

translations.literal: In past years when bandit rebels roamed, Nan Zheng was pressed to crisis; he drew sword at Flying Spring and alone roused the isolated city.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier years, when raiders threatened Nan Zheng, he seized his blade at Flying Spring and alone held the besieged city firm.

sentences.zh: 及中流逆命，憑陵京邑，謀猷禁省，指授羣帥，剋剪鯨鯢，清我王度。

translations.literal: When midstream rebellion defied orders and threatened the capital, he plotted within the forbidden precincts, directed the commanders, cut down the whale and crocodile, and cleared our royal measure.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion rose mid-river and pressed on the capital, he planned within the palace, directed the generals, destroyed the great foe, and restored the royal order.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景奇鋒迅駭，兵交象魏，武力喪魂，義夫奪膽，投名送款，比屋交馳，負糧影從，愚智競赴。

translations.literal: When Cui Huijing's strange blade flashed swift and dreadful, troops clashed at the Elephant Gate—armed might lost its spirit, men of righteous courage seized their courage; names were submitted in surrender, house after house raced to join, carrying grain and following like shadows, wise and foolish alike rushing forward.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Huijing struck with sudden fury and armies met at the palace gate, enemy courage broke and loyal men found theirs; men sent in their names, households rushed to join, grain carriers followed in their tracks, and wise and simple alike hurried to the cause.

sentences.zh: 復誓旅江甸，奮不顧身，獎厲義徒，電掩強敵，剋殲大憝，以固皇基。

translations.literal: Again he mustered troops on the Yangtze front, striving without regard for self, rousing loyal followers, lightning-swift against strong foes, destroying the great villain, to firm the imperial foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Again he gathered forces along the Yangtze, risking himself without hesitation, rousing loyal men, falling on strong enemies like lightning, and crushing the arch-villain to secure the throne.

sentences.zh: 功出桓、文，勳超伊、呂；

translations.literal: His merit exceeded Huan and Wen; his achievement surpassed Yi and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: His service outdid Duke Huan and Duke Wen; his achievement surpassed Yi Yin and Lu Wang.

sentences.zh: 而勞謙省己，事昭心迹，功遂身退，不祈榮滿。

translations.literal: Yet he was toilsome and modest, examining himself; the facts showed his heart's path—merit achieved, he withdrew, not seeking glory's fullness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he remained humble and restrained; his deeds revealed his heart—once success was won, he stepped back and asked for no excess of honor.

sentences.zh: 敦賞未聞，禍酷遄及，預稟精靈，孰不冤痛！

translations.literal: No generous reward was heard of; cruel disaster swiftly arrived—foreknowing the spirits, who was not aggrieved and pained!
translations.idiomatic: No reward came; brutal ruin followed at once—knowing what the spirits foresaw, who did not cry out in injustice and grief!

sentences.zh: 而羣孽放命，蜂蠆懷毒，乃遣劉山陽驅扇逋逃，招逼亡命，潛圖密構，規見掩襲。

translations.literal: Yet the wicked pack cast off restraint; bees and scorpions nursed poison—they sent Liu Shanyang to drive fugitives, summon desperate men, plot secretly, intending surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the villainous faction threw off all restraint; like bees and scorpions they brewed poison—sending Liu Shanyang to stir fugitives, gather outlaws, and plot a secret strike.

sentences.zh: 蕭右軍、夏侯征虜忠斷夙舉，義形於色，奇謀宏振，應手梟懸，天道禍淫，罪不容戮。

translations.literal: General of the Right Xiao and General Who Conquers Captives Xiahou—foremost in loyal resolve, righteousness shown on their faces—wondrous plans resounded greatly; at a touch, heads hung; Heaven's way punishes excess; their crimes admit no sparing.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Xiao and General Who Conquers Captives Xiahou, long steadfast in loyalty, showed justice in their bearing; their bold plans prevailed, and the enemy's heads fell at once—Heaven punishes excess, and such guilt cannot be spared.

sentences.zh: 至於悖禮違教，傷化虐人，射天彈路，比之猶善，刳胎斮脛，方之非酷，盡𥯔縣之竹，未足紀其過，窮山澤之兔，不能書其罪。

translations.literal: As for violating ritual and teaching, harming transformation and torturing people—compared to shooting at Heaven and pelting the roads, those were still mild; compared to gouging wombs and severing shins, those were not cruel—all the bamboo strips of the commanderies could not record his offenses; all the rabbits of hills and marshes could not inscribe his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Even his breaches of ritual, corruption of custom, and torture of the people—shooting at Heaven and stoning travelers seem mild beside them; gouging wombs and severing legs seem merciful by comparison—not all the bamboo records of every commandery could list his crimes; not all the brush pens in hill and marsh could write them out.

sentences.zh: 自草昧以來，圖牒所記，昏君暴后，未有若斯之甚者也。

translations.literal: Since primordial chaos, in all records charted and written, no depraved ruler or violent consort has been so extreme.
translations.idiomatic: From the earliest ages to all that history records, no depraved ruler or brutal consort has ever gone so far.

sentences.zh: 旣人神乏主，宗稷阽危，海內沸騰，氓庶板蕩，百姓懍懍，如崩厥角，蒼生喁喁，投足無地。

translations.literal: Since men and gods lack a master, the altars and grain stand on the brink—the realm within the seas boils, the common folk are swept away; the hundred surnames tremble like deer awaiting the horn-blow; the dark-haired people murmur, with nowhere to set foot.
translations.idiomatic: Men and gods are left without a ruler; the altars teeter on the edge; the realm seethes and the people are uprooted; common folk tremble like deer before the hunt; the living have nowhere to stand.

sentences.zh: 幕府荷眷前朝，義均休戚，上懷委付之重，下惟在原之痛，豈可臥薪引火，坐觀傾覆！

translations.literal: The headquarters bears the former dynasty's favor, sharing joy and sorrow alike—above bearing the weight of entrustment, below feeling the pain of kin; how can we lie on kindling and invite fire, sitting and watching collapse!
translations.idiomatic: This command bears the old court's trust and shares its weal and woe—charged from above, bound by kinship below—how can we lie on kindling beside the flames and watch the realm fall!

sentences.zh: 至尊體自高宗，特鐘慈寵，明並日月，粹昭靈神，祥啓元龜，符驗當璧，作鎮陝籓，化流西夏，謳歌攸奉，萬有樂推。

translations.literal: The Supreme One descends from High Ancestor, specially showered with tender favor—brightness matching sun and moon, pure spirit shining forth; auspice opened on the sacred tortoise, tokens verified the jade disk; he was made to guard the Shaan-Fan barrier, his transformation flowed to western Xia—all sang his praise, all under Heaven gladly pushed him forward.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign springs from High Ancestor, singled out for special grace—bright as sun and moon, pure in spirit; omens appeared on the sacred tortoise and the jade token confirmed his mandate; set to guard the western frontier, his virtue spread through the land—all the people sang his praise and pressed him forward.

sentences.zh: 右軍蕭穎胄、征虜將軍夏侯詳並同心翼戴，卽宮舊楚，三靈再朗，九縣更新，升平之運，此焉復始，康哉之盛，在乎茲日。

translations.literal: General of the Right Xiao Yingzhao and General Who Conquers Captives Xiahou Xiang together aided and upheld him with one heart—in the old Chu palace, the three spirits brightened anew, the nine provinces renewed; the fortune of rising peace begins here again, the grandeur of "How wholesome!" lies in this day.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Xiao Yingzhao and General Who Conquers Captives Xiahou Xiang have upheld him with one heart—in the old palace of Chu the three realms shine again, the nine domains are made new; the age of peace begins once more, and the glory of a well-ruled realm starts today.

sentences.zh: 然帝德雖彰，區宇未定，元惡未黜，天邑猶梗。

translations.literal: Yet though imperial virtue is manifest, the realm is not settled; the arch-villain is not removed; the capital still blocks the way.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though the emperor's virtue shines, the realm is still unsettled; the chief villain remains; the capital is still obstructed.

sentences.zh: 仰稟宸規，率前啓路。

translations.literal: Looking up to receive the imperial plan, we lead the vanguard and open the road.
translations.idiomatic: Obeying the imperial design, we march at the fore and clear the way.

sentences.zh: 卽日遣冠軍、竟陵內史曹景宗等二十軍主，長槊五萬，驥騄爲羣，鶚視爭先，龍驤並驅，步出橫江，直指朱雀。

translations.literal: This day we dispatch Champion and Interior Administrator of Jingling Cao Jingzong and twenty other army commanders—fifty thousand with long spears, swift horses in masses, eagle-eyed and striving to be first, dragon-mounting and charging together—marching from Hengjiang straight toward Zhuque.
translations.idiomatic: Today we send Champion Cao Jingzong, interior administrator of Jingling, and twenty army commanders with fifty thousand long spears—swift horses massed, eyes fierce as eagles, banners like dragons— marching from Hengjiang straight at Zhuque Gate.

sentences.zh: 長史、冠軍將軍、襄陽太守王茂等三十軍主，戈船七萬，乘流電激，推鋒扼險，斜趣白城。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator, Champion General, and Administrator of Xiangyang Wang Mao and thirty army commanders—seventy thousand war boats, riding the current like lightning, pressing the vanguard and holding narrow passes, cutting obliquely toward White City.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Wang Mao, champion general and administrator of Xiangyang, and thirty army commanders—seventy thousand war boats riding the current like lightning, driving the vanguard and seizing the defiles, angling toward White City.

sentences.zh: 南中郎諮議參軍、軍主蕭偉等三十九軍主，巨艦迅楫，沖波噎水，旗鼓八萬，焱集石頭。

translations.literal: Consulting Officer and Army Commander Xiao Wei and thirty-nine army commanders—great ships with swift oars, charging waves that choked the water, eighty thousand with banners and drums, blazing toward Stone Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Consulting officer and army commander Xiao Wei and thirty-nine commanders—great ships with swift oars, waves crashing until the river choked, eighty thousand banners and drums converging on Stone Fort.

sentences.zh: 南中郎諮議參軍、軍主蕭憺等四十二軍主，熊羆之士，甲楯十萬，沿波馳艓，掩據新亭。

translations.literal: Consulting Officer and Army Commander Xiao Dan and forty-two army commanders—warriors bold as bear and pi, a hundred thousand in armor and shields, racing boats along the waves, seizing and holding Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: Consulting officer and army commander Xiao Dan and forty-two commanders—warriors fierce as bear and pi, a hundred thousand in armor and shield, racing along the waves to seize Xinting.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史劉季連、梁州刺史柳惔、司州刺史王僧景、魏興太守裴帥仁、上庸太守韋叡、新城太守崔僧季，並肅奉明詔，龔行天罰。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yizhou Liu Jilian, Inspector of Liangzhou Liu Yan, Inspector of Sizhou Wang Sengjing, Administrator of Weixing Pei Shuairen, Administrator of Shangyong Wei Rui, Administrator of Xincheng Cui Sengji—all reverently obeying the clear edict, march to execute Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jilian, inspector of Yizhou; Liu Yan, inspector of Liangzhou; Wang Sengjing, inspector of Sizhou; Pei Shuairen, administrator of Weixing; Wei Rui, administrator of Shangyong; Cui Sengji, administrator of Xincheng—all reverently obey the imperial command and march to carry out Heaven's punishment.

sentences.zh: 蜀、漢果銳，沿流而下；

translations.literal: Shu and Han troops, sharp and bold, descend along the river;
translations.idiomatic: Shu and Han forces, keen and bold, come down the river;

sentences.zh: 淮、汝勁勇，望波遄騖。

translations.literal: Huai and Ru warriors, fierce and brave, gaze on the waves and race swiftly forward.
translations.idiomatic: Huai and Ru fighters, strong and brave, sight the river and rush forward at speed.

sentences.zh: 幕府總率貔貅，驍勇百萬，繕甲燕弧，屯兵冀馬，摐金沸地，鳴鞞聒天，霜鋒曜日，朱旗絳𥯔，方舟千里，駱驛係進。

translations.literal: The headquarters commands in all a million bold and brave troops—repairing armor and Yan bows, stationing soldiers on Ji horses; gongs shake the ground, drums deafen heaven; frost blades gleam in the sun, vermilion banners and crimson pennons; boats a thousand li, linked in succession advancing.
translations.idiomatic: This command gathers a million fierce warriors—armor polished, Yan bows strung, Ji horses stationed; bronze gongs shake the earth, war drums deafen the sky; frost-bright blades flash in sunlight, crimson banners and pennons blaze; a thousand li of boats advance in endless file.

sentences.zh: 蕭右軍訏謨上才，兼資文武，英略峻遠，執鈞匡世。

translations.literal: General of the Right Xiao—supreme talent in counsel, combining civil and martial gifts; heroic strategy lofty and far-reaching—holds the balance and rectifies the age.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Xiao is a man of supreme counsel, skilled in both civil and military affairs; his vision is bold and far-reaching, and he holds the scales that set the age right.

sentences.zh: 擁荊南之衆，督四方之師，宣贊中權，奉衛輿輦。

translations.literal: He holds the hosts of southern Jing, supervises armies of the four directions, proclaims and assists the central authority, guards and escorts the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He commands the forces of southern Jing, directs armies on every side, supports the central power, and guards the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 旍麾所指，威棱無外，龍驤虎步，並集建業。

translations.literal: Where his banners point, awe extends without outward limit; dragon-mounting, tiger-striding—all gather at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever his banners turn, none can stand against him; dragon and tiger alike converge on Jianye.

sentences.zh: 黜放愚狡，均禮海昏，廓清神甸，掃定京宇。

translations.literal: Drive out the foolish and cunning; restore proper ritual to the Sea-Dulled; clear the divine capital region; sweep and settle the capital realm.
translations.idiomatic: Cast out the wicked and deceitful; restore order to the ruined court; cleanse the sacred capital; sweep the realm clean.

sentences.zh: 譬猶崩泰山而壓蟻壤，決懸河而注熛燼，豈有不殄滅者哉！

translations.literal: It is like Mount Tai collapsing to crush an anthill, like a hanging river released to pour on blazing embers—how could anything not be exterminated!
translations.idiomatic: It is as if Mount Tai were falling on an anthill, as if a hanging river were poured onto burning coals—what could survive such ruin!

sentences.zh: 今資斧所加，止梅蟲兒、茹法珍而已。

translations.literal: Now the axe of punishment falls only on Mei Chon'er and Ru Fazhen.
translations.idiomatic: Now the punitive axe is aimed only at Mei Chon'er and Ru Fazhen.

sentences.zh: 諸君咸世胄羽儀，書勳王府，皆俛眉姦黨，受制凶威。

translations.literal: You all are noble heirs and feathered insignia of the age, merit recorded in the princely house—yet all bow brows to the wicked faction, controlled by brutal power.
translations.idiomatic: You are all noble scions and honored servants, men whose merit is recorded in the royal house—yet you bow to the villainous faction and submit to brutal force.

sentences.zh: 若能因變立功，轉禍爲福，並誓河、岳，永紆青紫。

translations.literal: If you can exploit change to achieve merit, turning disaster to blessing—all swearing by the River and Mount, forever granted purple and blue ranks.
translations.idiomatic: If you seize this moment to earn merit and turn disaster into fortune, you may swear by the River and Mount and receive rank and honor for generations.

sentences.zh: 若執迷不悟，距逆王師，大衆一臨，刑茲罔赦，所謂火烈高原，芝蘭同泯。

translations.literal: If you cling to delusion without awakening, resist the royal army—when the great host arrives, punishment will know no pardon; as they say, when fire blazes the high plain, orchid and mugwort perish together.
translations.idiomatic: If you persist in error and resist the imperial army, when the host arrives there will be no mercy—as the saying goes, when fire sweeps the high plain, orchid and mugwort burn alike.

sentences.zh: 勉求多福，無貽後悔。

translations.literal: Strive to seek much blessing; do not bring regret upon yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Seek your fortune now; do not leave yourselves room for regret.

sentences.zh: 賞罰之科，有如白水。

translations.literal: The law of reward and punishment is as clear as white water.
translations.idiomatic: Reward and punishment stand as clear as white water.

sentences.zh: 高祖至竟陵，命長史王茂與太守曹景宗爲前軍，中兵參軍張法安守竟陵城。

translations.literal: Gaozu reached Jingling and ordered Chief Administrator Wang Mao and Administrator Cao Jingzong as vanguard; Central Troops Officer Zhang Fa'an to hold Jingling city.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu reached Jingling and made Chief Administrator Wang Mao and Administrator Cao Jingzong the vanguard; Central Troops Officer Zhang Fa'an was left to guard Jingling city.

sentences.zh: 茂等至漢口，輕兵濟江，逼郢城。

translations.literal: Mao and the others reached Hankou; light troops crossed the river and pressed Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: Mao and his force reached Hankou; light troops crossed the river and pressed on Ying city.

sentences.zh: 其刺史張沖置陣據石橋浦，義師與戰不利，軍主朱僧起死之。

translations.literal: Its inspector Zhang Chong set battle lines and held Stone Bridge Ford; the righteous army fought without success, and Army Commander Zhu Sengqi died in the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Zhang Chong drew up his lines at Stone Bridge Ford; the righteous army fought unsuccessfully, and Army Commander Zhu Sengqi was killed.

sentences.zh: 諸將議欲並軍圍郢，分兵以襲西陽、武昌。

translations.literal: The generals discussed combining forces to besiege Ying and dividing troops to strike Xiyang and Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The generals debated merging the armies to besiege Ying while sending detachments against Xiyang and Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「漢口不闊一里，箭道交至，房僧寄以重兵固守，爲郢城人掎角。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "Hankou is less than a li wide; arrow-paths cross from every direction; Fang Sengji holds fast with heavy troops, forming pincers with the people of Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Hankou is less than a li across; arrows can cross from every side; Fang Sengji holds it with a heavy force, pincering Ying city from without.

sentences.zh: 若悉衆前進，賊必絕我軍後，一朝爲阻，則悔無所及。

translations.literal: If we advance with the full host, the enemy will certainly cut off our rear; once blocked in a day, regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: If we move the whole army forward, the enemy will surely cut our rear; once trapped, regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 今欲遣王、曹諸軍濟江，與荊州軍相會，以逼賊壘。

translations.literal: Now I wish to send Wang, Cao, and the other armies across the river to join the Jingzhou army and press the enemy fort.
translations.idiomatic: Now I mean to send Wang, Cao, and the rest across the river to join the Jingzhou force and press the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 吾自後圍魯山，以通沔、漢。

translations.literal: I myself will surround Mount Lu from behind to open the Mian and Han route.
translations.idiomatic: I will myself take Mount Lu from the rear and open the route between the Mian and Han rivers.

sentences.zh: 鄖城、竟陵間粟，方舟而下；

translations.literal: Grain between Ying city and Jingling will come down in linked boats;
translations.idiomatic: Grain from between Ying city and Jingling will be floated down in convoys;

sentences.zh: 江陵、湘中之兵，連旗繼至。

translations.literal: Troops from Jiangling and mid-Xiang will arrive with banners in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers from Jiangling and the Xiang basin will follow with banners one after another.

sentences.zh: 糧食旣足，士衆稍多，圍守兩城，不攻自拔，天下之事，臥取之耳。

translations.literal: Once provisions are sufficient and soldiers somewhat numerous, besieging and holding both cities—without attack they will surrender of themselves; the affairs of the realm will be taken while lying down."
translations.idiomatic: Once grain is ample and our numbers grow, we need only hold both cities under siege—they will fall without a fight, and the realm will be ours as if taken at rest."

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆曰「善」。

translations.literal: The generals all said, "Well said."
translations.idiomatic: The generals all agreed, "Excellent."

sentences.zh: 乃命王茂、曹景宗帥衆濟岸，進頓九里。

translations.literal: He then ordered Wang Mao and Cao Jingzong to lead the host across the shore and advance to encamp at Jiuli.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Wang Mao and Cao Jingzong to lead the army across and encamp at Jiuli.

sentences.zh: 其日，張沖出軍迎戰，茂等邀擊，大破之，皆棄甲奔走。

translations.literal: That day Zhang Chong came out with troops to meet battle; Mao and the others intercepted and struck, routing them completely—all cast off armor and fled.
translations.idiomatic: That day Zhang Chong came out to fight; Mao and the others intercepted him, broke his force completely, and the enemy threw off their armor and fled.

sentences.zh: 荊州遣冠軍將軍鄧元起、軍主王世興、田安等數千人，會大軍於夏首。

translations.literal: Jingzhou sent Champion General Deng Yuanqi, Army Commander Wang Shixing, Tian An, and several thousand others to join the main army at Xia Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou sent Champion General Deng Yuanqi, Army Commander Wang Shixing, Tian An, and several thousand men to join the main force at Xia Shou.

sentences.zh: 高祖築漢口城以守魯山，命水軍主張惠紹、朱思遠等游遏江中，絕郢、魯二城信使。

translations.literal: Gaozu built Hankou city to hold Mount Lu, and ordered naval commanders Zhang Huishao, Zhu Siyuan, and others to patrol and block the river, cutting communication between Ying and Lu cities.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu built Hankou city to guard Mount Lu and ordered naval commanders Zhang Huishao and Zhu Siyuan to patrol the river and sever communications between Ying and Lu.

sentences.zh: 三月，乃命元起進據南堂西陼，田安之頓城北，王世興頓曲水故城。

translations.literal: In the third month he ordered Yuanqi to advance and hold the western islet of South Hall; Tian An encamped north of the city; Wang Shixing encamped at the old city of Qu Shui.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he ordered Yuanqi to take the western islet of South Hall; Tian An encamped north of the city; Wang Shixing encamped at the old city of Qu Shui.

sentences.zh: 是時張沖死，其衆復推軍主薛元嗣及沖長史程茂爲主。

translations.literal: At this time Zhang Chong died; his troops again raised Army Commander Xue Yuansi and Chong's chief administrator Cheng Mao as leaders.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Zhang Chong died; his men again made Army Commander Xue Yuansi and Chong's chief administrator Cheng Mao their leaders.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，南康王卽帝位於江陵，改永元三年爲中興元年，遙廢東昏爲涪陵王。

translations.literal: On day yisi, the Prince of Nankang ascended the throne at Jiangling, changing the third year of Yongyuan to the first year of Zhongxing, and remotely deposed Dong Hun as Prince of Fuling.
translations.idiomatic: On day yisi the Prince of Nankang took the throne at Jiangling, renamed the third year of Yongyuan as the first year of Zhongxing, and deposed Dong Hun from afar as Prince of Fuling.

sentences.zh: 以高祖爲尚書左僕射，加征東大將軍、都督征討諸軍事，假黃鉞。

translations.literal: Gaozu was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, additionally Great General Who Conquers the East and Commander of all punitive military affairs, granted the yellow battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, additionally made Great General Who Conquers the East and commander of all punitive forces, and granted the yellow battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 西臺又遣冠軍將軍蕭穎達領兵會于軍。

translations.literal: The Western Secretariat also sent Champion General Xiao Yingda to lead troops and join the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Secretariat also sent Champion General Xiao Yingda with troops to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 是日，元嗣軍主沈難當率輕舸數千，亂流來戰，張惠紹等擊破，盡擒之。

translations.literal: That same day, Yuansi's Army Commander Shen Nandang led several thousand light boats, coming to fight in the confused current; Zhang Huishao and others struck and broke them, capturing all.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Yuansi's commander Shen Nandang led several thousand light boats into the swirling current to fight; Zhang Huishao and the others defeated them and took every man.

sentences.zh: 四月，高祖出沔，命王茂、蕭穎達等進軍逼郢城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Gaozu exited the Mian and ordered Wang Mao, Xiao Yingda, and others to advance and press Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Gaozu moved out along the Mian and ordered Wang Mao, Xiao Yingda, and the rest to advance against Ying city.

sentences.zh: 元嗣戰頗疲，因不敢出。

translations.literal: Yuansi was quite worn from battle and therefore dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansi was exhausted by fighting and no longer dared to sally forth.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲攻之，高祖不許。

translations.literal: The generals wished to attack; Gaozu did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to assault the city; Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 五月，東昏遣寧朔將軍吳子陽、軍主光子衿等十三軍救郢州，進據巴口。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Dong Hun sent Pacification North General Wu Ziyang, Army Commander Guang Zijin, and thirteen armies to relieve Yingzhou, advancing to hold Bako.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Dong Hun sent Pacification North General Wu Ziyang, Army Commander Guang Zijin, and thirteen armies to rescue Yingzhou, advancing to occupy Bako.

sentences.zh: 六月，西臺遣衛尉席闡文勞軍，齎蕭穎胄等議，謂高祖曰：「今頓兵兩岸，不併軍圍郢，定西陽、武昌，取江州，此機已失；

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Western Secretariat sent Chamberlain Xi Chanwen to comfort the army, bearing deliberations from Xiao Yingzhao and others, saying to Gaozu: "Now with troops halted on both banks, not combining forces to besiege Ying, securing Xiyang and Wuchang, and taking Jiangzhou—this opportunity is already lost;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Western Secretariat sent Chamberlain Xi Chanwen to visit the army with a proposal from Xiao Yingzhao and others, telling Gaozu, "With troops halted on both banks, failing to combine forces, besiege Ying, secure Xiyang and Wuchang, and seize Jiangzhou—that chance is already gone;

sentences.zh: 莫若請救於魏，與北連和，猶爲上策。

translations.literal: better to seek aid from Wei and join in alliance with the north—that would still be the superior plan."
translations.idiomatic: better to ask Wei for help and ally with the north—that would still be the best course."

sentences.zh: 」高祖謂闡文曰：「漢口路通荊、雍，控引秦、梁，糧運資儲，聽此氣息，所以兵壓漢口，連絡數州。

translations.literal: Gaozu said to Chanwen: "Hankou's routes connect Jing and Yong, control and draw on Qin and Liang; grain transport and supplies depend on its breath—therefore we press troops on Hankou, linking several provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told Chanwen, "Hankou links Jing and Yong, controls Qin and Liang, and holds the lifeline of grain and supplies—that is why we press the army on Hankou and tie several provinces together.

sentences.zh: 今若併軍圍城，又分兵前進，魯山必阻沔路，所謂扼喉。

translations.literal: If we now combine armies to besiege the city while also sending detachments forward, Lushan will block the Mian route—what they call "strangling the throat."
translations.idiomatic: If we mass for a siege and still split columns to push ahead, Lushan will choke the Mian route—the classic grip on the throat.

sentences.zh: 若糧運不通，自然離散，何謂持久？

translations.literal: If grain transport is cut off, the host will naturally disperse—what is meant by lasting out?
translations.idiomatic: Cut the grain lines and the army falls apart on its own—where is the staying power in that?

sentences.zh: 鄧元起近欲以三千兵往定尋陽，彼若歡然悟機，一酈生亦足；

translations.literal: Deng Yuanqi recently wishes to take three thousand men to secure Xunyang; if they readily grasp the moment, one Li Yi would suffice;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yuanqi wants three thousand men to take Xunyang; if the town sees its chance and yields, a single envoy like Li Yi is enough;

sentences.zh: 脫距王師，故非三千能下。

translations.literal: but if they resist the royal army, three thousand cannot take it.
translations.idiomatic: but if they stand against the imperial force, three thousand will not suffice.

sentences.zh: 進退無據，未見其可。

translations.literal: Advancing or retreating without footing—I do not see how it can work.
translations.idiomatic: With no firm ground to advance or fall back on, I see no way this succeeds.

sentences.zh: 西陽、武昌，取便得耳，得便應鎮守。

translations.literal: Xiyang and Wuchang can be taken when convenient; once taken they ought to be garrisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyang and Wuchang can be seized when the moment allows—and once taken, they must be held.

sentences.zh: 守兩城不減萬人，糧儲稱是，卒無所出。

translations.literal: Garrisoning both cities requires no fewer than ten thousand men, and commensurate grain stores—with no troops left over.
translations.idiomatic: Holding both towns takes at least ten thousand men and matching stores, leaving nothing in reserve.

sentences.zh: 脫賊軍有上者，萬人攻一城，兩城勢不得相救。

translations.literal: If enemy forces come upstream, ten thousand attack one city, and the two cities cannot aid each other.
translations.idiomatic: If rebels move upriver, ten thousand can storm one town while the other cannot help.

sentences.zh: 若我分軍應援，則首尾俱弱；

translations.literal: If we split forces to reinforce, both ends grow weak;
translations.idiomatic: Split to relieve them and both wings weaken;

sentences.zh: 如其不遣，孤城必陷。

translations.literal: if we send none, the isolated city will surely fall.
translations.idiomatic: send none and the lone fortress is lost.

sentences.zh: 一城旣沒，諸城相次土崩，天下大事於是去矣。

translations.literal: Once one city falls, the other cities collapse in succession, and the great enterprise of the realm is lost thereby.
translations.idiomatic: One city gone, the rest crumble in turn—and with them the realm's great cause.

sentences.zh: 若郢州旣拔，席捲沿流，西陽、武昌，自然風靡，何遽分兵散衆，自貽其憂！

translations.literal: If Yingzhou is taken, sweeping downstream, Xiyang and Wuchang will naturally bow before us—why hurry to divide troops and scatter the host, bringing trouble on ourselves!
translations.idiomatic: Take Yingzhou and sweep downriver—Xiyang and Wuchang will fall of themselves. Why rush to split the army and invite our own trouble!

sentences.zh: 且丈夫舉動，言靜天步；

translations.literal: Moreover, when a man of resolve acts, his words should steady the steps of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Besides, a true man's deeds should calm the very pace of Heaven;

sentences.zh: 況擁數州之兵以誅羣豎，懸河注火，奚有不滅？

translations.literal: how much more when wielding the armies of several provinces to execute the ruffian band—like pouring a river or pouring fire—is there anything that would not be destroyed?
translations.idiomatic: how much less when we hold several provinces' worth of troops to crush these villains—like a river poured out or fire tipped over—what could stand?

sentences.zh: 豈容北面請救，以自示弱！

translations.literal: How can we turn north to beg for aid and show our own weakness!
translations.idiomatic: How can we face north and plead for rescue, exposing our weakness!

sentences.zh: 彼未必能信，徒貽我醜聲。

translations.literal: They may well not trust us, and we gain only shame.
translations.idiomatic: They may not believe us anyway—we would only earn disgrace.

sentences.zh: 此之下計，何謂上策？

translations.literal: This is the lower plan—how can it be called the upper strategy?
translations.idiomatic: That is the worst counsel—how can anyone call it the best plan?

sentences.zh: 卿爲我白鎮軍：前途攻取，但以見付，事在目中，無患不捷，恃鎮軍靖鎮之耳。」

translations.literal: You tell the Pacification General for me: for future conquests, simply leave them to me; the matter is plain to the eye, and there is no fear of failure—I rely only on the Pacification General to hold things quiet and firm."
translations.idiomatic: Tell the Pacification General for me: leave the fighting ahead to me. It is plain before our eyes; success is certain. I ask only that he keep the rear calm and secure."

sentences.zh: 吳子陽等進軍武口，高祖乃命軍主梁天惠、蔡道祐據漁湖城，唐脩期、劉道曼屯白陽壘，夾兩岸而待之。

translations.literal: Wu Ziyang and others advanced on Wukou; Gaozu then ordered army commanders Liang Tianhui and Cai Daoyou to hold Yuhu City, and Tang Xiuqi and Liu Daoman to camp at Baiyang Fortress, waiting on both banks.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ziyang marched on Wukou. Gaozu posted Liang Tianhui and Cai Daoyou at Yuhu City and Tang Xiuqi and Liu Daoman at Baiyang Fortress, lining both shores.

sentences.zh: 子陽又進據加湖，去郢三十里，傍山帶水，築壘柵以自固。

translations.literal: Ziyang then advanced and held Jiahu, thirty li from Ying, leaning on mountains and embracing water, building ramparts and palisades for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyang next seized Jiahu, thirty li from Ying, backed by hills and fronted by water, and walled himself in with ramparts and palisades.

sentences.zh: 魯山城主房僧寄死，衆復推助防孫樂祖代之。

translations.literal: Lushan garrison commander Fang Sengji died; the host again raised Assistant Defender Sun Lezu to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Sengji, commander of Lushan, died; the garrison again chose Assistant Defender Sun Lezu to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 七月，高祖命王茂帥軍主曹仲宗、康絢、武會超等潛師襲加湖，將逼子陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Gaozu ordered Wang Mao to lead army commanders Cao Zhongzong, Kang Xuan, Wu Huichao, and others with a secret force to strike Jiahu, pressing close on Ziyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Gaozu sent Wang Mao with Cao Zhongzong, Kang Xuan, Wu Huichao, and others in a hidden column to strike Jiahu and close on Ziyang.

sentences.zh: 水涸不通艦，其夜暴長，衆軍乘流齊進，鼓噪攻之，賊俄而大潰，子陽等竄走，衆盡溺于江。

translations.literal: The water had fallen and boats could not pass; that night it rose in a sudden flood. The armies rode the current forward together, drumming and shouting in the assault; the rebels soon broke completely, and Ziyang and others fled—in the end all drowned in the river.
translations.idiomatic: The river had dropped too low for ships; that night it surged. The whole force rode the flood together, drums roaring as they attacked. The enemy broke at once. Ziyang and his officers fled—and in the end all drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 王茂虜其餘而旋。

translations.literal: Wang Mao captured the remainder and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mao took the survivors and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是郢、魯二城相視奪氣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the two cities of Ying and Lu lost heart at sight of each other.
