translations.idiomatic: Ying and Lushan, looking across at each other, lost all spirit.

sentences.zh: 先是，東昏遣冠軍將軍陳伯之鎮江州，爲子陽等聲援。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dong Hun had sent Champion General Chen Bozhi to garrison Jiangzhou as support for Ziyang and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Before this Dong Hun had posted Champion General Chen Bozhi at Jiangzhou to back Wu Ziyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃謂諸將曰：「夫征討未必須實力，所聽威聲耳。

translations.literal: Gaozu then told the generals: "Expedition and punishment do not always require real strength—what matters is the authority of renown.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told his commanders, "Campaigns are not always won by brute force alone. What counts is the weight of your name.

sentences.zh: 今加湖之敗，誰不弭服。

translations.literal: Who now, after the defeat at Jiahu, would not submit in awe?
translations.idiomatic: After Jiahu, who would not bow his head?

sentences.zh: 陳虎牙卽伯之子，狼狽奔歸，彼間人情，理當忷懼，我謂九江傳檄可定也。

translations.literal: Chen Huya is Bozhi's son; he fled back in disarray. The mood in that region must surely be panic—I say Jiujiang can be settled by proclamation alone."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huya is Bozhi's son—he ran home in tatters. The whole region must be terrified. I say Jiujiang can be taken by proclamation alone."

sentences.zh: 」因命搜所獲俘囚，得伯之幢主蘇隆之，厚加賞賜，使致命焉。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered a search among captured prisoners and found Bozhi's banner-chief Su Longzhi, richly rewarded him, and had him carry a message.
translations.idiomatic: He searched the prisoners, found Bozhi's banner-chief Su Longzhi, rewarded him generously, and sent him back with a letter.

sentences.zh: 魯山城主孫樂祖、郢城主程茂、薛元嗣相繼請降。

translations.literal: Lushan commander Sun Lezu, Ying commander Cheng Mao, and Xue Yuansi all successively asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lezu at Lushan, Cheng Mao at Ying, and Xue Yuansi all surrendered in turn.

sentences.zh: 初，郢城之閉，將佐文武男女口十餘萬人，疾疫流腫死者十七八，及城開，高祖並加隱卹，其死者命給棺槥。

translations.literal: At first, when Ying city was closed, civil and military officers and men, women and children numbered over a hundred thousand; plague and swelling sickness killed seven or eight in ten, and when the city opened Gaozu extended compassionate relief to all; for the dead he ordered coffins supplied.
translations.idiomatic: While Ying was besieged, more than a hundred thousand people—soldiers, officials, men, women, and children—were inside. Plague and swelling sickness killed seven or eight in ten. When the city fell Gaozu showed mercy to all survivors and ordered coffins for the dead.

sentences.zh: 先是，汝南人胡文超起義於灄陽，求討義陽、安陸等郡以自效，高祖又遣軍主唐脩期攻隨郡，並剋之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Runan man Hu Wenchao had risen in rebellion at Zhenyang, offering to attack Yiyang, Anlu, and other commanderies to prove his loyalty; Gaozu also sent army commander Tang Xiuqi to attack Suicommandery, and both were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Hu Wenchao of Runan had risen at Zhenyang, offering to seize Yiyang, Anlu, and neighboring commanderies for the cause. Gaozu also sent Tang Xiuqi against Suicommandery. Both efforts succeeded.

sentences.zh: 司州刺史王僧景遣子貞孫入質。

translations.literal: Inspector of Sizhou Wang Sengjing sent his son Zhensun in as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengjing, inspector of Sizhou, sent his son Zhensun as hostage.

sentences.zh: 司部悉平。

translations.literal: The Sizhou region was wholly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: All of Sizhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 陳伯之遣蘇隆之反命，求未便進軍。

translations.literal: Chen Bozhi sent Su Longzhi back with a reply, asking that advance not be made before a suitable moment.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bozhi returned Su Longzhi with a reply asking that the army not advance until conditions were right.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「伯之此言，意懷首鼠，及其猶豫，急往逼之，計無所出，勢不得暴。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "In this remark Bozhi reveals a vacillating mind; while he still hesitates, press him hard—he will have no plan, and circumstances will not allow violence."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "That answer shows a man with one foot in each camp. While he wavers, press him hard. He will have no plan left, and the moment will not allow him to resist."

sentences.zh: 」乃命鄧元起率衆，卽日沿流。

translations.literal: He then ordered Deng Yuanqi to lead the host downstream that same day.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he ordered Deng Yuanqi to march the army downriver.

sentences.zh: 八月，天子遣黃門郎蘇回勞軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Son of Heaven sent Yellow Gate Gentleman Su Hui to congratulate the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the emperor sent Yellow Gate Gentleman Su Hui to congratulate the troops.

sentences.zh: 高祖登舟，命諸將以次進路，留上庸太守韋叡守郢城，行州事。

translations.literal: Gaozu boarded his boat and ordered the generals to advance in turn; he left Upper Yong Administrator Wei Rui to guard Ying city and conduct provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu embarked and sent the generals forward in sequence, leaving Upper Yong Administrator Wei Rui to hold Ying and govern the province.

sentences.zh: 鄧元起將至尋陽，陳伯之猶猜懼，乃收兵退保湖口，留其子虎牙守盆城。

translations.literal: As Deng Yuanqi was about to reach Xunyang, Chen Bozhi still nursed suspicion and fear; he gathered his troops and withdrew to hold Hukou, leaving his son Huya to guard Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Yuanqi neared Xunyang, Chen Bozhi still mistrusted the cause. He pulled back to Hukou and left his son Huya at Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 及高祖至，乃束甲請罪。

translations.literal: When Gaozu arrived, Bozhi bound his armor and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu arrived, Bozhi laid down his arms and asked for pardon.

sentences.zh: 九月，天子詔高祖平定東夏，並以便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Son of Heaven decreed that Gaozu pacify Eastern Xia and act at discretion as events required.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor authorized Gaozu to pacify Eastern Xia and act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 是月，留少府、長史鄭紹叔守江州城。

translations.literal: That month, he left Junior Master of the Palace and Chief Clerk Zheng Shaoshu to guard Jiangzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: That month he left Junior Master of the Palace and chief clerk Zheng Shaoshu to hold Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 前軍次蕪湖，南豫州刺史申胄棄姑孰走，至是時大軍進據之，仍遣曹景宗、蕭穎達領馬步進頓江寧。

translations.literal: The vanguard halted at Wuhu; South Yuzhou Inspector Shen Zhou abandoned Gushu and fled; at this the great army advanced and occupied it, and still sent Cao Jingzong and Xiao Yingda to lead horse and foot and encamp at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard stopped at Wuhu. Shen Zhou, inspector of South Yuzhou, abandoned Gushu and fled. The main force took it and sent Cao Jingzong and Xiao Yingda with cavalry and infantry to encamp at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 東昏遣征虜將軍李居士率步軍迎戰，景宗擊走之。

translations.literal: Dong Hun sent Campaign General Li Jushi with foot soldiers to meet in battle; Jingzong struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Hun sent Campaign General Li Jushi with infantry to meet them. Cao Jingzong routed him.

sentences.zh: 於是王茂、鄧元起、呂僧珍進據赤鼻邏，曹景宗、陳伯之爲游兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Mao, Deng Yuanqi, and Lu Sengzhen advanced and held Chibiyi Rampart; Cao Jingzong and Chen Bozhi served as mobile detachments.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mao, Deng Yuanqi, and Lu Sengzhen then took Chibiyi Rampart. Cao Jingzong and Chen Bozhi served as flying columns.

sentences.zh: 是日，新亭城主江道林率兵出戰，衆軍擒之於陣。

translations.literal: That day, Xinting garrison commander Jiang Daolin led troops out to fight; the armies captured him in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: That day Xinting commander Jiang Daolin came out to fight and was taken in the line of battle.

sentences.zh: 大軍次新林，命王茂進據越城，曹景宗據皁莢橋，鄧元起據道士墩，陳伯之據籬門。

translations.literal: The great army reached Xinglin, ordered Wang Mao to advance and hold Yue City, Cao Jingzong to hold Zaojia Bridge, Deng Yuanqi to hold Daoshi Mound, and Chen Bozhi to hold Limen.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Xinglin. Wang Mao took Yue City, Cao Jingzong Zaojia Bridge, Deng Yuanqi Daoshi Mound, and Chen Bozhi Limen.

sentences.zh: 道林餘衆退屯航南，義軍迫之，因復散走，退保朱爵，憑淮以自固。

translations.literal: Daolin's remaining troops withdrew and encamped south of the crossing; the Righteous Army pressed them, and they again scattered and fled, retreating to hold Zhujue, relying on the Huai for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Daolin's survivors fell back south of the crossing. The Righteous Army pressed them; they broke again and withdrew to Zhujue, clinging to the Huai for cover.

sentences.zh: 時李居士猶據新亭壘，請東昏燒南岸邑屋以開戰場。

translations.literal: At the time Li Jushi still held the Xinting fortress and asked Dong Hun to burn the towns on the south bank to open a battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jushi still held the Xinting fort and asked Dong Hun to burn the south-bank towns and clear a field of battle.

sentences.zh: 自大航以西、新亭以北，蕩然矣。

translations.literal: From the Great Crossing west to Xinting north, all was laid bare.
translations.idiomatic: From the Great Crossing west to Xinting north, nothing was left standing.

sentences.zh: 十月，東昏石頭軍主朱僧勇率水軍二千人歸降。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Dong Hun's Shitou garrison commander Zhu Sengyong led two thousand water troops in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zhu Sengyong, Dong Hun's commander at Shitou, surrendered with two thousand sailors.

sentences.zh: 東昏又遣征虜將軍王珍國率軍主胡虎牙等列陣于航南大路，悉配精手利器，尚十餘萬人。

translations.literal: Dong Hun again sent Campaign General Wang Zhenguo leading army commanders Hu Huya and others to deploy ranks on the great road south of the crossing, all equipped with crack archers and sharp weapons—more than a hundred thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Hun sent Campaign General Wang Zhenguo with Hu Huya and other commanders to form battle lines on the road south of the crossing, all armed with elite archers and sharp weapons—more than a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 閹人王倀子持白虎幡督率諸軍，又開航背水，以絕歸路。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wang Shuan held the white tiger banner to supervise the armies, and opened the crossing with water at the rear to cut off retreat.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Shuan carried the white tiger banner to direct the host and flooded the crossing behind them to cut off retreat.

sentences.zh: 王茂、曹景宗等掎角奔之，將士皆殊死戰，無不一當百，鼓噪震天地。

translations.literal: Wang Mao, Cao Jingzong, and others attacked from both flanks; officers and men all fought to the death, none failing to meet one against a hundred—the drum and shout shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mao and Cao Jingzong hit them from both sides. Every man fought as if one could match a hundred. The roar of drums shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 珍國之衆，一時土崩，投淮死者，積尸與航等，後至者乘之以濟，於是朱爵諸軍望之皆潰。

translations.literal: Zhenguo's host collapsed at once; those who plunged into the Huai drowned until corpses piled level with the crossing, and those who came later crossed on them; thereupon all the Zhujue armies saw this and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguo's army shattered at once. Men who threw themselves into the Huai drowned until the dead piled even with the crossing, and those behind walked over them to get across. Every force at Zhujue broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 義軍追至宣陽門，李居士以新亭壘、徐元瑜以東府城降，石頭、白下諸軍並宵潰。

translations.literal: The Righteous Army pursued to Xuanyang Gate; Li Jushi surrendered with the Xinting fortress, and Xu Yuanyu with the Eastern Mansion city; the Shitou and Baixia garrisons all fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The Righteous Army chased them to Xuanyang Gate. Li Jushi surrendered the Xinting fort; Xu Yuanyu surrendered the Eastern Mansion. The garrisons at Shitou and Baixia melted away overnight.

sentences.zh: 壬午，高祖鎮石頭，命衆軍圍六門，東昏悉焚燒門內，驅逼營署、官府並入城，有衆二十萬。

translations.literal: On day rencwu, Gaozu garrisoned Shitou and ordered the armies to surround the six gates; Dong Hun burned everything inside the gates, drove camps and government offices into the city, and had two hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: On day rencwu Gaozu occupied Shitou and surrounded the six gates. Dong Hun burned the districts within the walls, herded camps and offices into the city, and mustered two hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史桓和紿東昏出戰，因以其衆來降。

translations.literal: Qingzhou Inspector Huan He deceived Dong Hun into coming out to fight, then came over with his troops in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Huan He, inspector of Qingzhou, tricked Dong Hun into marching out, then defected with his whole force.

sentences.zh: 高祖命諸軍築長圍。

translations.literal: Gaozu ordered the armies to build a long encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu ordered a long siege line built around the city.

sentences.zh: 初，義師之逼，東昏遣軍主左僧慶鎮京口，常僧景鎮廣陵，李叔獻屯瓜步，及申胄自姑孰奔歸，又使屯破墩以爲東北聲援。

translations.literal: At first, when the Righteous Army pressed close, Dong Hun had sent garrison commander Left Sengqing to hold Jingkou, Chang Sengjing to hold Guangling, and Li Shuxian to encamp at Guabu; when Shen Zhou fled Gushu and returned, he was also sent to encamp at Podun as northeast support.
translations.idiomatic: When the Righteous Army first closed in, Dong Hun had posted Left Sengqing at Jingkou, Chang Sengjing at Guangling, and Li Shuxian at Guabu. When Shen Zhou fled back from Gushu, he too was sent to Podun to guard the northeast.

sentences.zh: 至是，高祖遣使曉喻，並率衆降。

translations.literal: At this Gaozu sent envoys to explain and persuade them; all led their hosts in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu now sent envoys to win them over, and all came over with their troops.

sentences.zh: 乃遣弟輔國將軍秀鎮京口，輔國將軍恢屯破墩，從弟寧朔將軍景鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: He then sent his younger brother Auxiliary General Xiu to garrison Jingkou, Auxiliary General Hui to encamp at Podun, and his younger cousin Unassuming General Jing to garrison Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He posted his brother Auxiliary General Xiu at Jingkou, Auxiliary General Hui at Podun, and his cousin Unassuming General Jing at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 吳郡太守蔡夤棄郡赴義師。

translations.literal: Wu commandery Administrator Cai Yin abandoned his commandery and joined the Righteous Army.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yin, administrator of Wu commandery, left his post and joined the Righteous Army.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙寅旦，兼衛尉張稷、北徐州刺史王珍國斬東昏，送首義師。

translations.literal: On the morning of day bingyin in the twelfth month, Concurrent Minister of the Guard Zhang Ji and North Xuzhou Inspector Wang Zhenguo beheaded Dong Hun and sent his head to the Righteous Army.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on day bingyin in the twelfth month, Concurrent Minister of the Guard Zhang Ji and North Xuzhou Inspector Wang Zhenguo cut off Dong Hun's head and sent it to the Righteous Army.

sentences.zh: 高祖命呂僧珍勒兵封府庫及圖籍，收㜸妾潘妃及凶黨王咺之以下四十一人屬吏，誅之。

translations.literal: Gaozu ordered Lu Sengzhen to marshal troops to seal the treasuries and archives, seize the concubine Consort Pan and the villainous faction including Wang Xuanzhi—forty-one persons in all—and turn them over to the judicial officers for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu ordered Lu Sengzhen to seal the treasuries and archives, seize Consort Pan and the ringleaders led by Wang Xuanzhi—forty-one people in all—and hand them to the courts for execution.

sentences.zh: 宣德皇后令廢涪陵王爲東昏侯，依漢海昏侯故事。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuande decreed the deposed Prince of Fuling reduced to Marquis Donghun, following the precedent of Han's Marquis of Haihun.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuande stripped the deposed Prince of Fuling of his rank and made him Marquis Donghun, on the model of Han's Marquis of Haihun.

sentences.zh: 授高祖中書監、都督揚南徐二州諸軍事、大司馬、錄尚書、驃騎大將軍、揚州刺史，封建安郡公，食邑萬戶，給班劍四十人，黃鉞、侍中、征討諸軍事並如故；

translations.literal: Gaozu was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing, Commander of military affairs of Yang and South Xu provinces, Grand Marshal, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Fast General-in-Chief, and Inspector of Yangzhou; enfeoffed as Duke of Jian'an commandery, fief of ten thousand households; granted forty halberd guards; yellow battle-axe, Palace Attendant, and campaign command—all as before;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was made Director of the Masters of Writing, commander of Yang and South Xu military affairs, Grand Marshal, supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Fast General-in-Chief, and inspector of Yangzhou; enfeoffed Duke of Jian'an commandery with ten thousand households; granted forty halberd guards; yellow battle-axe, palace attendant, and campaign authority unchanged;

sentences.zh: 依晉武陵王遵承制故事。

translations.literal: following the precedent of Jin's Prince of Wuling Zun exercising regal authority.
translations.idiomatic: following Jin's precedent of Prince of Wuling Zun acting with imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 己卯，高祖入屯閱武堂。

translations.literal: On day jimao, Gaozu entered and encamped at the Review-of-Troops Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On day jimao Gaozu moved into the Review-of-Troops Hall.

sentences.zh: 下令曰：「皇家不造，遘此昏凶，禍挻動植，虐被人鬼，社廟之危，蠢焉如綴。

translations.literal: He issued an order: "The imperial house met misfortune and encountered this benighted villain; calamity reached moving things and planted things, cruelty afflicted men and ghosts; the altars hung by a thread, tottering as if on a fraying cord.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed, "The dynasty has suffered ruin and met this dark tyrant. Disaster touched every living thing; cruelty reached from men to ghosts. The altars of state hang by a thread, swaying as if on a fraying cord.

sentences.zh: 吾身籍皇宗，曲荷先顧，受任邊疆，推轂萬里，眷言瞻烏，痛心在目，故率其尊主之情，厲其忘生之志。

translations.literal: I by birth belong to the imperial clan, was privately favored by my predecessors, received duty on the frontier, trusted at the chariot yoke ten thousand li away; gazing at the parentless bird, the pain is before my eyes—therefore I lead the sentiment of honoring the sovereign and stiffen the will to forget life itself.
translations.idiomatic: I am of the imperial blood, was favored by those before me, and was trusted on the frontier a thousand leagues away. When I see the orphaned bird, grief is before my eyes—so I roused the loyal heart and hardened the will to risk my life.

sentences.zh: 雖寶曆重升，明命有紹，而獨夫醜縱，方煽京邑。

translations.literal: Though the precious mandate rises anew and the bright mandate has a successor, this lone villain's ugly excess still fans the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Though the throne is restored and the mandate renewed, this lone monster's wickedness still burns in the capital.

sentences.zh: 投袂援戈，克弭多難。

translations.literal: I flung aside my sleeves and grasped my weapon, and was able to quell many disasters.
translations.idiomatic: I rolled up my sleeves, took up arms, and put down many calamities.

sentences.zh: 虐政橫流，爲日旣久，同惡相濟，諒非一族。

translations.literal: Tyrannical government has flowed unchecked for long; those sharing the same evil aid one another—it is surely not one clan alone.
translations.idiomatic: Bad government has run wild for years. Those who shared in the evil helped one another—it was not one house alone.

sentences.zh: 仰稟朝命，任在專征，思播皇澤，被之率土。

translations.literal: Looking up to receive the court's command, my charge is sole expedition; I think to spread imperial grace and cover all within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Heeding the court's charge, my duty is to lead the campaign alone. I mean to spread imperial mercy over all the realm.

sentences.zh: 凡厥負釁，咸與惟新。

translations.literal: All who bear guilt shall share in renewal.
translations.idiomatic: All who have sinned shall share in a new beginning.

sentences.zh: 可大赦天下；

translations.literal: Let there be a great amnesty throughout the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the land;

sentences.zh: 唯王咺之等四十一人不在赦例。」

translations.literal: only Wang Xuanzhi and forty-one others are excluded from amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanzhi and forty-one others alone are excluded."

sentences.zh: 又令曰：「夫樹以司牧，非役物以養生；

translations.literal: Another order: "Trees are planted to appoint shepherds—not to enslave things to nourish the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered, "Officials are set over the people to govern them—not to grind the world down to feed a tyrant.

sentences.zh: 視民如傷，豈肆上以縱虐。

translations.literal: To see the people as wounded—how could one above indulge cruelty at will?
translations.idiomatic: To treat the people as if every wound were your own—how could a ruler indulge cruelty at will?

sentences.zh: 廢主棄常，自絕宗廟。

translations.literal: The deposed lord abandoned the constant way and cut himself off from the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor cast off the eternal order and severed himself from the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 窮凶極悖，書契未有。

translations.literal: His extremity of wickedness and utter perversity have no parallel in written record.
translations.idiomatic: His wickedness and perversity exceed anything recorded in history.

sentences.zh: 征賦不一，苛酷滋章。

translations.literal: Levies and taxes were inconsistent; harshness and cruelty daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were arbitrary and cruelty grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 緹繡土木，菽粟犬馬，徵發閭左，以充繕築。

translations.literal: Silk embroidery and timber works, grain and dogs and horses—the commonfolk of the lanes were conscripted to fill construction needs.
translations.idiomatic: Silk brocades and timber palaces, grain and horses and dogs—the people of the lanes were dragooned to build them.

sentences.zh: 流離寒暑，繼以疫鬁，轉死溝渠，曾莫救恤，朽肉枯骸，烏鳶是厭。

translations.literal: Driven from summer heat to winter cold, then struck by plague and pestilence; dying they fell into ditches, never once relieved—rotten flesh and dry bones fed crows and kites.
translations.idiomatic: They were driven through heat and cold, then plague followed. They died in ditches with no one to save them. Rotting flesh and bare bones were food for crows and kites.

sentences.zh: 加以天災人火，屢焚宮掖，官府臺寺，尺椽無遺，悲甚《黍離》，痛兼《麥秀》。

translations.literal: Added to this were heaven's disasters and human fires; palace quarters and official halls were repeatedly burned, not a foot of rafter left—grief like "Grain Tall," pain combining with "Wheat in Bloom."
translations.idiomatic: On top of that came fire from heaven and from men. Palaces and offices burned again and again until not a rafter remained—grief like Grain Tall, sorrow doubled like Wheat in Bloom.

sentences.zh: 遂使億兆離心，疆徼侵弱，斯人何辜，離此塗炭！

translations.literal: Thus millions lost heart, borders and marches grew weak—what crime did these people commit, that they should leave this scorched earth?
translations.idiomatic: Millions lost faith; the frontiers weakened. What had these people done to deserve such ruin?

sentences.zh: 今明昏遞運，大道公行，思治之氓，來蘇茲日。

translations.literal: Now bright replaces dark and the great Way goes forth openly; people who long for order return to life on this day.
translations.idiomatic: Now light follows darkness and the great Way is open again. People who hunger for peace may breathe free today.

sentences.zh: 猥以寡薄，屬當大寵，雖運距中興，艱同草昧，思闡皇休，與之更始。

translations.literal: I, unworthy and thin in virtue, happen to bear the great favor; though fate blocks full restoration and hardship matches the wild beginning, I mean to extend imperial blessing and begin anew with them.
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy and weak in virtue, yet have been given this great charge. Though fortune still blocks full revival and hardship matches the founding days, I will spread imperial grace and start anew with the people.

sentences.zh: 凡昏制、謬賦、淫刑、濫役，外可詳檢前源，悉皆除蕩。

translations.literal: All benighted institutions, mistaken levies, licentious punishments, and abusive corvée—outside these halls let a detailed review of their origins be made, and all be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Every dark law, mistaken tax, cruel punishment, and abusive levy—let the ministries trace each to its source and abolish them all.

sentences.zh: 其主守散失，諸所損耗，精立科條，咸從原例。」

translations.literal: Where prefects and defenders let things scatter and all kinds of losses occurred, let strict statutes be set and all be restored to former rules.
translations.idiomatic: Where local officials allowed losses and disorder, let clear rules be drawn up and all be made good under the old standards."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「永元之季，乾維落紐。

translations.literal: He also said: "In the last years of Yongyuan, the heavenly axis lost its knot.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "In the closing years of Yongyuan the axis of Heaven slipped its knot.

sentences.zh: 政實多門，有殊衛文之代；

translations.literal: Government indeed had many doors—as in Duke Wen of Wey's time;
translations.idiomatic: Government had too many masters, as in Duke Wen of Wei's day;

sentences.zh: 權移於下，事等曹恭之時。

translations.literal: authority shifted downward—events equaled Cao Gong's day.
translations.idiomatic: power sank to the bottom, as in the time of Cao Gong.

sentences.zh: 遂使閹尹有翁媼之稱，高安有法堯之旨。

translations.literal: Eunuch chamberlains acquired the titles of old man and old woman; Gao'an held the edict of Fa Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs were called Old Father and Old Mother; Gao'an carried the decree of Fa Yao.

sentences.zh: 鬻獄販官，錮山護澤，開塞之機，奏成小醜。

translations.literal: Selling verdicts and peddling offices, monopolizing mountains and guarding marshes—the keys of access were turned by petty villains.
translations.idiomatic: Justice was for sale, offices were traded, mountains and marshes were fenced off for private gain—the gates of power were worked by petty men.

sentences.zh: 直道正義，擁抑彌年，懷冤抱理，莫知誰訴。

translations.literal: The straight path and right justice were suppressed year on year; those nursing wrongs and holding reason knew not whom to appeal to.
translations.idiomatic: Honest men and just causes were crushed year after year. Those with grievances did not know where to turn.

sentences.zh: 姦吏因之，筆削自己。

translations.literal: Corrupt clerks seized on this, wielding brush and knife as they pleased."
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt clerks seized the chance and wrote the record—and the sentence—as they pleased."

sentences.zh: 豈直賈生流涕，許伯哭時而已哉！

translations.literal: How is it only Jia Yi weeping tears, or Xu Bo wailing at the appointed hour!
translations.idiomatic: This is not merely Jia Yi weeping for the realm, or Xu Bo's funeral lament—it goes far deeper!

sentences.zh: 今理運惟新，政刑得所，矯革流弊，實在茲日。

translations.literal: Now the principle of order is newly renewed, government and punishments are properly placed; to rectify and reform lingering abuses—truly this is the day.
translations.idiomatic: Now governance begins anew, law and punishment are right again, and the moment to uproot old abuses has come.

sentences.zh: 可通檢尚書衆曹，東昏時諸諍訟失理及主者淹停不時施行者，精加訊辨，依事議奏。」

translations.literal: Let all bureaus of the Secretariat be thoroughly inspected; for all unjust lawsuits during Dong Hun's time and cases where responsible officials delayed implementation without timely action, conduct careful inquiry and judgment, and memorial according to the facts."
translations.idiomatic: "Inspect every Secretariat bureau. For wrongful suits from Dong Hun's reign and officials who sat on cases without acting, investigate carefully and report findings for decision."

sentences.zh: 又下令，以義師臨陣致命及疾病死亡者，並加葬斂，收恤遺孤。

translations.literal: Another order: for righteous-army men who died in battle and those who died of illness, all were to receive burial at state expense and their orphaned survivors were to be cared for.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered that righteous troops killed in battle or dead of sickness receive proper burial, with their orphans taken in and cared for.

sentences.zh: 又令曰：「朱爵之捷，逆徒送死者，特許家人殯葬；

translations.literal: Another edict read: "At the victory at Zhujue, for rebel dead who were sent forth—families are specially permitted funeral burial;
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said: "After the victory at Red Sparrow, the dead among the rebels may be claimed by their families for burial;

sentences.zh: 若無親屬，或有貧苦，二縣長尉卽爲埋掩。

translations.literal: if there are no kin, or they are poor and destitute, the chief and assistant of the two counties shall immediately bury them.
translations.idiomatic: where there is no kin, or kin are too poor, the magistrates of both counties shall bury them at once.

sentences.zh: 建康城內，不達天命，自取淪滅，亦同此科。」

translations.literal: Within Jiankang city, those who did not grasp Heaven's mandate and brought ruin upon themselves—shall be treated under the same rule."
translations.idiomatic: Within Jiankang, those who defied Heaven's decree and brought destruction on themselves fall under the same provision."

sentences.zh: 二年正月，天子遣兼侍中席闡文、兼黃門侍郎樂法才慰勞京邑。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, the Son of Heaven sent Acting Attendant-in-Ordinary Xi Chuanwen and Acting Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yue Facai to comfort and reassure the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year two, the Emperor sent Xi Chuanwen and Yue Facai to console the capital.

sentences.zh: 追贈高祖祖散騎常侍左光祿大夫，考侍中丞相。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed Gaozu's grandfather as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Grand Master for Brightness; his father as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's grandfather was posthumously made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Grand Master for Brightness; his father, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 高祖下令曰：「夫在上化下，草偃風從，世之澆淳，恒由此作。

translations.literal: Gaozu issued an order: "He above transforms those below—the grass bends, the wind follows; whether an age runs thin or pure is always shaped from this.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu ordered: "Those who rule set the tone for all below—grass bends where the wind blows, and an age's corruption or virtue begins here.

sentences.zh: 自永元失德，書契未紀，窮凶極悖，焉可勝言。

translations.literal: From Yongyuan's loss of virtue, records went unkept—utter villainy and extreme perversity, how could words encompass it?
translations.idiomatic: Since Yongyuan, virtue collapsed and records could scarcely keep pace—the cruelty and perversity beggar description.

sentences.zh: 旣而琁室外構，傾宮內積，奇技異服，殫所未見。

translations.literal: Then the Xuan Chamber was built outside, palace treasures piled high, strange crafts and outlandish dress—exhausting what had never been seen.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces rose without end, inner treasuries overflowed, and bizarre arts and fashions appeared that none had ever seen.

sentences.zh: 上慢下暴，淫侈競馳。

translations.literal: Superiors were arrogant, inferiors violent; debauchery and extravagance raced one another.
translations.idiomatic: The high grew contemptuous, the low turned brutal, and debauchery and excess raced unchecked.

sentences.zh: 國命朝權，盡移近習。

translations.literal: The nation's mandate and court power were wholly shifted to intimate favorites.
translations.idiomatic: State affairs and court authority fell entirely into the hands of cronies.

sentences.zh: 販官鬻爵，賄貨公行。

translations.literal: Offices were sold, ranks traded for cash; bribes walked openly in public.
translations.idiomatic: Offices and ranks went up for sale, and graft flourished in the open.

sentences.zh: 並甲第康衢，漸臺廣室。

translations.literal: Together with mansions on grand avenues, tiered terraces and vast halls.
translations.idiomatic: Grand estates lined the main roads; tiered towers and sprawling halls multiplied.

sentences.zh: 長袖低昂，等和戎之賜；

translations.literal: Long sleeves swaying up and down, equal to the gifts of pacifying barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: Swishing sleeves like the gifts lavished on pacifying barbarians;

sentences.zh: 珍羞百品，同伐冰之家。

translations.literal: delicacies of a hundred kinds, like households that break ice for luxury.
translations.idiomatic: delicacies by the hundred, fit for households rich enough to cut ice in winter.

sentences.zh: 愚民因之，浸以成俗。

translations.literal: Simple folk followed suit; soaked through, it became custom.
translations.idiomatic: Common people took it up, and by degrees it hardened into custom.

sentences.zh: 驕豔競爽，夸麗相高。

translations.literal: Proud beauty vied in brilliance; boastful splendor outdid one another.
translations.idiomatic: Ostentation and glamour competed; each tried to outshine the next.

sentences.zh: 至乃市井之家，貂狐在御；

translations.literal: So far that market-stall households kept sable and fox in daily use;
translations.idiomatic: Even market families wore sable and fox fur;

sentences.zh: 工商之子，緹繡是襲。

translations.literal: sons of artisans and merchants robed themselves in brocade and embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: merchants' and craftsmen's sons dressed in brocade and silk.

sentences.zh: 日入之次，夜分未反，昧爽之朝，期之清旦。

translations.literal: At sunset's turn they had not yet returned; at night's middle still abroad—at dawn's grey they looked for clear morning.
translations.idiomatic: They did not come home at dusk, nor by midnight; at grey dawn they still waited for morning light.

sentences.zh: 聖明肇運，厲精惟始，雖曰纘戎，殆同創革。

translations.literal: Sage brilliance inaugurated the age; keen resolve at the very start—though called succession to arms, it is nearly the same as founding anew.
translations.idiomatic: A sage ruler opens a new age and sharpens himself from the first day; though this is formally succession, it is almost a new founding.

sentences.zh: 且淫費之後，繼以興師，巨橋、鹿臺，凋罄不一。

translations.literal: Moreover after debauched spending came raising armies—Juqiao and Lutai, depletion not of one kind alone.
translations.idiomatic: After wasteful excess came war—like Juqiao's granaries and Lutai's treasuries emptied without end.

sentences.zh: 孤忝荷大寵，務在澄清，思所以仰述皇朝大帛之旨，俯厲微躬鹿裘之義，解而更張，斵雕爲樸。

translations.literal: I unworthily bear great favor; my task is to clarify—to think how to uphold the imperial court's intent of great plain silk above, and below to toughen this humble person with the meaning of a deer-fur robe—loosen and restring, carve away ornament to plainness.
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy of this great charge, yet my duty is to set things right—to honor the court's spirit of plain great silk, and in my own life the lesson of the deer-fur coat: loosen what binds, restring the bow, strip ornament back to simplicity.

sentences.zh: 自非可以奉粢盛，脩紱冕，習禮樂之容，繕甲兵之備，此外衆費，一皆禁絕。

translations.literal: Save what serves to offer sacrificial grain, repair insignia and coronets, practice ritual and music's forms, and maintain arms and armor—in all other collective expense, each item is forbidden and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from what serves sacrifice, ritual vestments, music and ceremony, or arming the troops, every other extravagance is abolished.

sentences.zh: 御府中署，量宜罷省。

translations.literal: The imperial storehouses and inner offices—abolish or reduce as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial warehouses and inner departments shall be cut back as fit.

sentences.zh: 掖庭備禦妾之數，大予絕鄭衛之音。

translations.literal: The Rear Palace shall reduce the number of imperial concubines; the Grand Music Director shall cut off Zheng and Wei music.
translations.idiomatic: The palace will limit concubines; court music will ban licentious Zheng and Wei tunes.

sentences.zh: 其中有可以率先卿士，准的甿庶，菲食薄衣，請自孤始。

translations.literal: Among these, where one can lead ministers and scholars by example, set the mark for the common people—plain food and thin dress—let it begin with me.
translations.idiomatic: Where I can lead officials and set an example for the people—simple fare and plain clothes—let it start with me.

sentences.zh: 加羣才並軌，九官咸事，若能人務退食，競存約己，移風易俗，庶朞月有成。

translations.literal: Moreover with many talents walking in one track, and the nine officers all at their tasks—if men can devote themselves to retiring after meals, competing to keep restraint upon themselves, shifting wind and changing custom—perhaps in a month there will be achievement.
translations.idiomatic: With able men in post and every office working, if each guards against excess and holds himself to restraint, custom may turn within a month.

sentences.zh: 昔毛玠在朝，士大夫不敢靡衣偷食。

translations.literal: Formerly when Mao Jie was at court, scholars and officials dared not wear wasteful dress or eat beyond their due.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mao Jie served at court, officials dared not dress beyond their rank or eat beyond their share.

sentences.zh: 魏武歎曰：『孤之法不如毛尚書。

translations.literal: Cao Cao sighed: "My laws are not the equal of Minister Mao's.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao once sighed, "My rules fall short of Minister Mao's.

sentences.zh: 』孤雖德謝往賢，任重先達，實望多士得其此心。

translations.literal: " Though my virtue falls short of past worthies and my burden is great before those who came first, I truly hope many officers will grasp this intent.
translations.idiomatic: " My own virtue cannot match the ancients and the burden is heavy, but I hope the realm's officers will share this resolve.

sentences.zh: 外可詳爲條格。」

translations.literal: Externally, detailed regulations may be drawn up."
translations.idiomatic: "Let detailed rules be issued for all to follow."

sentences.zh: 戊戌，宣德皇后臨朝，入居內殿。

translations.literal: On day wuxu, Empress Xuan of Virtue held court, entering and dwelling in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: On day wuxu, Empress Dowager Xuan took the regency from the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 拜帝大司馬，解承制，百僚致敬如前。

translations.literal: The Emperor was appointed Grand Marshal; the provisional-regime authority was released; the hundred officials paid homage as before.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was confirmed as Grand Marshal, his provisional powers ended, and officials paid homage as before.

sentences.zh: 詔進高祖都督中外諸軍事，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名。

translations.literal: An edict advanced Gaozu to commander of all military affairs within and without, granted sword and shoes in the hall, no need to hurry entering court, and no personal name in ceremonial address.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was made supreme commander of all armies, with sword and shoes permitted in the throne room, no haste in court, and address without his personal name.

sentences.zh: 加前後部羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: Added front and rear guard of feather-canopies and drum-and-pipe music.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted imperial escort with canopy and martial music, front and rear.

sentences.zh: 置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎、掾、屬各四人，並依舊辟士，餘並如故。

translations.literal: Left and Right Chief Clerks, Marshals, Attendant Gentlemen, aides, and clerks were each set at four, all recruiting scholars as of old; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Four each were appointed as Left and Right Chief Clerks, Marshals, Attendant Gentlemen, aides, and clerks, recruited as before; other offices unchanged.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict read:
translations.idiomatic: The edict said:

sentences.zh: 夫日月麗天，高明所以表德；

translations.literal: Sun and moon adorn the sky—height and brightness therefore manifest virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon crown the sky, and by their height and light virtue is shown;

sentences.zh: 山岳題地，柔博所以成功。

translations.literal: mountains and peaks mark the earth—gentleness and breadth therefore accomplish achievement.
translations.idiomatic: mountains stand upon the earth, and through their breadth and steadfastness deeds are done.

sentences.zh: 故能庶物出而資始，河海振而不洩。

translations.literal: Thus the myriad things emerge and draw their beginning from them; rivers and seas surge yet do not spill over.
translations.idiomatic: From this the ten thousand things arise and take their start; rivers and seas heave yet do not burst their bounds.

sentences.zh: 二象貞觀，代之者人。

translations.literal: The two signs are constantly observed; human beings stand in their place.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth hold their course, and humanity stands as their heir.

sentences.zh: 是以七輔、四叔，致無爲於軒、昊；

translations.literal: Hence the Seven Assistants and Four Uncles brought non-action to Xuanyuan and Haohao;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Seven Assists and Four Uncles brought effortless rule to the Yellow Emperor and Emperor Yao;

sentences.zh: 韋、彭、齊、晉，靖衰亂於殷、周。

translations.literal: Wei, Peng, Qi, and Jin quieted decline and disorder in Yin and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, Peng, Qi, and Jin stilled chaos in the Yin and Zhou dynasties.

sentences.zh: 大司馬攸縱自天，體茲齊聖，文洽九功，武苞七德。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal You was unbridled from Heaven, embodying such complete sageliness—literary accomplishment harmonizing the Nine Achievements, military virtue embracing the Seven Moral Powers.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal You was heaven-sent in gifts, wholly sage in nature—literary virtue completing the Nine Works, martial virtue holding the Seven Powers.

sentences.zh: 欽惟厥始，徽猷早樹，誠著艱難，功參帷幙。

translations.literal: Reverently considering his beginning, fine policies were planted early; sincerity showed in hardship, achievement shared the command tent.
translations.idiomatic: From the first his fine counsel took root; his loyalty proved in hardship and his merit was won within the command tent.

sentences.zh: 錫賦開壤，式表厥庸。

translations.literal: Gifts of tax lands were granted to open his fief, thus displaying his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Tax lands were granted to mark his worth.

sentences.zh: 建武升歷，邊隙屢啓，公釋書輟講，經營四方。

translations.literal: When Jianwu began its reign, border gaps opened repeatedly; the Duke set aside books and ceased lectures, managing the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jianwu era opened, the frontiers flared again; the Duke laid aside his books and took up the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 司、豫懸切，樊、漢危殆，覆強寇於沔濱，僵胡馬於鄧汭。

translations.literal: Si and Yu hung in peril, Fan and Han in deadly danger—overturning fierce enemies on the Mian's banks, stiffening barbarian horses at Deng's mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Si and Yu teetered, Fan and Han were near ruin—he crushed strong foes on the Han River and froze the barbarian cavalry at Deng's ford.

sentences.zh: 永元肇號，難結羣醜，專威擅虐，毒被含靈，溥天惴惴，命懸晷刻。

translations.literal: Yongyuan first took its name; troubles knotted the vile band—monopolizing power, arbitrary in cruelty, poison reaching all living souls; all under Heaven trembled, life hanging by the sundial's moments.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongyuan began, villains gathered power, cruel and unchecked, poison spread to every living soul, all Heaven trembled, and men's lives hung by moments.

sentences.zh: 否終有期，神謨載挺，首建大策，惟新鼎祚。

translations.literal: When evil ends there is a term; divine counsel arose in support—first establishing the great strategy, renewing the tripod throne.
translations.idiomatic: Darkness at last had its limit; heaven's counsel rose with him—first to frame the great plan and renew the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 投袂勤王，沿流電舉，魯城雲撤，夏汭霧披，加湖羣盜，一鼓殄拔，姑孰連旍，倏焉冰泮。

translations.literal: He flung his sleeves to aid the king, sped along the current like lightning—Luzhou's walls dispersed like clouds, Xia's mouth cleared like mist parting; at Jiahu the bandits, one drumstroke exterminated; at Gushu the linked banners, in a flash melted like ice.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied to rescue the throne, racing downstream like lightning—Luzhou fell like clouds scattering, Xia's mouth cleared like lifted fog; at Jiahu the bandits were crushed in one assault, at Gushu their banners melted like ice in spring.

sentences.zh: 取新壘其如拾芥，撲朱爵其猶掃塵。

translations.literal: Taking Xinyu fortress was like picking up a mustard seed; storming Zhujue was still like sweeping dust.
translations.idiomatic: Xinyu fell as easily as lifting a mustard seed; Zhujue was seized as lightly as sweeping dust.

sentences.zh: 霆電外駭，省闥內傾，餘醜纖蠹，蚳蝝必盡。

translations.literal: Thunder and lightning struck outward in alarm; the palace gates inward collapsed—the remaining villains, fine worms, ant larvae all to be utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder struck outward in terror, the palace swayed within, and every remnant vermin was stamped out to the last.

sentences.zh: 援彼已溺，解此倒懸，塗歡裏抃，自近及遠。

translations.literal: Saving those already drowning, releasing those upside-down suspended—joy on the roads, clapping in the lanes, from near reaching far.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled the drowning from the water and cut the bound free from the beam—roads rang with joy and lanes with clapping, from the capital outward.

sentences.zh: 畿甸夷穆，方外肅寧，解茲虐網，被以寬政。

translations.literal: The capital region was mild and tranquil, the outer lands solemn and peaceful—this cruel net was released, covered with lenient government.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland grew calm, the frontiers quiet; the tyrant's snares were cut and gentler rule spread.

sentences.zh: 積弊窮昏，一朝載廓，聲教遐漸，無思不被。

translations.literal: Accumulated abuses of exhausted darkness—in one morning broadly cleared; voice and teaching reached far in gradual spread, no thought unreached.
translations.idiomatic: Ages of rot were cleared in a single day; his voice and teaching reached far, and no heart was left untouched.

sentences.zh: 雖伊尹之執茲壹德，姬旦之光于四海，方斯蔑如也。

translations.literal: Though Yi Yin's holding to this single virtue, and the Duke of Zhou's light upon the four seas—compared with this, how could they not be dismissed as nothing?
translations.idiomatic: Even Yi Yin's single-minded virtue and the Duke of Zhou's light over the four seas pale beside this.

sentences.zh: 昔呂望翼佐聖君，猶享四履之命；

translations.literal: Formerly Lü Wang aided and assisted the sage ruler, yet still enjoyed the command of four domains;
translations.idiomatic: Once Lü Wang served the sage king, he still received command over four regions;

sentences.zh: 文侯立功平后，尚荷二弓之錫，況於盛德元勳，超邁自古。

translations.literal: Marquis Wen achieved merit in pacifying the empress, yet still bore the gift of two bows—how much more for overflowing virtue and founding merit, surpassing the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Wen earned merit pacifying the realm yet still received two bows as reward—how much more for virtue and achievement that outstrip all former ages.

sentences.zh: 黔首惵惵，待以爲命，救其已然，拯其方斮，式閭表墓，未或能比；

translations.literal: The black-haired people trembled, waiting on him as their life; saving what was already done, rescuing what was about to be severed, marking gates and tombs with honor—none could compare;
translations.idiomatic: The people looked to him for life itself—rescuing the doomed, saving what was already lost, honoring the worthy at gate and grave—none could match this;

sentences.zh: 而大輅渠門，輟而莫授，眷言前訓，無忘終食。

translations.literal: yet the great chariot and raised gate were paused and not granted; mindful of former instruction, not forgetting even at the final meal.
translations.idiomatic: yet the highest honors were held back; remembering ancient precedent, he did not forget even over a single meal.

sentences.zh: 便宜敬升大典，式允羣望。

translations.literal: It is fitting respectfully to ascend the great ceremony, truly fulfilling the multitude's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: It is right to raise him to the supreme rite and satisfy the people's longing.

sentences.zh: 其進位相國，總百揆，揚州刺史；

translations.literal: Let him advance to Chancellor, overseeing the hundred affairs, and Governor of Yangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: He shall be promoted to Chancellor, head of all government, and Governor of Yangzhou;

sentences.zh: 封十郡爲梁公，備九錫之禮，加璽紱遠遊冠，位在諸王上，加相國綠綟綬。

translations.literal: enfeoff ten commanderies as Duke of Liang, complete with the Nine Bestowments rites, add seal-ribbon and the Far-Wandering cap, rank above all princes, and add the Chancellor's green-and-yellow cord.
translations.idiomatic: granted ten commanderies as Duke of Liang with full Nine Bestowments, the seal-ribbon and Far-Wandering cap, rank above all princes, and the Chancellor's green-and-yellow sash.

sentences.zh: 其驃騎大將軍如故。

translations.literal: His General of Agile Cavalry remains as before.
translations.idiomatic: He retains his post as General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 依舊置梁百司。

translations.literal: Establish the Liang bureaus as of old.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang administrative offices shall be set up as before.

sentences.zh: 策曰：

translations.literal: The investiture decree read:
translations.idiomatic: The formal decree said:

sentences.zh: 二儀寂寞，由寒暑而代行，三才並用，資立人以爲寶，故能流形品物，仰代天工。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth stand in silence, yin and yang passing in turn through cold and heat; the three powers jointly employed, relying on humanity established as treasure—thus able to give form to the myriad things, upholding Heaven's work in their place.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth endure in stillness, seasons turning through cold and heat; the three realms work together, and humanity is their treasure—shaping the ten thousand things and standing in for Heaven's craft.

sentences.zh: 允茲元輔，應期挺秀，裁成天地之功，幽協神明之德。

translations.literal: Truly this chief minister, responding to the age and standing forth in excellence, completing Heaven and earth's achievement, secretly harmonizing with the divine spirits' virtue.
translations.idiomatic: This chief minister rose to meet the age, completing heaven and earth's work and moving in secret accord with the gods.

sentences.zh: 撥亂反正，濟世寧民，盛烈光於有道，大勳振於無外，雖伊陟之保乂王家，姬公之有此丕訓，方之蔑如也。

translations.literal: Setting chaos aright and restoring order, saving the age and settling the people—glorious deeds shining upon the realm of the Way, great merit shaking the lands beyond, though Yi Zhi's safeguarding of the royal house and the Duke of Zhou's possession of this great instruction—compared with this, how could they not be dismissed as nothing?
translations.idiomatic: He set chaos right, saved the age, and settled the people—glory for the realm, renown beyond the borders; even Yi Zhi guarding the royal house and the Duke of Zhou's great teaching pale beside him.

sentences.zh: 今將授公典策，其敬聽朕命：

translations.literal: Now I shall confer upon the Duke the canonical decree—reverently hear my command:
translations.idiomatic: Now I invest the Duke with the formal decree—hear and obey:

sentences.zh: 上天不造，難鐘皇室，世祖以休明早崩，世宗以仁德不嗣，高宗襲統，宸居弗永，雖夙夜劬勞，而隆平不洽。

translations.literal: Heaven did not preserve; disaster struck the imperial house—the Founding Emperor with early brilliance perished young, the Heir Emperor with benevolent virtue left no successor, the High Emperor inherited the line yet the throne was not long held; though toiling day and night, flourishing peace was not achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven withheld its favor; calamity fell on the royal house—the Founding Emperor died young in his brilliance, the Heir Emperor left no son of virtue, the High Emperor took the throne but did not long hold it; though he labored day and night, lasting peace never came.

sentences.zh: 嗣君昏暴，書契弗睹。

translations.literal: The succeeding ruler was benighted and violent, records unseen.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was brutal and blind, beyond what records can tell.

sentences.zh: 朝權國柄，委之羣㜸。

translations.literal: Court power and the nation's handle were entrusted to a clique of women.
translations.idiomatic: Court authority and the nation's reins passed into the hands of a faction of women.

sentences.zh: 剿戮忠賢，誅殘台輔，含冤抱痛，噍類靡餘。

translations.literal: They slaughtered the loyal and worthy, destroyed the terrace ministers; bearing wrongs and clutching pain, not a mouthful of kind left.
translations.idiomatic: They butchered loyal men and killed high ministers; the wronged and grieving were wiped out to the last mouth.

sentences.zh: 實繁非一，並專國命。

translations.literal: Truly many and not one—all monopolizing the nation's command.
translations.idiomatic: Many were they, and not one alone—all seized the nation's power.

sentences.zh: 嚬笑致災，睚眦及禍。

translations.literal: A frown or smile brought disaster; the slightest grudge reached ruin.
translations.idiomatic: A smile or frown brought calamity; the smallest slight brought destruction.

sentences.zh: 嚴科毒賦，載離比屋，溥天熬熬，置身無所。

translations.literal: Harsh law and poisonous taxation left house after house; all under Heaven burned, nowhere to set one's body.
translations.idiomatic: Cruel law and crushing taxes emptied every household; all Heaven scorched, and men had nowhere to stand.

sentences.zh: 冤頸引決，道樹相望，無近無遠，號天靡告。

translations.literal: Necks wronged, they took their own lives; trees by the road stood in rows of the dead—near or far, crying to Heaven with none to hear.
translations.idiomatic: The wronged cut their own throats; corpses hung from roadside trees near and far, crying to Heaven with no one to answer.

sentences.zh: 公藉昏明之期，因兆民之願，援帥羣后，翊成中興。

translations.literal: The Duke, relying on the term of darkness and brightness, following the hundred thousand people's wish, leading the host of lords, assisted in completing the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke seized the turning of dark to light, answered the people's prayer, rallied the lords, and helped restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 宗社之危已固，天人之望允塞，此實公紐我絕綱，大造皇家者也。

translations.literal: The altars' peril was already firm, Heaven and humanity's hope truly fulfilled—this truly is the Duke tying up our broken net, greatly creating the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: The altars were saved, Heaven and earth's wish fulfilled—this is the Duke who mended our broken bonds and remade the royal house.

sentences.zh: 永明季年，邊隙大啓，荊河連率，招引戎荒，江、淮擾逼，勢同履虎。

translations.literal: In the late Yongming years, border gaps opened wide; the Jing and He regional commanders invited in barbarians from the wilds—Jiang and Huai were disturbed and pressed, the situation like treading a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yongming the frontiers burst open; commanders of Jing and He invited barbarians in—Jiang and Huai shook under threat, as if walking on a tiger's back.

sentences.zh: 公受言本朝，輕兵赴襲，縻以長算，制之環中。

translations.literal: The Duke received orders from the court, led light troops in swift attack, restrained them with long calculation, controlled them within the circle.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered by the court, he led light forces in a swift strike, held them with long strategy, and contained them within his grasp.

sentences.zh: 排危冒險，強柔遞用，坦然一方，還成籓服。

translations.literal: Braving danger and braving peril, strong and soft used in turn—one region stood tranquil, again becoming a frontier domain.
translations.idiomatic: He braved every danger, shifting between force and forbearance—one region grew calm and again bowed as a vassal frontier.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 在昔隆昌，洪基已謝，高宗慮深社稷，將行權道。

translations.literal: In former Longchang, the great foundation was already spent; the High Emperor deeply considered the altars and was about to employ expedient means.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang the dynasty's base was already spent; the High Emperor, fearing for the altars, prepared to act by necessity.

sentences.zh: 公定策帷帳，激揚大節，廢帝立王，謀猷深著。

translations.literal: The Duke fixed strategy within the command tent, rousing great integrity, deposing the emperor and establishing the king—counsel deeply manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke decided policy in the tent, upheld great principle, deposed one emperor and raised another—his counsel shone clear.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 建武闡業，厥猷雖遠，戎狄內侵，憑陵關塞，司部危逼，淪陷指期。

translations.literal: Jianwu opened its enterprise; though its plans were far-reaching, barbarians invaded within, leaning on passes and barriers—Si Province hung in peril, fall imminent within days.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu began its rule with far-reaching plans, yet barbarians invaded the passes—Si Province teetered on the brink of fall.

sentences.zh: 公治兵外討，卷甲長騖，接距交綏，電激風掃，摧堅覆銳，咽水塗原，執俘象魏，獻馘海渚，焚廬毀帳，號哭言歸。

translations.literal: The Duke ordered troops for external campaign, rolled armor and rode far, met the foe and joined battle—lightning strike, wind sweep, crushing the hard and overturning the sharp, water choked and plains stained; captives taken at the Elephant Gate, severed ears offered at the sea's edge, huts burned and tents destroyed, wailing as they spoke of return.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke marched out to war, armor rolled and horses driven far—he met the enemy, struck like lightning, swept like wind, broke the strong and crushed the sharp, choked streams and stained the plains; he took prisoners at the Elephant Gate, offered severed ears at the sea's edge, burned camps and destroyed tents, and the foe wailed homeward.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 樊、漢阽切，羽書續至。

translations.literal: Fan and Han hung on the brink; urgent dispatches came in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and Han stood on the edge of ruin; urgent reports arrived one after another.

sentences.zh: 公星言鞠旅，稟命徂征，而軍機戎統，事非己出，善策嘉謀，抑而莫允。

translations.literal: The Duke at star-rise marshaled troops, received orders and marched forth—yet military plans and campaign command were matters not of his own issuing; fine strategies and excellent counsel were suppressed and not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke mustered his army at dawn and marched on orders—yet strategy and command were not his to decide; good counsel was offered and refused.

sentences.zh: 鄧城之役，胡馬卒至，元帥潛及，不相告報，棄甲捐師，餌之虎口。

translations.literal: At the battle of Dengcheng, barbarian horses suddenly arrived; the commander secretly reached the field and gave no report—armor cast off, troops abandoned, fed to the tiger's mouth.
translations.idiomatic: At Dengcheng barbarian cavalry struck without warning; the commander slipped in unseen and gave no word—armor was cast aside, troops abandoned, and men fed to the tiger's maw.

sentences.zh: 公南收散卒，北禦雕騎，全衆方軌，案路徐歸，拯我邊危，重獲安堵。

translations.literal: The Duke southward gathered scattered soldiers, northward resisted the carved cavalry—preserving the host in ordered ranks, tracing the road and returning slowly, saving our border peril, again obtaining peace and security.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke gathered the scattered in the south and held the barbarian horse in the north—kept the army intact, withdrew in good order, saved the frontier, and restored peace.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 漢南迥弱，咫尺勍寇，兵糧蓋闕，器甲靡遺。

translations.literal: South of the Han was weak and far; powerful enemies stood within a hand's reach—military grain was likely spent, weapons and armor all but gone.
translations.idiomatic: The lands south of the Han had grown feeble and remote, yet fierce enemies pressed within arm's reach—grain for the armies was nearly gone, arms and armor nearly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 公作籓爰始，因資靡託，整兵訓卒，蒐狩有序，俾我危城，飜爲強鎮。

translations.literal: When the Duke first took up his fief, though resources could not be relied upon, he drilled soldiers and ordered hunts in due season—our perilous city was turned into a strong fortress.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke first went out to his fief, though he had little to lean on, he trained troops and kept hunts in order—what had been a city in peril became a stronghold.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 永元紀號，瞻烏已及，雖廢昏有典，而伊、霍稱難。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era title the crow-fearing omen had already come—though there was precedent for deposing a worthless ruler, even Yi Yin and Huo Guang found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yongyuan reign the omen of the perched crow had arrived—though deposing a worthless ruler had precedent, even Yi Yin and Huo Guang had called it hard.

sentences.zh: 公首建大策，爰立明聖，義逾邑綸，勳高代入，易亂以化，俾昏作明。

translations.literal: The Duke first framed the great policy and established the enlightened sage—righteousness beyond the hemp tally, merit surpassing the replacement of one ruler, changing disorder into order and making the blind see clear.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke was first to set the great design and raise the enlightened sovereign—his righteousness exceeded the hemp tally of enfeoffment, his merit outshone a change of dynasties; he turned chaos to order and darkness to light.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 文王之風，雖被江、漢，京邑蠢動，湮爲洪流，句吳、於越，巢幕匪喻。

translations.literal: Though King Wen's transforming wind reached the Yangtze and Han, the capital stirred and was swallowed in a flood tide—Wu and Yue were like birds in a nest over a burning curtain, beyond all comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Though the civilizing wind of King Wen had reached the Yangtze and Han, the capital seethed and sank under a rising flood—Wu and Yue were birds nesting above a burning curtain, a peril beyond words.

sentences.zh: 公投袂萬里，事惟拯溺，義聲所覃，無思不韙。

translations.literal: The Duke set out ten thousand li with sleeve thrust aside, intent only on saving the drowning—where his righteous renown reached, none failed to approve.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke flung aside his sleeve and marched ten thousand li, thinking only of those drowning in peril—wherever his righteous name reached, none withheld approval.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 魯城、夏汭，梗據中流，乘山置壘，縈川自固。

translations.literal: Lucheng and Xia Rui blocked the midstream, building ramparts on mountains and entrenching along rivers for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Lucheng and Xia Rui held the river's heart, piling ramparts on the hills and winding defenses along the streams.

sentences.zh: 公御此烏集，陵茲地險，頓兵坐甲，寒往暑移，我行永久，士忘歸願，經以遠圖，御以長策，費無遺矢，戰未窮兵，踐華之固，相望俱拔。

translations.literal: The Duke faced these gathered crows, crossed this treacherous terrain, halted troops in armor through cold and heat—our march was long and soldiers forgot return; with far-reaching strategy and enduring policy, not an arrow wasted and battle never pushed to exhaustion—the fortified positions at Jianhua were taken one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke met this flock of crows, crossed perilous ground, and held his army in armor through winter into summer—our campaign ran long and the men forgot home; with distant design and patient strategy he spent no arrow in vain and never drove war to its limit—the strongholds of Jianhua fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 惟此羣凶，同惡相濟，緣江負險，蟻聚加湖。

translations.literal: These villains aided one another's evil, clinging to river hazards and swarming at Jia Lake like ants.
translations.idiomatic: These criminals helped one another in wickedness, hugging the river's defenses and massing at Jia Lake like ants.

sentences.zh: 水陸盤據，規援夏首，桴鳷一臨，應時褫潰。

translations.literal: They held land and water, planning to reinforce Xia Shou—with one approach of the fleet they collapsed at once.
translations.idiomatic: They occupied land and water alike, scheming to relieve Xia Shou—but at the first arrival of our fleet they crumbled on the spot.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 姦㜸震皇，復懷舉斧，蓄兵九派，用擬勤王。

translations.literal: The treacherous minister shook the throne, again harbored axe-raising intent, and massed troops at the nine branches of the Yangtze to muster for loyal rescue of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: A treacherous minister alarmed the throne, again nursed rebellion, and gathered armies at the Yangtze's nine mouths under the banner of saving the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 公棱威直指，勢踰風電，旌旆小臨，全州稽服。

translations.literal: The Duke's stern prestige pointed straight—momentum surpassing wind and lightning; at the slightest arrival of banners and flags the whole province submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke's aweful authority drove straight ahead, swifter than wind or lightning—at the least touch of his banners and flags, the whole province bowed.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 姑孰沖要，密邇京畿，凶徒熾聚，斷塞津路。

translations.literal: Gushu was strategically vital and close to the capital—a nest of villains blocked the ferry routes.
translations.idiomatic: Gushu was a vital crossing near the capital, where fierce rebels massed and cut the ferry roads.

sentences.zh: 公偏師啓塗，排方繼及，兵威所震，望旗自駭，焚舟委壁，卷甲宵遁。

translations.literal: The Duke's detached force opened the road, columns following in succession—where military prestige fell, flags alone made them tremble; they burned boats, abandoned walls, rolled armor and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke sent a flanking force to clear the way, columns pressing after in turn—where his army's might struck, men quailed at the sight of his flags; they burned their boats, abandoned their walls, and fled by night in rolled armor.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 羣豎倡狂，志在借一，豕突淮涘，武騎如雲。

translations.literal: The mob ran wild, intent on one last gamble—boars charging the Huai shore, martial cavalry cloud-thick.
translations.idiomatic: The rabble raged, staking everything on one throw—charging the Huai like wild boars, war-horses massed like clouds.

sentences.zh: 公爰命英勇，因機騁銳，氣冠版泉，勢逾洹水，追奔逐北，奄有通津，熊耳比峻，未足云擬，睢水不流，曷其能及。

translations.literal: The Duke summoned the brave, seized the moment and unleashed sharp forces—spirit surpassing Banquan, momentum exceeding the Huan River; pursuing routed foes northward he seized the vital crossings—Bear-Ear Peaks' steepness cannot compare, the Sui River ceasing to flow falls short.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke called forth the valiant and, seizing the moment, let loose his keenest troops—his spirit outdid Banquan, his force surpassed the Huan; chasing the routed north he seized every crossing—steep as Bear-Ear Peaks, still not his equal; still as the Sui, who could match him?

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 琅邪、石首，襟帶岨固，新壘、東墉，金湯是埒。

translations.literal: Langye and Shishou girded by steep passes, Xinlei and East Wall ramparts gold-boiling-water strongholds.
translations.idiomatic: Langye and Shishou were belted by rugged terrain; Xinlei and the eastern wall were strongholds of bronze and boiling water.

sentences.zh: 憑險作守，兵食兼資，風激電駭，莫不震疊，城復于隍，於是乎在。

translations.literal: They relied on terrain for defense with both troops and grain—in wind and lightning shock all trembled and collapsed; cities returned to their moats—thus it came to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting to terrain, they held out with arms and provisions—struck by wind and lightning, all quaked and fell; the cities sank back into their moats, and so it was done.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 獨夫昏很，憑城靡懼，鼓鐘鞺鞜，慠若有餘。

translations.literal: The sole tyrant was blind and cruel, unafraid behind his walls—drums and bells throbbed as if he had surplus strength.
translations.idiomatic: The lone despot was maddened and savage, fearless behind his walls—drums and bells thundered as though strength still overflowed.

sentences.zh: 狎是邪㜸，忌斯冠冕，凶狡因之，將逞孥戮。

translations.literal: He indulged wicked favorites, envied this crown and robe—the treacherous seized their chance, about to extend slaughter to wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: He doted on evil favorites and resented the crown upon another head—the vicious took their opening and were ready to slaughter families whole.

sentences.zh: 公奇謨密運，盛略潛通，忠勇之徒，得申厥效，白旗宣室，未之或比。

translations.literal: The Duke's hidden counsel ran in secret, grand strategy passed underground—the loyal and brave achieved their purpose; the white banners at the Palace of Bright Cultivation were matchless.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke's secret design worked unseen, his great plan passed in silence—loyal and brave men at last could act; the white banners raised at the Bright Cultivation Hall had no parallel.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This too is the Duke's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: This too was the Duke's merit.

sentences.zh: 公有拯億兆之勳，重之以明德，爰初厲志，服道儒門，濯纓來仕，清猷映代。

translations.literal: The Duke had merit of saving the millions, weighted with bright virtue—from the first he set his will, embraced the Way of the Confucian gates, washed his tassel to enter office, and his pure governance shone across the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke had saved the myriad people and was crowned with bright virtue—from the first he hardened his purpose, took the Way from the gates of the Ru, washed his tassel to enter service, and his clean governance lit the age.

sentences.zh: 時運艱難，宗社危殆，崑崗已燎，玉石同焚。

translations.literal: Times were hard, the altars in peril—the Kunlun ridge already burned, jade and stone burned together.
translations.idiomatic: The times were dire and the altars tottered—the ridge of Kunlun was already afire, jade and common stone consumed together.

sentences.zh: 驅率貔貅，抑揚霆電，義等南巢，功齊牧野。

translations.literal: He drove the fierce warriors, wielded thunder and lightning—righteousness equal to Nanchao, merit matching Muye.
translations.idiomatic: He led the tiger hosts, wielding thunder and lightning—righteous as the campaign at Nanchao, meritorious as the battle at Muye.

sentences.zh: 若夫禹功寂漠，微管誰嗣，拯其將魚，驅其被𩬃，解茲亂網，理此棼絲，復禮衽席，反樂河海。

translations.literal: As for Yu's silent merit, who would succeed if not for Guan Zhong—rescuing those about to become fish, driving off those wearing unkempt hair, undoing this tangled net, ordering these tangled threads, restoring ritual and mats, returning joy to the rivers and seas.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu's achievement lay in silence, who could follow if not Guan Zhong? He saved men about to become fish, drove off those with shorn and tangled hair, cut this snarled net, straightened these knotted threads, restored ritual to the mat, and brought music back to river and sea.

sentences.zh: 永平故事，聞之者歎息；

translations.literal: Yongping's old example—those who hear it sigh;
translations.idiomatic: The old ways of Yongping—those who hear of them sigh;

sentences.zh: 司隸舊章，見之者隕涕。

translations.literal: the Commandant's former regulations—those who see them shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: the Commandant's former statutes—those who read them weep.

sentences.zh: 請我民命，還之斗極。

translations.literal: He petitioned for the people's lives, returning them to the pole star's protection.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded for the people's lives and restored them to the turning of the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 憫憫搢紳，重荷戴天之慶；

translations.literal: Sighing gentry bore anew heaven's grace;
translations.idiomatic: The gentry sighed and again bore the blessing of Heaven above;

sentences.zh: 哀哀黔首，復蒙履地之恩。

translations.literal: wretched common folk again received earth-treading kindness.
translations.idiomatic: the common people mourned and again received the mercy of firm ground beneath their feet.

sentences.zh: 德逾嵩、岱，功鄰造物，超哉邈矣，越無得而言焉。

translations.literal: Virtue surpassed Song and Dai, merit neighbored creation—so far beyond speech that words fail.
translations.idiomatic: His virtue exceeded Song and Dai, his achievement touched the work of creation—so lofty and far that words cannot reach it.

sentences.zh: 朕又聞之：疇庸命德，建侯作屏，咸用剋固四維，永隆萬葉。

translations.literal: I have also heard: rewarding merit and assigning virtue, enfeoffing lords as screens—all to strengthen the four corners and forever flourish through myriad branches.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that merit must be rewarded and virtue appointed, that lords are enfeoffed as bulwarks—all to brace the four corners of the realm and make the ten thousand branches flourish forever.

sentences.zh: 是以《二南》流化，九伯斯征，王道淳洽，刑措罔用。

translations.literal: Thus the "Two Souths" spread transformation, the nine lords were dispatched, the royal way ran pure and penalties went unused.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the "Two Souths" flowed with transforming influence, the nine lords went forth on campaign, the royal Way ran clear, and punishments fell unused.

sentences.zh: 覆政弗興，歷茲永久，如燬旣及，晉、鄭靡依。

translations.literal: Overturning governance did not arise through this long span—as at the burning of the beacon towers, Jin and Zheng had none to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: No overturning of rule arose through all this long age—yet as when beacon fires already burn, Jin and Zheng had none to lean on.

sentences.zh: 惟公經綸天地，寧濟區夏，道冠乎伊、稷，賞薄于桓、文，豈所以憲章齊、魯，長轡宇宙。

translations.literal: Only the Duke orders heaven and earth and pacifies the realm—Way surpassing Yi Yin and Hou Ji, reward thinner than Duke Huan and Duke Wen—how can this model Qi and Lu and hold long reins over the cosmos?
translations.idiomatic: Only the Duke has woven heaven and earth and brought peace to the realm—his Way crowns Yi Yin and Hou Ji, yet his reward is less than Duke Huan's or Duke Wen's; how can this be the model of Qi and Lu, the long reins over all under heaven?

sentences.zh: 敬惟前烈，朕甚懼焉。

translations.literal: Reverently considering former worthies, I am deeply afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently weighing the deeds of those before me, I am deeply afraid.

sentences.zh: 今進授相國，改揚州刺史爲牧，以豫州之梁郡歷陽、南徐州之義興、揚州之淮南宣城吳吳興會稽新安東陽十郡，封公爲梁公。

translations.literal: Now I advance and confer Chancellor of State, change Yangzhou Inspector to Governor, and with ten commanderies—Liang and Liyang of Yuzhou, Yixing of South Xuzhou, Huainan, Xuancheng, Wu, Wuxing, Kuaiji, Xin'an, and Dongyang of Yangzhou—enfeoff you as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Now I advance you to Chancellor of State, change the Yangzhou inspector to governor, and with ten commanderies—Liang and Liyang in Yuzhou, Yixing in South Xuzhou, and Huainan, Xuancheng, Wu, Wuxing, Kuaiji, Xin'an, and Dongyang in Yangzhou—I enfeoff you as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 錫茲白土，苴以白茅，爰定爾邦，用建冢社。

translations.literal: Bestow this white earth wrapped in white thatch—thus fixing your state and establishing your ancestral shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Grant this white soil bound in white thatch—thereby fixing your domain and founding your ancestral altar.

sentences.zh: 在昔旦、奭，入居保佑，逮于畢、毛，亦作卿士，任兼內外，禮實宜之。

translations.literal: In former times the Dukes of Zhou and Shao dwelt in protecting blessing; down to Bi and Mao, who also served as ministers—holding duties inner and outer, ritual truly demands it.
translations.idiomatic: In olden days the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao entered to guard and bless; later Bi and Mao too became ministers—bearing duties within and without, as ritual truly requires.

sentences.zh: 今命使持節兼太尉王亮授相國揚州牧印綬，梁公璽紱；

translations.literal: Now I order Bearer of the Staff and concurrent Grand Commandant Wang Liang to confer the Chancellor of State and Yangzhou Governor seals and cords, and the Duke of Liang credentials;
translations.idiomatic: Now I command Bearer of the Staff and concurrent Grand Commandant Wang Liang to confer the seals and cords of Chancellor of State and Yangzhou governor, and the Duke of Liang insignia;

sentences.zh: 使持節兼司空王志授梁公茅土，金虎符第一至第五左，竹使符第一至第十左。

translations.literal: Bearer of the Staff and concurrent Minister of Works Wang Zhi to confer the Duke of Liang thatched earth, gold tiger tally first through fifth left, and bamboo envoy tally first through tenth left.
translations.idiomatic: and Bearer of the Staff and concurrent Minister of Works Wang Zhi to confer the Duke of Liang's earthen fief wrapped in thatch, gold tiger tallies one through five left, and bamboo envoy tallies one through ten left.

sentences.zh: 相國位冠羣后，任總百司，恒典彝數，宜與事革。

translations.literal: Chancellor of State ranks above all lords, duties summing all bureaus—constant regulations and canonical numbers should change with affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor stands above all feudal lords and oversees every office—fixed statutes and canonical numbers should shift with the times.

sentences.zh: 其以相國總百揆，去錄尚書之號，上所假節、侍中貂蟬、中書監印、中外都督大司馬印綬，建安公印策，驃騎大將軍如故。

translations.literal: Let him as Chancellor oversee all governance, remove the Recorder of the Masters of Writing title, and return the provisional tally, Attendant-in-Ordinary cicada badge, Masters of Writing Director seal, Inner-Outer Commander Grand Marshal seals, and Jian'an Duke patent and credentials—Grand General of Agile Cavalry as before.
translations.idiomatic: Let him, as chancellor, govern all affairs, drop the title Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and return the borrowed tally, Attendant-in-Ordinary cicada badge, Director of the Secretariat seal, seals of Inner-Outer Commander and Grand Marshal, and the Jian'an Duke patent and credentials—Grand General of Agile Cavalry unchanged.

sentences.zh: 又加公九錫，其敬聽後命：以公禮律兼修，刑德備舉，哀矜折獄，罔不用情，是用錫公大輅、戎輅各一，玄牡二駟。

translations.literal: Further bestow the Nine Gifts—listen respectfully to the ensuing commands: because the Duke jointly cultivated ritual and law, punishment and virtue complete, pitying in judging cases and using no feeling improperly—therefore bestow one great chariot and one war chariot, and two teams of black stallions.
translations.idiomatic: I further add the Nine Bestowments—hear and obey what follows: because the Duke has perfected both ritual and law, both punishment and virtue, and in judging cases shows pity without bending feeling—therefore I bestow one grand chariot and one war chariot, and two four-horse teams of black stallions.

sentences.zh: 公勞心稼穡，念在民天，丕崇本務，惟穀是寶，是用錫公袞冕之服，赤舄副焉。

translations.literal: The Duke toiled at agriculture, mind on the people's heaven, greatly honored fundamental work and grain as treasure—bestow the ceremonial robe and cap, with vermilion shoes beside.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Duke labors over the fields and keeps the people as his heaven, exalting the root and treasuring grain—I bestow the sacrificial robe and cap, with vermilion shoes to match.

sentences.zh: 公熔鈞所被，變風以雅，易俗陶民，載和邦國，是用錫公軒懸之樂，六佾之舞。

translations.literal: Where the Duke's transforming power reached, vulgar custom became refined, people molded and nations harmonized—bestow suspended bells and the six-row dance.
translations.idiomatic: Where the Duke's melting influence has touched, rough ways turn elegant and peoples are shaped into harmony—I bestow suspended bells and the six-row dance.

sentences.zh: 公文德廣覃，義聲遠洽，椎髻髽首，夷歌請吏，是用錫公朱戶以居。

translations.literal: His civil virtue spread wide, righteous fame reached far—topknotted barbarians sang songs requesting officials—bestow vermilion doorposts for residence.
translations.idiomatic: Because his civil virtue spreads far and his righteous name reaches distant lands, and men with knotted hair and shaved crowns sing barbarian songs asking for officers—I bestow vermilion gateposts for his dwelling.

sentences.zh: 公揚清抑濁，官方有序，多士聿興，《棫樸》流詠，是用錫公納陛以登。

translations.literal: He raised the pure and suppressed the foul, official ranks ordered, many scholars arose and "Old Stump" flowed in song—bestow the inner steps for ascent.
