translations.idiomatic: Because he lifts the clear and checks the turbid, puts office in order, and many scholars rise while "Old Stump" is sung in praise—I bestow the inner steps for ascent.

sentences.zh: 公正色御下，以身軌物，式遏不虞，折衝惟遠，是用錫公虎賁之士三百人。

translations.literal: Upright in mien governing below, by body setting things straight, checking the unforeseen and repelling foes afar—bestow three hundred tiger-guard warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Because he governs with stern countenance and by his own conduct sets the measure, checking the unforeseen and breaking the enemy from afar—I bestow three hundred tiger guards.

sentences.zh: 公威同夏日，志清姦宄，放命圮族，刑茲罔赦，是用錫公鈇、鉞各一。

translations.literal: His prestige like summer sun, intent to purge traitors—those who defy fate and ruin clans, punish without pardon—bestow one axe and one battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: Because his authority is like the summer sun and his will is to purge treachery, and those who defy command and destroy clans shall not be spared—I bestow one axe and one ceremonial axe.

sentences.zh: 公跨躡嵩溟，陵厲區宇，譬諸日月，容光必至，是用錫公彤弓一，彤矢百；

translations.literal: He strode across Mount Song and the eastern sea, towered over the realm—as sun and moon, where light falls it must reach—bestow one red bow and one hundred red arrows;
translations.idiomatic: Because he strides over Mount Song and the eastern sea and towers over the realm, like sun and moon whose radiance must reach wherever it shines—I bestow one red bow and one hundred red arrows;

sentences.zh: 盧弓十，盧矢千。

translations.literal: ten black bows and one thousand black arrows.
translations.idiomatic: ten black bows and one thousand black arrows.

sentences.zh: 公永言惟孝，至感通神，恭嚴祀典，祭有餘敬，是用錫公秬鬯一卣，圭瓚副焉。

translations.literal: Ever speaking of filial piety, utmost feeling reaching spirits—reverently strict in sacrificial rites, offering surplus reverence—bestow one ewer of dark millet wine, with libation cup beside.
translations.idiomatic: Because he ever speaks of filial piety and deepest feeling moves the spirits, reverently observing the sacrifices with overflowing respect—I bestow one ewer of dark millet wine, with libation vessels to match.

sentences.zh: 梁國置丞相以下，一遵舊式。

translations.literal: The Liang state appoints Chancellor of State downward, all following the old pattern.
translations.idiomatic: In the state of Liang, appointments from chancellor downward shall all follow the former pattern.

sentences.zh: 欽哉！

translations.literal: Take heed!
translations.idiomatic: Take heed!

sentences.zh: 其敬循往策，祗服大禮，對揚天眷，用膺多福，以弘我太祖之休命！

translations.literal: Respectfully follow past policy, reverently accept the great rites, respond to Heaven's favor, receive abundant blessing, and spread our founding ancestor's auspicious mandate!
translations.idiomatic: Reverently follow the policies of old, humbly receive the great rites, answer Heaven's grace, take up many blessings, and extend the glorious mandate of our founding ancestor!

sentences.zh: 高祖固辭。

translations.literal: Gaozu firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 府僚勸進曰：「伏承嘉命，顯至佇策。

translations.literal: His staff urged acceptance: "We respectfully receive the splendid mandate and plainly await your policy.
translations.idiomatic: His staff urged him onward: "We humbly receive this glorious command and plainly await your design.

sentences.zh: 明公逡巡盛禮，斯實謙尊之旨，未窮遠大之致。

translations.literal: The Illustrious Duke hesitates at the grand rites—this is truly modest reverence, not yet reaching far-reaching purpose.
translations.idiomatic: The Illustrious Duke holds back from these great rites—this is indeed the intent of humble respect, yet it does not exhaust the greater need.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why so?

sentences.zh: 嗣君棄常，自絕宗社，國命民主，剪爲仇讐，折棟崩榱，壓焉自及，卿士懷脯斮之痛，黔首懼比屋之誅。

translations.literal: The successor ruler abandoned norm and cut himself from the altars—the nation's mandate and its master were carved into enemies; beams broke, rafters collapsed, crushing upon himself—ministers felt the pain of minced flesh, common folk feared extermination house by house.
translations.idiomatic: The reigning lord cast off the constant way and severed himself from the ancestral temples—the nation's mandate and its sovereign were hacked into foes; beams snapped, rafters fell, and the ruin crushed him in turn—ministers tasted the agony of being minced alive, common people feared slaughter house by house.

sentences.zh: 明公亮格天之功，拯水火之切，再躔日月，重綴參辰，反龜玉於塗泥，濟斯民於坑岸，使夫匹婦童兒，羞言伊、呂，鄉校里塾，恥談五霸。

translations.literal: The Illustrious Duke displayed heaven-reaching merit, rescued from fire and water's urgency, twice tracked sun and moon and re-strung the constellation stars, returned jade and turtle to mud, saved these people from pit and cliff—so that wives and children blush to speak of Yi and Lü, village schools shame to discuss the Five Hegemons.
translations.idiomatic: The Illustrious Duke showed merit that measured heaven, pulled the realm from fire and flood, twice restored sun and moon and restrung the stars of Shen, returned jade and turtle from the mud, and lifted the people from pit and cliff—so that wives and children blush to name Yi and Lü, and village schools are ashamed to speak of the Five Hegemons.

sentences.zh: 而位卑乎阿衡，地狹於曲阜，慶賞之道，尚其未洽。

translations.literal: Yet your rank is lower than Aheng, your lands narrower than Qufu—the way of reward and favor is still not complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your rank stands below Aheng, your domain is narrower than Qufu—the path of reward and grace is still unfinished.

sentences.zh: 夫大寶公器，非要非距，至公至平，當仁誰讓？

translations.literal: The great treasure is a public vessel—not to be craved, not to be refused—in utmost fairness, who yields when it is one's turn for benevolent rule?
translations.idiomatic: The great mandate is a vessel for all—not to be grasped, not to be pushed away—in perfect fairness, when benevolent rule is due, who should yield?

sentences.zh: 明公宜祗奉天人，允膺大禮。

translations.literal: The Illustrious Duke should reverently receive Heaven and the people, fully accept the great rite.
translations.idiomatic: The Illustrious Duke should reverently answer Heaven and the people and fully accept the great rite.

sentences.zh: 無使後予之歌，同彼胥怨，兼濟之人，翻爲獨善。

translations.literal: Do not let songs of "after me" echo that old resentment, turning one who would benefit all into one who benefits himself alone.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let the song of "after me" share that ancient bitterness, making one who would rescue all become one who saves himself alone.

sentences.zh: 」公不許。

translations.literal: " The Duke did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " The Duke would not consent.

sentences.zh: 二月辛酉，府僚重請曰：「近以朝命蘊策，冒奏丹誠，奉被還令，未蒙虛受，搢紳顒顒，深所未達。

translations.literal: On day xinyou in the second month, the staff again petitioned: "Recently, bearing the court's mandate in secret policy, we presumptuously presented our sincere hearts, received return orders, and were not granted empty acceptance—gentry look on eagerly, deeply unable to comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinyou in the second month the staff petitioned again: "Not long ago, carrying the court's hidden design, we ventured to lay our loyal hearts bare; we received your refusal and were not granted gracious acceptance—the gentry look on with longing, deeply unable to understand.

sentences.zh: 蓋聞受金於府，通人弘致，高蹈海隅，匹夫小節，是以履乘石而周公不以爲疑，贈玉璜而太公不以爲讓。

translations.literal: We have heard: receiving gold from the treasury is the great man's broad purpose; high stepping to the sea corner is the petty man's small scruple—thus treading the stone steps, the Duke of Zhou was not suspected; gifted the jade tablet, Duke Tai was not deemed to have refused.
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that to take gold from the treasury is the enlightened man's broad aim, while to hide oneself at the sea's edge is the common man's petty scruple—thus when the Duke of Zhou trod the stone steps, none doubted him; when Duke Tai was given the jade tablet, none called it refusal.

sentences.zh: 況世哲繼軌，先德在民，經綸草昧，歎深微管。

translations.literal: How much more when a sage successor follows the track, ancestral virtue lives in the people—in ordering the primeval chaos, who does not sigh deeply for "if not for Guan Zhong"?
translations.idiomatic: How much more when a sage heir follows the former path and ancestral virtue still lives in the people—in ordering the realm from chaos, who does not sigh over "if not for Guan Zhong"?

sentences.zh: 加以朱方之役，荊河是依，班師振旅，大造王室。

translations.literal: Add to this the campaign at Zhufang, reliance on Jing and He—withdrawal of troops and shaking of armies, great savior of the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Add the campaign at Zhufang, leaning on the Jing and the He—withdrawing the army and rallying the host, a great renewal of the royal house.

sentences.zh: 雖復累繭救宋，重胝存楚，居今觀古，曾何足云。

translations.literal: Though again shoes piled with calluses saved Song, soles layered thick preserved Chu—measured against the ancients from today, what are those beside this?
translations.idiomatic: Even shoes heaped with calluses for Song, even soles thickened to save Chu—set beside your deeds today, what are they worth?

sentences.zh: 而惑甚盜鐘，功疑不賞，皇天后土，不勝其酷。

translations.literal: Yet doubts like the bell-thief's confusion, merit doubted and unrewarded—Heaven and Earth cannot bear such cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet merit is doubted and left unrewarded, as though one were the bell-thief deceiving himself—Heaven and Earth cannot endure such harshness.

sentences.zh: 是以玉馬駿奔，表微子之去；

translations.literal: Thus the jade horses galloped swift, showing Weizi's departure;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the jade horses ran in haste, showing Weizi's going away;

sentences.zh: 金板出地，告龍逢之冤。

translations.literal: the gold tablets emerged from earth, reporting Longfeng's grievance.
translations.idiomatic: and the gold tablets rose from the ground, proclaiming Longfeng's wrong.

sentences.zh: 明公據鞍輟哭，厲三軍之志，獨居掩涕，激義士之心，故能使海若登祗，罄圖效祉，山戎、孤竹，束馬影從，伐罪弔民，一匡靜亂。

translations.literal: The Illustrious Duke gripped the saddle and halted weeping, steeling the three armies' will; alone in private he wiped tears, stirring the righteous—thus making the sea lord ascend and offer blessings, Mountain Rong and Guzhu tying horses to follow in shadow—punishing crime and mourning for the people, one correction and chaos stilled.
translations.idiomatic: The Illustrious Duke clutched the saddle and checked his tears, hardening the will of the three armies; alone he hid his weeping and stirred the hearts of men of honor—so that the sea lord came up to offer blessing, Mountain Rong and Guzhu tied their horses and followed like shadows—punishing the guilty, comforting the people, and in one stroke setting chaos at rest.

sentences.zh: 匪叨天功，實勤濡足。

translations.literal: Not claiming Heaven's work—in truth he toiled with wet feet.
translations.idiomatic: This was not stealing Heaven's achievement; in truth he labored with soaked feet.

sentences.zh: 且明公本自諸生，取樂名教，道風素論，坐鎮雅俗，不習孫、吳，遘茲神武。

translations.literal: Moreover the Illustrious Duke came from the schoolmen, took joy in name and teaching—Way-wind and plain discourse, sitting firm over refined custom—he did not study Sun and Wu, yet met this divine martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Illustrious Duke began as a scholar, finding joy in teaching and moral order—his Way and plain speech steadied elegant custom; he did not study Sun and Wu, yet met this divine martial gift.

sentences.zh: 驅盡誅之氓，濟必封之俗，龜玉不毀，誰之功與？

translations.literal: He drove the utterly condemned mob, aided customs ripe for enfeoffment—turtle and jade undestroyed—whose achievement is this if not yours?
translations.idiomatic: He drove off the mob marked for destruction and lifted customs ready for enfeoffment—the turtle and jade were not shattered—whose work is this if not yours?

sentences.zh: 獨爲君子，將使伊、周何地？

translations.literal: To remain alone a gentleman—where then would Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou stand?"
translations.idiomatic: If you alone remain the gentleman, where shall Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou have place?"

sentences.zh: 」於是始受相國梁公之命。

translations.literal: Thereupon he first accepted appointment as Chancellor and Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he first accept appointment as Chancellor and Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 是日，焚東昏淫奢異服六十二種於都街。

translations.literal: That day, sixty-two kinds of Dong Hun's lewd, extravagant, and strange garments were burned in the capital streets.
translations.idiomatic: That same day sixty-two kinds of Dong Hun's licentious, luxurious, and outlandish dress were burned in the streets of the capital.

sentences.zh: 湘東王寶晊謀反，賜死。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangdong Bao Zhi plotted rebellion and was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangdong Bao Zhi plotted rebellion and was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 詔追贈梁公故夫人爲梁妃。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed the late wife of the Duke of Liang as Liang Consort.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made the Duke of Liang's late wife Consort of Liang.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，南兗州隊主陳文興於桓城內鑿井，得玉鏤騏驎、金鏤玉璧、水精環各二枚。

translations.literal: On day yichou, Chen Wenxing, squad chief of South Yanzhou, digging a well within Huan city, obtained two jade-inlaid qilin, two gold-inlaid jade bi, and two crystal rings each.
translations.idiomatic: On day yichou, Chen Wenxing, squad chief of South Yanzhou, while digging a well inside Huan city, found two jade-inlaid qilin, two gold-inlaid jade bi, and two crystal rings.

sentences.zh: 又建康令羊瞻解稱鳳皇見縣之桐下里。

translations.literal: Jiankang Magistrate Yang Zhan also reported that a phoenix was seen at Tongxia village in the county.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang magistrate Yang Zhan also reported that a phoenix had been seen at Tongxia village in the county.

sentences.zh: 宣德皇后稱美符瑞，歸于於相國府。

translations.literal: Empress Xuande praised the auspicious signs and attributed them to the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuande praised these auspicious omens and ascribed them to the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，詔：「梁國初建，宜須綜理，可依舊選諸要職，悉依天朝之制。

translations.literal: On day bingyin, an edict: "The Liang state is newly established and requires comprehensive governance—select all key posts according to the old pattern, all following the imperial court's system.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingyin an edict said: "The state of Liang is newly founded and must be put in order—choose all important offices as before, all according to the imperial court's system.

sentences.zh: 」高祖上表曰：

translations.literal: " Gaozu submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞以言取士，士飾其言，以行取人，人竭其行。

translations.literal: " Your subject has heard: if you choose scholars by words, scholars adorn their words; if you choose men by deeds, men exhaust their deeds.
translations.idiomatic: " Your subject has heard that if one selects scholars by speech, scholars polish their speech; if one selects men by conduct, men spend themselves in conduct.

sentences.zh: 所謂才生於世，窮達惟時；

translations.literal: So it is said: talent is born of the age, and success or failure depends on the times alone;
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, talent rises with the age, and fortune turns on timing alone;

sentences.zh: 而風流遂往，馳騖成俗，媒孽誇衒，利盡錐刀，遂使官人之門，肩摩轂擊。

translations.literal: yet the elegant spirit has passed away, rushing pursuit has become custom, slander and boasting flourish, and profit is measured to the knife's edge—so that at officials' gates shoulders rub and wheels collide.
translations.idiomatic: Yet refinement has faded, ambition has hardened into habit, flattery and self-display rule the day, and every gain is counted to the last coin—until the doors of office swarm shoulder to shoulder and wheel to wheel.

sentences.zh: 豈直暴蓋露冠，不避寒暑，遂乃戢屨杖策，風雨必至。

translations.literal: Not only do they go bareheaded and uncapped, unafraid of heat and cold; they even tie up their shoes and take up staffs, coming even through wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: Men no longer merely brave sun and frost with uncovered heads; they strap on their sandals, take up their staves, and come through storm and tempest.

sentences.zh: 良由鄉舉里選，不師古始，稱肉度骨，遺之管庫。

translations.literal: Truly because village recommendation and district selection no longer follow ancient ways—flesh is weighed to judge the bone, and men are left to granary posts.
translations.idiomatic: The cause lies in local recommendation and district selection turned from ancient practice: appearance is weighed like meat on a scale, and worthy men are shelved in storehouse clerkships.

sentences.zh: 加以山河梁畢，闕輿徵之恩；

translations.literal: Added to this, the grace of imperial summons after the Mount Liang examination is lacking;
translations.idiomatic: On top of this, the old favor of imperial summons after the frontier examination has vanished;

sentences.zh: 金、張、許、史，忘舊業之替。

translations.literal: the Jin, Zhang, Xu, and Shi clans forget the decline of their ancestral calling.
translations.idiomatic: and clans once as proud as Jin, Zhang, Xu, and Shi forget how far their old estates have fallen.

sentences.zh: 吁，可傷哉！

translations.literal: Alas—how sad!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 且夫譜牒訛誤，詐偽多緒，人物雅俗，莫肯留心。

translations.literal: Moreover, genealogical registers are riddled with error and fraud has many threads; no one attends to whether a man is refined or coarse.
translations.idiomatic: Genealogies are corrupt, imposture ramifies in every direction, and no one cares whether a man is cultivated or crude.

sentences.zh: 是以冒襲良家，卽成冠族；

translations.literal: Thus those who falsely claim good families at once become crowned clans;
translations.idiomatic: So a man who steals a respectable lineage becomes a great clan overnight;

sentences.zh: 妄修邊幅，便爲雅士；

translations.literal: those who vainly dress up their appearance at once become elegant scholars;
translations.idiomatic: one who merely trims his outward show passes for a man of taste;

sentences.zh: 負俗深累，遽遭寵擢；

translations.literal: those deeply burdened by vulgar repute are suddenly favored and promoted;
translations.idiomatic: men long stained by ill repute are suddenly raised and favored;

sentences.zh: 墓木已拱，方被徽榮。

translations.literal: when the tomb trees already arch, then they receive glory and honor.
translations.idiomatic: and honor arrives only after the trees above their graves have grown tall.

sentences.zh: 故前代選官，皆立選簿，應在貫魚，自有銓次。

translations.literal: Therefore in former ages, when selecting officials, they all established selection registers; those who should stand in the string of fish had their own order of evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times every office of selection kept its own register, and men due for advancement stood in a fixed order, like fish strung on a line.

sentences.zh: 胄籍升降，行能臧否，或素定懷抱，或得之餘論，故得簡通賓客，無事掃門。

translations.literal: Pedigree rose and fell, conduct and ability were praised or condemned—sometimes settled by long-held judgment, sometimes obtained from wider discussion; thus they could briefly receive guests without needing to sweep the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Family standing, talent, and moral worth were already known—by long acquaintance or public report—so a man could receive visitors without waiting at his gate for petitioners.

sentences.zh: 頃代陵夷，九流乖失。

translations.literal: In recent generations decline has set in; the nine currents have gone awry.
translations.idiomatic: In recent generations standards have collapsed, and every path of worth has lost its way.

sentences.zh: 其有勇退忘進，懷質抱真者，選部或以未經朝謁，難於進用。

translations.literal: Those who bravely withdraw and forget advancement, who embrace quality and hold to truth—the Selection Bureau sometimes, because they have not yet had audience at court, finds it hard to appoint them.
translations.idiomatic: Men who shun ambition and keep their integrity are often passed over because they have never yet presented themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 或有晦善藏聲，自埋衡蓽，又以名不素著，絕其階緒。

translations.literal: Some who hide their goodness and conceal their voice, burying themselves in humble thatch—because their names are not known, their ladder of advancement is cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Others bury their gifts in obscurity and live in humble seclusion, only to find the rungs of office closed to them because no one knows their names.

sentences.zh: 必須畫刺投狀，然後彈冠，則是驅迫廉撝，獎成澆競。

translations.literal: They must write visiting cards and submit petitions, then only dust off the hat—this drives and compels modest restraint, rewarding shallow competition.
translations.idiomatic: Only after writing cards and filing petitions may they dust off the official cap—thus integrity is driven out and shameless rivalry is rewarded.

sentences.zh: 愚謂自今選曹宜精隱括，依舊立簿，使冠屨無爽，名實不違，庶人識崖涘，造請自息。

translations.literal: I foolishly think that from now on the Selection Bureau should carefully scrutinize and select, establish registers as before, so cap and sandal do not err and name and reality do not diverge; then common people will know the bank, and forced visits will cease of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that hereafter the Bureau of Selection should examine candidates with rigor, restore the old registers, and keep rank and conduct, name and fact, in accord—so that men know their bounds and the plague of importunate petitioning dies away.

sentences.zh: 且聞中間立格，甲族以二十登仕，後門以過立試吏，求之愚懷，抑有未達。

translations.literal: Moreover I hear that in between rules were established: noble clans enter office at twenty, while back doors after thirty become probationary clerks—seeking this in my foolish thought, I fear there is what is not understood.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that new rules were set: great families may take office at twenty, while lesser men must wait until after thirty to serve as clerks—and in my humble judgment this too misses the mark.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why so?

sentences.zh: 設官分職，惟才是務。

translations.literal: Establishing offices and dividing duties—only talent is the aim.
translations.idiomatic: Offices exist and duties are divided for one purpose: to employ the able.

sentences.zh: 若八元立年，居皁隸而見抑；

translations.literal: If the Eight Worthies at their appointed age were stationed among black-robed clerks and were suppressed;
translations.idiomatic: If the Eight Worthies, come of age, were kept among menials and passed over;

sentences.zh: 四凶弱冠，處鼎族而宜甄。

translations.literal: the Four Evils at weak cap could sit in great clans and should be selected.
translations.idiomatic: while the Four Evils, barely grown, sat in great houses and were deemed fit for office—

sentences.zh: 是則世祿之家，無意爲善；

translations.literal: then hereditary salary families would have no intent to do good;
translations.idiomatic: then hereditary houses would see no reason to cultivate virtue;

sentences.zh: 布衣之士，肆心爲惡。

translations.literal: common cloth scholars would give free rein to evil.
translations.idiomatic: and men of humble birth would feel free to do as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 豈所以弘獎風流，希向後進？

translations.literal: How is this the way to broadly encourage elegant spirit and hope for later generations?
translations.idiomatic: How could this encourage excellence or give the young anything worth striving toward?

sentences.zh: 此實巨蠹，尤宜刊革。

translations.literal: This is truly a great pest; especially it should be cut and reformed.
translations.idiomatic: This is a grievous corruption and should be abolished at once.

sentences.zh: 不然，將使周人有路傍之泣，晉臣興漁獵之歎。

translations.literal: Otherwise, it will make Zhou people weep by the roadside and Jin ministers sigh at fishing and hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise we shall again see the roadside weeping of Zhou and the hunting-sighs of Jin ministers who neglect the realm.

sentences.zh: 且俗長浮競，人寡退情，若限歲登朝，必增年就宦，故貌實昏童，籍已逾立，滓穢名教，於斯爲甚。

translations.literal: Moreover custom favors shallow rivalry; people lack retiring sentiment; if age limits entry to court, ages for office must increase—thus appearance is truly a child but the register already passes thirty; defiling name and teaching, in this it is worst.
translations.idiomatic: The age loves display and hates restraint; if office is tied to a fixed age, men will delay entry and grow old in waiting—so that a man looks like a boy while his record says he is past thirty. Nothing defiles the teaching of the sages more than this.

sentences.zh: 臣總司內外，憂責是任，朝政得失，義不容隱。

translations.literal: Your servant oversees inner and outer affairs; worry and responsibility are mine; gains and losses of court government—righteousness cannot permit concealment.
translations.idiomatic: I oversee affairs within and without the palace, and the burden of care is mine; on the right and wrong of government I cannot keep silent.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下垂聖淑之姿，降聽覽之末，則彝倫自穆，憲章惟允。

translations.literal: Humbly I wish Your Majesty to let fall sacred and fine bearing, descend to the end of listening—then constant norms will harmonize themselves, and statutes will be just.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will lend your sacred ear to these words at last, so that human order may right itself and law may stand true.

sentences.zh: 詔依高祖表施行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Gaozu's memorial be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved Gaozu's memorial and ordered it carried out.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，詔曰：

translations.literal: On day bingxu, an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day, an edict read:

sentences.zh: 嵩高惟岳，配天所以流稱；

translations.literal: Song Mountain alone is the peak; pairing with Heaven is why its fame flows abroad;
translations.idiomatic: Song Mountain stands supreme among peaks, and its name endures because it shares Heaven's majesty;

sentences.zh: 大啓南陽，霸德所以光闡。

translations.literal: great founding at Nanyang—overbearing virtue is why its glory spreads.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang saw a great founding, and hegemonic virtue is why its light still shines.

sentences.zh: 忠誠簡帝，番君膺上爵之尊；

translations.literal: Loyalty and sincerity choosing the emperor—Lord Fan received the honor of highest rank;
translations.idiomatic: Lord Fan, loyal and discerning, won the highest noble rank;

sentences.zh: 勤勞王室，姬公增附庸之地。

translations.literal: diligent labor for the royal house—Duke Ji increased attached fief lands.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ji, toiling for the royal house, was granted broader domains.

sentences.zh: 前王令典，布諸方策，長祚字甿，罔不由此。

translations.literal: Former kings' fine statutes, spread in writings on bamboo—long reign and the prosperity of the people, none not from this.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy precedents of former kings, set down in the records, have ever been the source of long rule and the people's peace.

sentences.zh: 相國梁公，體茲上哲，齊聖廣淵。

translations.literal: The Chancellor of State, Duke of Liang, embodies this supreme wisdom, equal in holiness and broad in depth.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor of State, Duke of Liang, embodies this highest wisdom—holy in stature and vast in understanding.

sentences.zh: 文教內洽，武功外暢。

translations.literal: Civil teaching harmonized within, martial achievement flourishing without.
translations.idiomatic: Within, culture has taken root; without, martial glory has spread.

sentences.zh: 推轂作籓，則威懷被於殊俗；

translations.literal: Pushing the wheel and serving as frontier lord—then awe and gentle rule spread to foreign customs;
translations.idiomatic: As frontier lord he drove the chariot of state, and his awe and kindness reached distant peoples;

sentences.zh: 治兵教戰，則霆雷赫於萬里。

translations.literal: training soldiers and teaching war—then thunder and lightning blaze ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: training armies and teaching war—until thunder rolled across ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 道喪時昏，讒邪孔熾。

translations.literal: The Way was lost in dark times; slander and evil greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The age had lost the Way; slander and wickedness ran wild.

sentences.zh: 豈徒宗社如綴，神器莫主而已哉！

translations.literal: Was it merely that the altars hung by a thread and the sacred vessel had no master!
translations.idiomatic: And was the ruin only that the altars hung by a thread and the throne stood empty?

sentences.zh: 至於兆庶殲亡，衣冠殄滅，餘類殘喘，指命崇朝，含生業業，投足無所，遂乃山川反覆，草木塗地。

translations.literal: As for the hundred million slaughtered, caps and robes extinguished, remnant kinds gasping, life hanging by a morning—all living things trembled, nowhere to set foot—so mountains and rivers overturned and grass and trees painted the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Countless people were slain, scholars and officials wiped out, survivors gasping out their lives from dawn to dusk; every living thing trembled with nowhere to stand, until mountains and rivers were overturned and the earth was covered with the dead.

sentences.zh: 與夫仁被行葦之時，信及豚魚之日，何其遼夐相去之遠歟！

translations.literal: Compared with the time when benevolence covered the marching rushes, when faith reached pigs and fish—how vast the distance between them!
translations.idiomatic: What a gulf lies between that age and the days when benevolence fell even on roadside weeds and trust reached beasts in the pen!

sentences.zh: 公命師鞠旅，指景長騖。

translations.literal: The Duke ordered armies and mustered troops, pointing to the sun and racing far.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke raised armies and mustered his hosts, driving forward as though chasing the sun itself.

sentences.zh: 而本朝危切，樊、鄧遐遠，凶徒盤據，水陸相望，爰自姑孰，屈于夏首，嚴城勁卒，憑川爲固。

translations.literal: Yet our dynasty was critically imperiled; Fan and Deng were distant; violent bands entrenched, land and water facing each other—from Gushu, pinned at Xiashou—strong cities and fierce troops, relying on rivers for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the dynasty stood on the brink; Fan and Deng were far away; rebels held entrenched positions across land and water, from Gushu to Xiashou, with strong walls, fierce soldiers, and rivers for their ramparts.

sentences.zh: 公沿漢浮江，電激風掃，舟徒水覆，地險雲傾，藉茲義勇，前無強陣，拯危京邑，清我帝畿，撲旣燎於原火，免將誅於比屋。

translations.literal: The Duke floated along the Han and sailed the river—lightning shock, wind sweep; boatmen drowned, terrain fell like clouds; with these righteous warriors, no strong formation stood before him; saving the perilous capital, clearing our imperial domain; beating fire already burning on the plain, sparing those about to be executed house to house.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke swept down the Han and sailed the Yangtze like lightning and wind; boats capsized, defenses crumbled like clouds in storm; led by loyal courage he broke every line, rescued the capital in its peril, cleansed the imperial domain, stamped out fires already running across the fields, and spared household after household from the executioner.

sentences.zh: 悠悠兆庶，命不在天；

translations.literal: Far and wide the hundred million—fate was not in Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: For countless people, life no longer hung on Heaven alone;

sentences.zh: 茫茫六合，咸受其賜。

translations.literal: vastly the six directions all received his gift.
translations.idiomatic: throughout the six directions all shared in his deliverance.

sentences.zh: 匡俗正本，民不失職。

translations.literal: Correcting custom and righting the root, people did not lose their posts.
translations.idiomatic: He set custom aright and restored the foundations, so that men did not lose their proper place.

sentences.zh: 仁信並行，禮樂同暢。

translations.literal: Benevolence and faith together practiced, rites and music together fluent.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence and trust went hand in hand, and rites and music flourished together.

sentences.zh: 伊、周未足方軌，桓、文遠有慚德。

translations.literal: Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou are not enough to share the track; Duke Huan and Duke Wen far have shame in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Even Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou cannot stand beside him; Duke Huan and Duke Wen would blush at the comparison.

sentences.zh: 而爵後籓牧，地終秦、楚，非所以式酬光烈，允答元勳。

translations.literal: Yet ennobling him as later frontier lord, with lands ending at Qin and Chu—this is not the way to repay glorious deeds and fully answer primal merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to reward him only as a frontier prince, with lands bounded by Qin and Chu, is no fit repayment for such blazing merit and founding achievement.

sentences.zh: 寔由公履謙爲本，形於造次，嘉數未申，晦朔增佇。

translations.literal: Truly because the Duke takes humility as root, shown even in haste, fine rewards not yet declared, new moon and old moon add longing.
translations.idiomatic: This is because the Duke, rooted in humility, has again and again refused what is due—so that month after month the realm waits in longing.

sentences.zh: 便宜崇斯禮秩，允副遐邇之望。

translations.literal: It is fitting to exalt this ritual rank, fully matching the hope of far and near.
translations.idiomatic: It is right to raise him to this higher station and satisfy the hopes of all, near and far.

sentences.zh: 可進梁公爵爲王。

translations.literal: He may advance the Duke of Liang to King.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Liang shall be advanced to King.

sentences.zh: 以豫州之南譙、盧江、江州之尋陽、郢州之武昌、西陽、南徐州之南琅邪、南東海、晉陵、揚州之臨海、永嘉十郡，益梁國，並前爲二十郡。

translations.literal: With the ten commanderies of Southern Qiao and Lujiang of Yuzhou, Xunyang of Jiangzhou, Wuchang and Xiyang of Yingzhou, Southern Langye, Southern Donghai, and Jinling of South Xuzhou, and Linhai and Yongjia of Yangzhou—increase the State of Liang, together with the former domains making twenty commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Let the ten commanderies of Southern Qiao and Lujiang in Yuzhou, Xunyang in Jiangzhou, Wuchang and Xiyang in Yingzhou, Southern Langye, Southern Donghai, and Jinling in South Xuzhou, and Linhai and Yongjia in Yangzhou be added to the State of Liang, making twenty commanderies in all with those already held.

sentences.zh: 其相國、揚州牧、驃騎大將軍如故。

translations.literal: His posts as Chancellor of State, Governor of Yangzhou, and General of Cavalry on the Fast March remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: He shall retain his posts as Chancellor of State, Governor of Yangzhou, and General of Cavalry on the Fast March.

sentences.zh: 公固辭。

translations.literal: The Duke firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke refused firmly.

sentences.zh: 有詔斷表。

translations.literal: An edict cut off his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rejected his refusal.

sentences.zh: 相國左長史王瑩等率百僚敦請。

translations.literal: Left Chief Clerk of the Chancellery Wang Ying and others led the hundred officials in earnest urging.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying, Left Chief Clerk of the Chancellery, led the hundred officials in pressing him to accept.

sentences.zh: 三月辛卯，延陵縣華陽邏主戴車牒稱云：「十二月乙酉，甘露降茅山，彌漫數里。

translations.literal: Third month, xinmao: Yanling county Huayang district chief Dai Che submitted a report saying, "Twelfth month, yiyou: sweet dew fell on Maoshan, spreading several li.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, xinmao: Dai Che, chief of Huayang district in Yanling county, reported, "On yiyou in the twelfth month, sweet dew fell on Maoshan and spread for several li.

sentences.zh: 正月己酉，邏將潘道蓋于山石穴中得毛龜一。

translations.literal: First month, jiyou: district general Pan Daogai obtained one hairy turtle in a mountain stone cave.
translations.idiomatic: First month, jiyou: district general Pan Daogai found a hairy turtle in a mountain cave.

sentences.zh: 二月辛酉，邏將徐靈符又於山東見白麞一。

translations.literal: Second month, xinyou: district general Xu Lingfu again saw one white deer on the eastern mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, xinyou: district general Xu Lingfu also saw a white deer on the eastern slope.

sentences.zh: 丙寅平旦，山上雲霧四合，須臾有玄黃之色，狀如龍形，長十餘丈，乍隱乍顯，久乃從西北升天。

translations.literal: On day bingyin at dawn, clouds and mist on the mountain joined on four sides; in a moment there was black-yellow color, shaped like a dragon more than ten zhang long, now hidden now visible; long after, it rose to heaven from the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin at dawn, cloud and mist closed in on every side; then black and yellow light took the shape of a dragon more than ten zhang long, now vanishing, now appearing, until at last it ascended to heaven from the northwest.

sentences.zh: 」丁卯，兗州刺史馬元和籤：「所領東平郡壽張縣見騶虞一。」

translations.literal: " On day dingmao, Yanzhou Inspector Ma Yuanhe reported: "In Shouzhang county of Dongping commandery under his jurisdiction one Zouyu was seen."
translations.idiomatic: " On dingmao, Yanzhou Inspector Ma Yuanhe reported, "In Shouzhang county of Dongping, under his command, a Zouyu was seen."

sentences.zh: 癸巳，受梁王之命。

translations.literal: On day guisi, he received the mandate of King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day, he accepted the mandate of King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「孤以虛昧，任執國鈞，雖夙夜勤止，念在興治，而育德振民，邈然尚遠。

translations.literal: An order said: "I, in my emptiness and dimness, take charge of the nation's helm; though I toil early and rest late, my thought is on raising governance, yet nurturing virtue and stirring the people still seems far.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: "I, unworthy and obscure, hold the nation's helm; though I rise early and sleep late with governance always in mind, to nurture virtue and lift the people still seems far off.

sentences.zh: 聖朝永言舊式，隆此眷命。

translations.literal: The sacred court ever speaks of the old style, elevating this cherished mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred court has honored the old forms and raised me to this cherished charge.

sentences.zh: 侯伯盛典，方軌前烈，嘉錫隆被，禮數昭崇。

translations.literal: Marquis and count grand ceremony, sharing track with former glorious ones; fine gifts richly spread, ritual number clearly exalted.
translations.idiomatic: The rites due a marquis or count now match the great founders of old; honors have been heaped upon me and ceremonial rank made bright.

sentences.zh: 徒守愿節，終隔體諒。

translations.literal: In vain I guard willing integrity, finally separated from mutual understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have held to modest refusal and remain far from true accord.

sentences.zh: 羣后百司，重茲敦獎，勉茲厚顏，當此休祚。

translations.literal: All the lords and hundred offices, again this earnest reward—putting forth thick face at this fine fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The lords and the hundred offices have pressed this reward upon me again, and I must bear the shame of accepting in such a fortunate hour.

sentences.zh: 望昆、彭以長想，欽桓、文而歎息，思弘政塗，莫知津濟。

translations.literal: Looking to Kun Wu and Peng Zu for long thought, admiring Duke Huan and Duke Wen and sighing, I think to spread the path of governance yet know not the ford.
translations.idiomatic: I think of Kun Wu and Peng Zu and feel how small I am; I look to Duke Huan and Duke Wen and sigh; I would broaden the way of rule, yet cannot see the crossing.

sentences.zh: 邦甸初啓，籓宇惟新，思覃嘉慶，被之下國。

translations.literal: The realm's inner territories have just opened, frontier domains are just new—I think to spread fine celebration, covering the lower states.
translations.idiomatic: The inner realm has only just been restored and the frontiers made new; I would spread this blessing through all the lands below.

sentences.zh: 國內殊死以下，今月十五日昧爽以前，一皆原赦。

translations.literal: Within the state below death penalty—before dawn on the fifteenth of this month, all entirely pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the realm, all crimes short of death are pardoned before dawn on the fifteenth of this month.

sentences.zh: 鰥寡孤獨不能自存者，賜穀五斛。

translations.literal: Widows, widowers, orphans, and the alone who cannot support themselves—given five hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Widows, widowers, orphans, and the destitute who cannot support themselves shall receive five hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 府州所統，亦同蠲蕩。」

translations.literal: Prefectures and provinces under command—also same exemption and sweeping."
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures and provinces under my rule shall grant the same pardon and relief."

sentences.zh: 丙午，命王冕十有二旒，建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，乘金根車，駕六馬，備五時副車，置旄頭雲罕，樂舞八佾，設鐘鋋宮縣。

translations.literal: On day bingwu, he was ordered the king's cap of twelve tassels, established the Son of Heaven's banners, going out with police and entering with halts, riding the golden-root chariot, driving six horses, equipped with seasonal secondary chariots, setting battle-standard and cloud banner, music and dance in eight rows, establishing bell and chime palace ensemble.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day he was granted the twelve-tasseled royal cap, the banners of the Son of Heaven, imperial escort on departure and return, the golden-root chariot drawn by six horses, seasonal secondary chariots, the battle-standard and cloud banner, eight rows of dancers, and the full palace bell ensemble.

sentences.zh: 王妃王子王女爵命之號，一依舊儀。

translations.literal: Queen consort, princes, and princesses—the titles of rank and command, all according to old ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Titles for the queen, princes, and princesses followed the old rites.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，齊帝禪位于梁王。

translations.literal: On day bingchen, the Qi emperor abdicated the throne to the King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day, the Qi emperor abdicated in favor of the King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: An edict read:

sentences.zh: 夫五德更始，三正迭興，馭物資賢，登庸啓聖，故帝跡所以代昌，王度所以改耀，革晦以明，由來尚矣。

translations.literal: The five virtues alternate and renew; the three orthodoxies rise in succession; governing things requires the worthy, and ascending to office opens the sage—thus imperial traces change and flourish, royal measures change and shine, changing darkness to light, from of old this has been honored.
translations.idiomatic: The five virtues succeed one another, the three calendars take turn after turn; to govern the world one must employ the worthy, and to rise to office is to open the way for sages. Dynasties flourish as they change, royal law shines as it is renewed, and the turning of darkness into light has been honored since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 齊德淪微，危亡薦襲。

translations.literal: Qi's virtue sank in decline; danger and extinction came in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's virtue collapsed, and ruin followed ruin.

sentences.zh: 隆昌凶虐，實違天地；

translations.literal: Longchang's cruel tyranny truly violated Heaven and Earth;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Longchang was savage and cruel, offending Heaven and Earth;

sentences.zh: 永元昏暴，取紊人神。

translations.literal: Yongyuan's disordered violence seized and confused human and divine.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yongyuan was violent and benighted, overturning the order of men and gods.

sentences.zh: 三光再沉，七廟如綴。

translations.literal: The three luminaries again sank; the seven temples hung like a thread.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, moon, and stars were darkened again; the seven ancestral temples hung by a thread.

sentences.zh: 鼎業幾移，含識知泯。

translations.literal: The cauldron enterprise nearly shifted; all knowing consciousness nearly extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The royal mandate nearly passed away, and all who had understanding were nearly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 我高、明之祚，眇焉將墜。

translations.literal: Our Gao and Ming dynastic fortune, faintly about to fall.
translations.idiomatic: The fortune of our Gao and Ming line trembled on the edge of collapse.

sentences.zh: 永惟屯難，冰谷載懷。

translations.literal: Ever thinking of accumulated hardship, ice and valley fill the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering these accumulated calamities, I feel perils as cold as ice and as deep as a ravine.

sentences.zh: 相國梁王，天誕睿哲，神縱靈武，德格玄祇，功均造物。

translations.literal: Chancellor of State King of Liang—Heaven bore keen wisdom, spirit unrestrained in divine martiality, virtue reaching dark deities, achievement equal to creating things.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor of State, King of Liang, was born with Heaven's keen wisdom and a spirit of divine martial power; his virtue moves the hidden powers, his achievement matches the work of creation.

sentences.zh: 止宗社之橫流，反生民之塗炭。

translations.literal: He stopped the altars' cross-flow and reversed the people's burnt coating.
translations.idiomatic: He halted the flood that threatened the altars and turned the people back from charred ruin.

sentences.zh: 扶傾頹構之下，拯溺逝川之中。

translations.literal: Under leaning pillars and collapsing framework, he saved the drowning in the flowing river.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath tottering beams and falling rafters, he pulled the drowning from the rushing stream.

sentences.zh: 九區重緝，四維更紐。

translations.literal: The nine regions re-gathered; the four bonds were re-threaded.
translations.idiomatic: The nine regions were knit together again; the four pillars of order were restored.

sentences.zh: 絕禮還紀，崩樂復張。

translations.literal: Broken rites returned to order; collapsed music was restored and spread.
translations.idiomatic: Rites that had broken were made whole again; music that had fallen silent sounded once more.

sentences.zh: 文館盈紳，戎亭息警。

translations.literal: Literary halls full of girdled officials; martial posts ceased alarms.
translations.idiomatic: Literary halls filled again with robed scholars; frontier posts fell quiet of alarm.

sentences.zh: 浹海宇以馳風，罄輪裳而稟朔。

translations.literal: Reaching sea and realm with running wind, exhausting wheel and robe in receiving the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: His influence ran like wind across land and sea; every cart and robe turned to acknowledge the new dawn.

sentences.zh: 八表呈祥，五靈效祉。

translations.literal: Eight directions show auspice; five spirits show blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The eight directions brought forth omens; the five spirits offered their blessing.

sentences.zh: 豈止鱗羽禎奇，雲星瑞色而已哉！

translations.literal: This is not merely scales and feathers showing marvels, cloud-stars and auspicious colors!
translations.idiomatic: These are not mere fish and birds bearing omens, or lucky clouds and stars in the sky!

sentences.zh: 勳茂於百王，道昭乎萬代，固以明配上天，光華日月者也。

translations.literal: Merit surpasses the hundred kings; the Way shines through ten thousand generations—truly he matches bright Heaven, his glory rivaling sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: His achievement outshines every king before him, his Way luminous for ages to come—he stands beside Heaven itself, bright as sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 河嶽表革命之符，圖讖紀代終之運。

translations.literal: Rivers and mountains bear the token of revolution; chart-prognostications record the mandate's end.
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and mountains proclaim the sign of dynastic change; prophecies mark the turning of the age.

sentences.zh: 樂推之心，幽顯共積；

translations.literal: The will to yield the throne willingly—dark and bright realms alike have gathered it;
translations.idiomatic: The people's wish to transfer power—seen and unseen worlds alike have stored it up;

sentences.zh: 歌頌之誠，華裔同著。

translations.literal: Sincerity of praise and song—Chinese and barbarian lands alike manifest it.
translations.idiomatic: The truth of their songs and hymns—Han and foreign lands alike proclaim it.

sentences.zh: 昔水政旣微，木德升緒，天之曆數，寔有所歸，握鏡琁樞，允集明哲。

translations.literal: When the Water reign waned and the Wood virtue rose, Heaven's cycle had its destination; holding the mirror and pivot, the wise truly gathered.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi's Water mandate faded and Liang's Wood virtue ascended, Heaven's count had found its home—and the wise gathered round the throne.

sentences.zh: 朕雖庸蔽，闇于大道，永鑒崇替，爲日已久，敢忘列代之高義，人祇之至願乎！

translations.literal: Though I am dull and blind to the Great Way, I have long contemplated rise and fall—how dare I forget the high righteousness of successive ages, humanity and spirits' utmost wish!
translations.idiomatic: Though I am obtuse and lost in the great Way, I have watched glory and ruin for many years—how could I forget what every age has honored, what gods and men most desire!

sentences.zh: 今便敬禪于梁，卽安姑孰，依唐虞、晉宋故事。

translations.literal: Now I respectfully yield the throne to Liang, taking my repose at Gufu, following the precedents of Tang-Yao, Yu-Shun, Jin and Song.
translations.idiomatic: Today I formally abdicate to Liang, retire to Gufu, and follow the precedent set by Yao and Shun, Jin and Song.

sentences.zh: 四月辛酉，宣德皇后令曰：「西詔至，帝憲章前代，敬禪神器于梁。

translations.literal: On day xinyou of the fourth month, the Virtuous Empress Dowager ordered: "The western edict has arrived. The Emperor, following earlier generations' pattern, respectfully yields the sacred regalia to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth month, day xinyou, the Virtuous Empress Dowager ordered: "The edict from the west has come. The Emperor, honoring the ways of former ages, yields the imperial regalia to Liang.

sentences.zh: 明可臨軒遣使，恭授璽紱，未亡人便歸於別宮。

translations.literal: Tomorrow at the imperial audience I shall dispatch envoys to bestow the seal and ribbon with ceremony; this widow shall withdraw to the detached palace."
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow I shall receive envoys at court and solemnly hand over the seal and sash; this widow will retire to the detached palace."

sentences.zh: 」壬戌，策曰：

translations.literal: On day renxu, the abdication proclamation read:
translations.idiomatic: On day renxu the investiture edict ran:

sentences.zh: 咨爾梁王：惟昔邃古之載，肇有生民，皇雄、大庭之辟，赫胥、尊盧之後，斯並龍圖鳥跡以前，慌忽杳冥之世，固無得而詳焉。

translations.literal: To thee, Prince of Liang: In remote antiquity, when life first arose, from the sovereigns Huangxiong and Dating to the heirs of Hexu and Zunlu—all prior to dragon charts and bird tracks, in dim ages beyond detail.
translations.idiomatic: To you, Prince of Liang: In deepest antiquity, when humankind first appeared—from Huangxiong and Dating to the heirs of Hexu and Zunlu—all before dragon charts and bird tracks, in misty ages no one can fully trace.

sentences.zh: 洎乎農、軒、炎、皞之代，放勳、重華之主，莫不以大道君萬姓，公器御八紘。

translations.literal: Down through the eras of Shennong, Xuanyuan, Yandi, and Shaohao, sovereigns like Yao and Shun—all governed the myriad people by the Great Way and wielded the common vessel to hold the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: Through the ages of Shennong, the Yellow Emperor, Yandi, and Shaohao—sovereigns like Yao and Shun—all ruled the people by the great Way and held the realm as a trust for all.

sentences.zh: 居之如執朽索，去之若捐重負。

translations.literal: They held power as one grips a rotting rope; they gave it up as one casts off a heavy burden.
translations.idiomatic: They clung to the throne like a man holding a fraying rope; they left it like a man dropping a crushing weight.

sentences.zh: 一駕汾陽，便有窅然之志；

translations.literal: One visit to Fenyang, and already the mind turned toward obscurity;
translations.idiomatic: A single journey to Fenyang, and the heart already turned toward retreat;

sentences.zh: 暫適箕嶺，卽動讓王之心。

translations.literal: A brief stay on Mount Ji, and the heart moved to yield the throne.
translations.idiomatic: A short sojourn on Mount Ji, and the will to abdicate awakened.

sentences.zh: 故知戴黃屋，服玉璽，非所以示貴稱尊；

translations.literal: Thus one knows that wearing the yellow canopy and holding the jade seal are not means to display rank and honor;
translations.idiomatic: So we know that the yellow canopy and jade seal are not worn to show off rank and glory;

sentences.zh: 乘大輅，建旂旌，蓋欲令歸趣有地。

translations.literal: Riding the great chariot and raising banners and flags—these were meant to give direction a place to return.
translations.idiomatic: The great chariot, the banners and pennants—these exist so that power may one day be returned.

sentences.zh: 是故忘己而字兆民，殉物而君四海。

translations.literal: Therefore they forgot themselves to nurture the myriad people, and devoted themselves to ruling all beneath Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: They forgot themselves for the sake of the people, and gave their lives to governing the world.

sentences.zh: 及于精華內竭，畚橇外勞，則撫茲歸運，惟能是與。

translations.literal: When inner essence was spent and outward toil with basket and spade exhausted them, then, welcoming this returning mandate, they gave it only to the capable.
translations.idiomatic: When their strength was spent within and their labor worn out without, they welcomed the turning of fate and yielded only to the worthy.

sentences.zh: 況兼乎笙管革文，威圖啓瑞，攝提夜朗，螢光晝發者哉！

translations.literal: How much more when reed pipes and drums proclaim new rule, auspicious charts open, Sheti shines clear at night, and fireflies blaze by day!
translations.idiomatic: How much more now, when music heralds a new age, auspicious signs appear, Sheti burns bright at night, and fireflies shine by day!

sentences.zh: 四百告終，有漢所以高揖；

translations.literal: Four hundred years ended, and Han therefore bowed high and yielded;
translations.idiomatic: When four hundred years ran out, Han bowed and yielded the throne;

sentences.zh: 黃德旣謝，魏氏所以樂推。

translations.literal: The Yellow virtue having faded, Wei thus gladly received the push of the people.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow virtue waned, Wei gladly accepted what the people thrust upon it.

sentences.zh: 爰及晉、宋，亦弘斯典。

translations.literal: Extending to Jin and Song, they too magnified this rite.
translations.idiomatic: Down through Jin and Song, each honored this same rite.

sentences.zh: 我太祖握《河》受曆，應符啓運，二葉重光，三聖系軌。

translations.literal: Our founding ancestor grasped the River Chart and received the calendar, matching the token and opening fortune—two reigns doubly bright, three sages linking the track.
translations.idiomatic: Our founding emperor took the River Chart and received Heaven's calendar, answered the omen and opened a new fortune—two reigns shone in succession, three sage rulers linked the line.

sentences.zh: 嗣君喪德，昏棄紀度，毀紊天綱，凋絕地紐。

translations.literal: The succeeding ruler lost virtue, blindly abandoned measure and law, destroyed and confused Heaven's net, withered earth's cords.
translations.idiomatic: The heir lost his virtue, cast off all order, tangled Heaven's laws and snapped the bonds of earth.

sentences.zh: 茫茫九域，剪爲仇讎，溥天相顧，命縣晷刻。

translations.literal: Across the boundless nine regions all were cut to mutual hatred; all under Heaven looked at one another, life hanging by a moment's thread.
translations.idiomatic: The nine regions became a wilderness of enemies; all under Heaven stared at one another, each life hanging by a thread.

sentences.zh: 斮涉刳孕，於事已輕；

translations.literal: Slicing the pregnant, wading through blood—even these weigh light beside what was done;
translations.idiomatic: Slaughtering the unborn, wading through gore—even these were trifles compared with what followed;

sentences.zh: 求雞徵杖，曾何足譬。

translations.literal: Seeking a chicken, demanding a staff—how could such petty cruelties even serve as comparison?
translations.idiomatic: Demanding a chicken, seizing a walking stick—how could such petty tyrannies even begin to compare?

sentences.zh: 是以谷滿川枯，山飛鬼哭，七廟已危，人神無主。

translations.literal: Thus valleys brimmed yet rivers dried, mountains flew and ghosts wept—the seven temples already endangered, neither men nor spirits had a lord.
translations.idiomatic: Valleys overflowed while rivers ran dry, mountains trembled and ghosts wailed—the ancestral temples stood in peril, and neither men nor gods had a master.

sentences.zh: 惟王體茲上哲，明聖在躬，稟靈五緯，明並日月。

translations.literal: Only Your Highness embodies this supreme wisdom, sagacity in person, receiving the spirit of the five planets, brilliance equal to sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: You alone embody supreme wisdom, sage virtue in your person, blessed by the five planets, bright as sun and moon together.

sentences.zh: 彝倫攸序，則端冕而協邕熙；

translations.literal: When human relations are ordered, you don the formal cap and robe and harmonize universal flourishing;
translations.idiomatic: In times of peace you don the ceremonial cap and robe and bring harmony to all;

sentences.zh: 時難孔棘，則推鋒而拯塗炭。

translations.literal: When hardship is most pressing, you thrust forward the blade and rescue men from fire and charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: In times of crisis you take up the sword and save the people from fire and ruin.

sentences.zh: 功逾造物，德濟蒼生，澤無不漸，仁無不被，上達蒼昊，下及川泉。

translations.literal: Merit surpasses creation's work, virtue aids the living masses—grace reaches none untainted, benevolence covers all, rising to azure Heaven, descending to rivers and springs.
translations.idiomatic: Your achievement exceeds what Heaven itself has wrought; your virtue succors all the living—no one goes untouched by your grace, no one left outside your mercy, from the sky above to the springs below.

sentences.zh: 文教與鵬翼齊舉，武功與日車並運。

translations.literal: Cultural teaching rises together with the roc's wings; martial achievement runs alongside the sun's chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Culture spreads on wings as broad as the roc's; martial glory rides beside the chariot of the sun.

sentences.zh: 固以幽顯宅心，謳訟斯屬；

translations.literal: Truly dark and bright realms have taken you to heart, and the songs of praise belong to you;
translations.idiomatic: The seen and unseen worlds have set their hearts on you; the songs of the people belong to you alone;

sentences.zh: 豈徒桴鼓播地，卿雲叢天而已哉！

translations.literal: Not merely drums sounding across the earth, auspicious clouds clustering in heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Not merely drums beating across the land and auspicious clouds filling the sky!

sentences.zh: 至如晝睹爭明，夜飛枉矢，土淪彗刺，日旣星亡，除舊之徵必顯，更姓之符允集。

translations.literal: As when by day one sees the sun and moon contend for light, by night wayward stars fly, earth sinks and comets pierce, sun eclipses and stars vanish—the signs of removing the old surely appear, the tokens of changing surname truly gather.
translations.idiomatic: When sun and moon vie for brightness by day, stray stars streak by night, earth collapses and comets pierce the sky, the sun darkens and stars fall—the omens of casting off the old are plain, the signs of dynastic change have gathered.

sentences.zh: 是以義師初踐，芳露凝甘，仁風旣被，素文自擾，北闕藁街之使，風車火徼之民，膜拜稽首，願爲臣妾。

translations.literal: Thus when the righteous army first stepped forth, sweet dew condensed; once humane wind spread, white patterns stirred of themselves—envoys from the northern gates and straw-market frontier, chariot-wind and fire-sign peoples, bowed and prostrated, wishing to become servants.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army first marched, sweet dew gathered; when benevolent winds blew, white banners rose of their own accord—envoys from the northern capital, peoples from the farthest frontiers, all bowed and prostrated themselves, begging to become your subjects.

sentences.zh: 鐘石畢變，事表于遷虞；

translations.literal: Bells and stones all changed—events signaled the transfer from Yu;
translations.idiomatic: Bells and stone chimes all changed—the omen of Yu's abdication appeared;

sentences.zh: 蛟魚並出，義彰于事夏。

translations.literal: Dragons and fish appeared together—the righteousness shown in serving Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Dragons and fish rose together—the righteousness of serving Xia was made manifest.

sentences.zh: 若夫長民御衆，爲之司牧，本同己於萬物，乃因心於百姓。

translations.literal: As for governing the people and leading the multitude, acting as shepherd—the root is to make oneself one with the myriad things, to follow the heart of the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: To govern the people and lead the masses as their shepherd—the root of it is to become one with all creation, to follow the hearts of the common people.

sentences.zh: 寶命無常主，帝王非一族。

translations.literal: The precious mandate has no fixed lord; emperors are not of one clan alone.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate has no permanent master; the throne does not belong to one family forever.

sentences.zh: 今仰祗乾象，俯藉人願，敬禪神器，授帝位于爾躬。

translations.literal: Now, reverencing Heaven's signs above and relying on the people's wish below, I respectfully yield the sacred regalia and confer the imperial position upon your person.
translations.idiomatic: Now, looking up to Heaven's signs and down to the people's will, I yield the imperial regalia and confer the throne upon you.

sentences.zh: 大祚告窮，天祿永終。

translations.literal: The great fortune declares its end; Heaven's stipend is forever concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Our great fortune is spent; Heaven's blessing upon us is ended.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 王允執其中，式遵前典，以副昊天之望。

translations.literal: Prince, hold the center between extremes, follow the former canon, to answer bright Heaven's expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Prince, hold the middle way, follow the ancient precedent, and fulfill what bright Heaven expects.

sentences.zh: 禋上帝而臨億兆，格文祖而膺大業，以傳無疆之祚，豈不盛歟！

translations.literal: Sacrifice to High God and face the hundred millions, approach the civil ancestors and receive the great enterprise—to transmit boundless fortune: is this not magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Worship Heaven and rule the hundred million people, receive the ancestors' blessing and take up the great enterprise—to pass on an endless fortune: what glory could be greater!

sentences.zh: 又璽書曰：

translations.literal: Another imperial letter read:
translations.idiomatic: Another letter bearing the imperial seal read:

sentences.zh: 夫生者天地之大德，人者含生之通稱，並首同本，未知所以異也。

translations.literal: Life is Heaven and Earth's greatest virtue; humans are the general name of the living—same head, same origin, none know why they should differ.
translations.idiomatic: Life is the greatest virtue of Heaven and Earth; humanity is the common name of all who live—we share the same form, the same root; who knows why we should be divided?

sentences.zh: 而稟靈造化，賢愚之情不一；

translations.literal: Yet receiving spirit from creation, wise and foolish natures are not one;
translations.idiomatic: Yet endowed by creation, the wise and the foolish are not alike;

sentences.zh: 託性五常，強柔之分或舛。

translations.literal: Resting in the five constants, strong and soft divisions may go awry.
translations.idiomatic: Rooted in the five virtues, the strong and the weak may fall out of balance.

sentences.zh: 羣后靡一，爭犯交興，是故建君立長，用相司牧。

translations.literal: Lords were not one, contention and offense arose together—therefore they established rulers and elders to assist in governing.
translations.idiomatic: When rulers were many and strife arose, they set up kings and chiefs to govern on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 非謂尊驕在上，以天下爲私者也。

translations.literal: Not meaning to be proud above and take all under Heaven as private property.
translations.idiomatic: Not so that the proud might stand above and treat the realm as their private possession.

sentences.zh: 兼以三正迭改，五運相遷，綠文赤字，徵《河》表《洛》。

translations.literal: Moreover the three calendars changed in turn, five agents shifted; green script and red characters testified, the River Chart and Luo Writ exemplified.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the three calendars succeeded one another, the five phases turned in cycle—green writing and red characters bore witness, the River Chart and Luo Writ gave proof.

sentences.zh: 在昔勛、華，深達茲義，眷求明哲，授以蒸民。

translations.literal: In ancient times Yao and Shun deeply grasped this meaning, sought the wise, and entrusted the masses.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times Yao and Shun understood this deeply, sought out the wise, and entrusted the people to them.

sentences.zh: 遷虞事夏，本因心於百姓；

translations.literal: Transferring from Yu, serving Xia—the root was following the heart of the people;
translations.idiomatic: Yu yielded to Shun, Shun served the Xia—the root of it was following the people's hearts;

sentences.zh: 化殷爲周，實受命於蒼昊。

translations.literal: Transforming Yin to Zhou—truly receiving mandate from azure Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou replaced the Shang—truly receiving mandate from Heaven above.

sentences.zh: 爰自漢、魏，罔不率由；

translations.literal: From Han and Wei on, none failed to follow this path;
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei onward, none failed to follow this way;

sentences.zh: 降及晉、宋，亦遵斯典。

translations.literal: Descending to Jin and Song, they too observed this canon.
translations.idiomatic: Down through Jin and Song, each honored this same tradition.

sentences.zh: 我高皇所以格文祖而撫歸運，畏上天而恭寶曆者也。

translations.literal: Our High Emperor therefore approached the civil ancestors and embraced the returning mandate, revering Heaven and respectfully receiving the precious calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Our High Emperor therefore received the ancestors' blessing and embraced the turning of fate, revering Heaven and respectfully taking up the imperial calendar.

sentences.zh: 至于季世，禍亂荐臻，王度紛糾，姦回熾積。

translations.literal: When the final generation came, calamity and chaos piled up, royal measure tangled, treacherous wickedness accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: In the last days calamity piled upon calamity, royal order collapsed, and wickedness flourished unchecked.

sentences.zh: 億兆夷人，刀俎爲命，已然之逼，若線之危，跼天蹐地，逃形無所。

translations.literal: Millions of common people—knife and chopping block for their fate; already-nearer oppression, peril thin as thread; crawling between heaven and earth, nowhere to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Millions of ordinary people faced the knife and the block; danger pressed close as a thread; they crawled between heaven and earth with nowhere to hide.

sentences.zh: 羣凶挾煽，志逞殘戮，將欲先殄衣冠，次移龜鼎。

translations.literal: Fierce evils fanned the flames, intent on indulging slaughter—they meant first to destroy the gentry, then move the sacred vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The wicked fanned the flames of chaos, hungry for slaughter—they meant first to wipe out the educated classes, then seize the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 衡、保、周、召，並列宵人。

translations.literal: Heng, Bao, Zhou, and Shao stood ranked with night people.
translations.idiomatic: Men who should have been like Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou stood instead among villains of the night.

sentences.zh: 巢幕累卵，方此非切。

translations.literal: Nest on awning, piled eggs—even these pale before the present danger.
translations.idiomatic: A nest in a burning rafter, eggs stacked on a collapsing wall—even these do not capture the peril we faced.

sentences.zh: 自非英聖遠圖，仁爲己任，則鴟梟厲吻，剪焉已及。

translations.literal: Had it not been for heroic sage far-seeing, taking benevolence as personal charge—owls and falcons would already have snapped shut and cut one down.
translations.idiomatic: Had you not been a heroic sage of far vision, taking benevolence as your own burden—the owls would already have closed their beaks upon us all.

sentences.zh: 惟王崇高則天，博厚儀地，鎔鑄六合，陶甄萬有。

translations.literal: Only Your Highness is lofty as Heaven, broad and thick as Earth, smelting the six directions, molding the myriad beings.
translations.idiomatic: You alone are lofty as Heaven, vast as Earth, forging the six directions, shaping the ten thousand things.

sentences.zh: 鋒馹交馳，振靈武以遐略；

translations.literal: Blazing spears and swift couriers raced together, stirring martial spirit for distant campaigns;
translations.idiomatic: Spears flashed and couriers raced, rousing martial valor for campaigns far and wide;

sentences.zh: 雲雷方扇，鞠義旅以勤王。

translations.literal: Thunder clouds just spreading, mustering righteous troops to aid the king.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder clouds gathering, you raised righteous armies to rescue the throne.

sentences.zh: 揚旍旆於遠路，戮姦宄於魏闕。

translations.literal: Raising banners and flags on distant roads, executing traitors at the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: You raised your banners on distant roads and executed traitors at the capital gates.

sentences.zh: 德冠往初，功無與二。

translations.literal: Virtue crowns all former beginnings; achievement matches no second.
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue surpasses all who came before; your achievement has no equal.

sentences.zh: 弘濟艱難，緝熙王道。

translations.literal: Greatly crossing hardship, brightening the kingly Way.
translations.idiomatic: You crossed through hardship and restored the brightness of the kingly Way.

sentences.zh: 懷柔萬姓，經營四方。

translations.literal: Embracing and soothing the myriad surnames, managing the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: You embraced and comforted the people, and set the four directions in order.

sentences.zh: 舉直措枉，較如畫一。

translations.literal: Raising the straight and setting aside the crooked—measured as if drawn with one line.
translations.idiomatic: You promoted the upright and removed the corrupt—as uniform as a line drawn with one stroke.

sentences.zh: 待旦同乎殷后，日昃過於周文。

translations.literal: Staying awake till dawn like the Shang queen; laboring past noon exceeding King Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: You waited for dawn like a worthy Shang ruler; you toiled past noon surpassing King Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 風化肅穆，禮樂交暢。

translations.literal: Wind of transformation solemn and reverent; rites and music interflowing smoothly.
translations.idiomatic: Customs grew solemn and pure; rites and music flourished together.

sentences.zh: 加以赦過宥罪，神武不殺，盛德昭於景緯，至義感於鬼神。

translations.literal: Adding forgiveness of faults and pardoning crimes, divine martiality without killing—grand virtue shines in the stellar girdle, supreme righteousness moves ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: You pardoned the guilty and forgave offenses, wielded divine power without needless killing—your great virtue shines among the stars, your supreme righteousness moves ghosts and spirits.

sentences.zh: 若夫納彼大麓，膺此歸運，烈風不迷，樂推攸在。

translations.literal: As for receiving that great foothill, accepting this returning mandate—fierce wind did not confuse, the willing push of people was there.
translations.idiomatic: In receiving the great mandate at Mount Tai, accepting this turning of fate—the fierce wind did not lead you astray, and the people's will to yield was plain.

sentences.zh: 治五韙於已亂，重九鼎於旣輕。

translations.literal: Ordering the five musical instruments in already-disordered times, restoring the nine cauldrons that had grown light.
translations.idiomatic: You set right the five rites in a broken age, and restored the nine cauldrons that had lost their weight.

sentences.zh: 自聲教所及，車書所至，革面回首，謳吟德澤。

translations.literal: From where culture's voice reached, where chariots and writing arrived—faces changed, heads turned back, singing praise of virtue's grace.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever your civilizing voice reached, wherever your chariots and writing arrived—people turned their faces and sang of your grace.

sentences.zh: 九山滅祲，四瀆安流。

translations.literal: Nine mountains' evil vapors extinguished, four great rivers flowing peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: Evil mists vanished from the nine mountains; the four great rivers flowed in peace.

sentences.zh: 祥風扇起，淫雨靜息。

translations.literal: Auspicious winds fan and rise, excessive rains quiet and cease.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious winds rose; floods and storms subsided.

sentences.zh: 玄甲游於芳荃，素文馴於郊苑。

translations.literal: Dark armor roams amid fragrant herbs; white patterns are gentle in suburban parks.
translations.idiomatic: Armored soldiers walk peacefully among fragrant meadows; white banners flutter calmly in the royal parks.

sentences.zh: 躍九川於清漢，鳴六象於高崗。

translations.literal: Leaping through nine rivers in clear skies; six symbolic beasts call from high knolls.
translations.idiomatic: Fish leap in the clear rivers; the six auspicious beasts call from the high hills.

sentences.zh: 靈瑞雜杳，玄符昭著。

translations.literal: Spirit omens mixed and manifold, dark tokens clearly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Spiritual omens appeared in profusion; Heaven's signs shone clear.

sentences.zh: 至於星孛紫宮，水效孟月，飛鴻滿野，長彗橫天，取新之應旣昭，革故之徵必顯。

translations.literal: As when comets bristle in the Purple Palace, water-signs appear in the first month, wild geese fill the fields, long comets span heaven—the response of taking the new already bright, the sign of replacing the old surely manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Comets blazed in the Purple Palace, water omens appeared in the first month, wild geese filled the fields, long comets crossed the sky—the signs of a new beginning were plain, the omens of dynastic change unmistakable.

sentences.zh: 加以天表秀特，軒狀堯姿；

translations.literal: Adding heavenly countenance uniquely fine, lofty bearing like Yao's form;
translations.idiomatic: Your heavenly bearing is uniquely noble, your stature like that of Emperor Yao;

sentences.zh: 君臨之符，諒非一揆。

translations.literal: Tokens of ruling—surely not of one measure alone.
translations.idiomatic: The signs that you are meant to rule—surely they are not of one kind alone.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：「天鑒厥德，用集大命。

translations.literal: The Documents says: "Heaven observes his virtue and gathers the great mandate to him."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Heaven sees his virtue and brings the great mandate to him."

sentences.zh: 」《詩》云：「文王在上，於昭于天。

translations.literal: The Odes say: "King Wen above—how bright he is before Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says: "King Wen above—how bright he shines before Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」所以二儀乃眷，幽明允葉，豈惟宅是萬邦，緝茲謳訟而已哉！

translations.literal: Therefore Yin and Yang both favor, dark and bright truly harmonize—not merely to possess this myriad realm and gather these songs of praise!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth both look upon you with favor, the seen and unseen worlds agree—not merely to win this realm and gather the people's songs!

sentences.zh: 朕是用擁琁沉首，屬懷聖哲。

translations.literal: Therefore I bow the head upon the precious jade and entrust my heart to the sage and wise.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I bow my head upon the jade scepter and place my trust in your sage wisdom.

sentences.zh: 昔水行告厭，我太祖旣受命代終；

translations.literal: Formerly the Water reign declared its satiety; our founding ancestor already received mandate to succeed the ending;
translations.idiomatic: When the Water mandate ran its course, our founding emperor received Heaven's charge to succeed the dying dynasty;

sentences.zh: 在日天祿云謝，亦以木德而傳于梁。

translations.literal: On this day Heaven's stipend declares its departure, and by Wood virtue passes to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Today Heaven's blessing upon us is ended, and by Wood virtue the mandate passes to Liang.

sentences.zh: 遠尋前典，降惟近代，百辟遐邇，莫違朕心。

translations.literal: Searching far the former canon, lowering regard to recent ages—lords near and far, none contradict my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back to ancient precedent and down to recent times—ministers near and far, none oppose what my heart commands.

sentences.zh: 今遣使持節、兼太保、侍中、中書監、兼尚書令汝南縣開國侯亮，兼太尉、散騎常侍、中書令新吳縣開國侯志，奉皇帝璽紱。

translations.literal: Now I dispatch the Commissioner with Staff, concurrent Grand Mentor, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Master of Affairs, Marquis of Ruinan, Liang; and concurrent Grand Commandant, Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Director of the Secretariat, Marquis of Xinwu, Zhi—to present the imperial seal and ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Now I send Commissioner with Staff, concurrent Grand Tutor, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Master of Affairs, Marquis of Ruinan Liang, and concurrent Grand Commandant, Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, Marquis of Xinwu Zhi, to deliver the imperial seal and sash.

sentences.zh: 受終之禮，一依唐虞故事。

translations.literal: The rite of receiving the end shall wholly follow the Tang-Yu precedents.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremony of succession shall follow entirely the precedent of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 王其陟茲元后，君臨萬方，式傳洪烈，以答上天之休命！

translations.literal: Prince, ascend as this primal sovereign, rule the ten thousand regions, transmit the grand achievement—to answer Heaven's gracious mandate!
translations.idiomatic: Prince, ascend the throne, rule the ten thousand regions, pass on your great achievement—and answer Heaven's gracious command!

sentences.zh: 高祖抗表陳讓，表不獲通。

translations.literal: Gaozu submitted memorials refusing, protestations that were not forwarded.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu submitted memorials declining the throne, but they were not delivered onward.

sentences.zh: 於是，齊百官豫章王元琳等八百一十九人，及梁臺侍中臣雲等一百一十七人，並上表勸進，高祖謙讓不受。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qi hundred officials—Prince of Yuzhang Yuanlin and eight hundred nineteen others—and Liang Platform Attendant-in-Ordinary Minister Yun and one hundred seventeen others all submitted memorials urging accession; Gaozu modestly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon eight hundred nineteen Qi officials, led by Prince Yuanlin of Yuzhang, and one hundred seventeen Liang Platform officials, led by Attendant-in-Ordinary Fan Yun, all submitted memorials urging accession; Gaozu modestly declined.

sentences.zh: 是日，太史令蔣道秀陳天文符讖六十四條，事並明著。

translations.literal: That day, Imperial Astronomer Jiang Daoxiu presented sixty-four items of astronomical omens and portents; the matters were all clearly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: That day Imperial Astronomer Jiang Daoxiu presented sixty-four astronomical omens and portents, each clearly established.

sentences.zh: 羣臣重表固請，乃從之。

translations.literal: The ministers again submitted memorials firmly requesting; then he assented.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers again memorialized, firmly urging him, he at last consented.
